articles.title: Troubleshooting Zendesk–ClickUp Integration via Zapier
articles.content:
Overview This guide helps troubleshoot issues with the Zendesk–ClickUp integration, which relies on Zapier automations.  If the integration stops working (for example, Click Up status not syncing to Zendesk), follow the steps below to identify and resolve the issue. Common Causes for Integration Failures 
Authentication or permission changes – such as revoked tokens or admin updates.
API rate limits or temporary outages – on ClickUp, Zendesk, or Zapier.
Changes to integration settings – including updated fields or app connections.
Service disruptions – on any of the connected platforms.
 Recommended Actions Check connection status 
Ensure ClickUp, Zendesk, and Zapier app connections are authenticated and active.
Reconnect any accounts showing errors or expired tokens. 
Review recent changes Check if there have been any updates to admin permissions, API tokens, or integration settings, as these can interrupt authentication or break Zaps. Check for reported outages Visit the ClickUp Status Page and Zapier Status Page to see if downtime was reported during the issue window. Re-authenticate or retry Zaps if required Sometimes temporary disruptions require a simple reconnection or Zap refresh. If unresolved, escalate to ClickUp Provide the details listed in the section below to help expedite investigation. Information Required for EscalationIf the issue persists and you need to contact ClickUp support, please include: 
A clear description of the issue.
Zapier Task ID(s) and error messages (see how to find these below).
Approximate time range the issue occurred.
Confirmation that authentication and permissions were checked.
 How to Find Zapier Task IDs and Error LogsFinding Zapier Task IDs: 
Log in to Zapier.
Go to Zap History: https://zapier.com/app/history.
Click on any Zap run to view its details.
The Task ID (or Zap Run ID) is shown in the details or in the URL.
Copy this ID and include it in your support request. 
Accessing Zapier Error Logs: 
From Zap History, look for Zap runs marked as Failed (usually highlighted in red).
Click on the failed run to view detailed error messages, including which step failed and the specific error.
Copy or screenshot the error details for reference.
 Checking ClickUp Integration Logs Admins can also view audit or integration logs (if enabled) for further details. Helpful Resources 
Zendesk Integration Documentation
Zapier Integration Help
ClickUp API & Integrations

Transcript (AI Generated):
Before you can set up Atlas integration with Titan, you need to get a good understanding of how the basics of Titan work. It is normally a good idea to have used Titan for about six weeks or so before you get started. When you're ready to set up Titan integration with Atlas, have a chat with the Atlas help desk and they'll get the compatible version of Kappa installed and show you how it works. Once signed off as fully trained on the new version, it's time to set Titan up. The first thing that you need to do is to install the Atlas app from the marketplace. This is done in the normal way. Just click on the app. Click the pricing button. Confirm the EULA and click accept. Now that the app has been added, we need to create a tag. Just go to the settings screen. And go into the patient tag manager. Create a new workflow tag. And give it the name of the care home. Then just turn on the Atlas integration toggle and click confirm. The next thing to do is to assign that tag to a patient. To do this, we can just go into the search bar and search for a patient as normal. A good option is to actually search by postcode, as all of your care home patients will share the same postcode. This will return results in the list, making it easier for you to apply one tag at a time to each patient. Click on the patient name. Click add tag and select the tag that you just created. And continue to add tags for all of the rest of the patients. Now that the tag has been added, you can just dispense as normal, and the messages will be sent to CAPA and subsequently to Atlas at the point of handout.

Transcript (AI Generated):
Titan PMR have teamed up with BD Rowa to bring you the most advanced dispensing system yet. Using the BD Rowa integration, picking and managing stock becomes quick, easy, and efficient from the labeling screen. Just hit the request stock button, and Titan will trigger the BD Rowa robot to pick all the required items and send them straight to you ready for labelling. Then just label and handout as normal. You can also request stock independently of any prescriptions from the F2 BD Rowa flyout. We have also included a pre-pack function allowing you to label your split packs with the Titan and BD Rowa recognised QR code for maximum efficiency and waste reduction. Just scan the product into the stock management screen on the assembled packs tab. Enter the new pack size, the batch number, and the expiry date. And then enter how many labels you want to produce. Finally, click create. You can then stick the new labels onto the packs before feeding them into the robot. Just be sure to get the items checked by a pharmacist before you add them to the robot. Simply scan the label into the same screen and click approve. Another feature that comes with the BD Rowa integration is stock management. Titan is now able to display the exact stock level of each item that's inside the robot, making sure you never run out of stock.

articles.title: Batch Owing
articles.content:
Once you have labelled all the picked items from your batch, it's easy to set all the remaining items to Owing in one go. 
Just hit the Batch Owing button from the labelling screen and all items will be set to owing.

 Tips: 
It is not possible to remove all owings in one click. This will need to be done one at a time in the normal way (just scan the item you want to dispense and the owing will be dispensed. If the package doesn't scan, find the owing, click it, hit the dustbin icon, then dispense manually as normal.

articles.title: Dispensing Process
articles.content:
Create a batch

Go to the prescriptions board.
Click the Bulk toggle at the top of the picking list.
Tick the prescriptions that you want to add to the batch.
Select “Create Batch Flow”.
Enter a name for your batch (this will appear on the Prescription Board card and the picking list).
Choose how you want to print/display the Picking List.
Click Confirm

Your tray labels will now be printed, together with your picking lists or TITAN Mobile label:
    
Label the baskets

On your bench, set up one basket for each patient.
Label each basket with the labels that have been printed

 
 
Pick the stock in bulk
Picking list on TITAN Mobile 
Login to TITAN Mobile and scan the Batch Flow TITAN Mobile Picking Label from the patients screen (you can also scan the normal picking label or sheet)
Start picking each item from the displayed list into a large container such as a delivery tote. Optionally, you can also barcode verify the product at this point using the auto scan feature to ensure that you have selected the correct item.

 
 
Picking List on labels or A4
Pick each item from the printed list into a large container such as a delivery tote.

    
Start labelling and distribute into the correct baskets
Pick any item at random from the tote and scan it. A dispensing label will be printed if you have scanned the right item as normal for you to stick onto the box.  Check on screen or on the dispensing label to see which basket to put the packet into. Put the packet into the corresponding basket. Repeat this process until you have labelled all picked items. Once you have labeled all items, click Batch Owing to send any remaining items for the batch to Owing.

 

 
Accuracy Checking and Packaging
TITAN Quick Packaging is not an available feature with Batch Flow. All items must be scanned into the bag from the packaging screen. As normal, dispensers without the “Can package needs check items” permission on their role will not have access to the packaging screen if there is a check due.
If you prefer to have the checks done on TITAN, just put the basket to one side as normal. The ACT/Pharmacist will then be able to scan the basket label to access the labelling screen where they can either Quick Check the items and give them back to the dispenser to package, or they can scan each item into the package, checking as they go.
A great way to do your accuracy checks is with TITAN Mobile Quick Check. Checking a batch flow item on TITAN Mobile will automatically change the status from Needs Check (red) to Clean (green) without you having to refresh the labelling page (TITAN Mobile menu>Quick Check>scan the picking label>Accept Checks).

 
Assign to shelf and Handout 
The assign to shelf and hand out processes are no different to normal in Batch Flow

articles.title: Video
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Hello everybody. Today's video is about huge innovation in pharmacy, brought to you by Titan Batch Flow. With batch flow, you are able to dispense multiple patient's medications all in one go. To begin, just install the batch flow app as normal. Set your picking item, order to drug name, and choose how you want to print the picking lists. If you use Titan Mobile, it's a good idea to choose Titan Mobile Here. You can also opt to send the list to an A four page or to your label printer. And finally, we just need to set up the print profiles. Pop over to the settings page and go into the profile tab. From here, you can set the picking reports to the relevant print profile. We recommend that you use the same print profiles that you would normally use for your dispensing labels and your backing cards or mar charts. And that's it. That's the setup done. Now let's have a look at the dispensing process. The first thing we need to do is to create a new batch from the prescription board. Toggle the bulk button at the top of the picking column. Next, select the cards that you want to add to the batch and click create batch flow. Note that the select all button will respect the filters. So if you wanted to filter to show all the patients of a particular care home, for example, you can do that and then select all and dispense 'em all as a single batch. Give the batch a name if you want. You can change the stationary use to print the picking list. For our purposes, we'll use Titan Mobile. When you click confirm, your basket labels will be printed along with your picking lists or the Titan Mobile label. Begin by setting out one basket for each patient and then label each basket. Next, grab yourself a delivery tote or something similar and start picking. Either pick from the list or if you're using Titan Mobile. Log in and scan the barcode on the label into the patient screen. As you pick, there's an option to scan the item to check that it's the correct one, and that will also remove the item from the list as you go. You can pick the items in any order and type or sort them out for you later. Once you picked all the items, it's time to start labeling. Choose from single or multi patient mode. In multi patient mode, you'll be able to label any item for any patient in your batch in any order. Single patient mode will ensure that you only label the item for the patient on the screen before manually moving onto the next patient. For the purposes of this video, we'll use the multi patient mode. Select any item from your tote at random and scan it in as normal. Basket Three and dispensing label will be produced. If the item is required, you'll see which basket to put them into and Titan will tell you verbally. Basket one Titan will also switch to the correct patient's labeling screen with the basket number highlighted at the top of the screen. Stick the label on the box and place the product into the corresponding basket. Continue dispensing until you scanned all the items in your tote basket. One. Once you've finished, scanning everything in your tote, hit the batch owing button to send any missing items to owing. It's now time to package the items. If the basket is clean, meaning there are no checks due, you can tell this because the basket number will have a tick against it and will normally be green in S any owings. Just scan the corresponding baskets to access the packaging screen where you can package the items as normal. If there are any checks due as indicated by the warning triangle and normally the color red, you can put these baskets to one side to be checked later as per the normal process. Or you could of course get someone to check them on Titan Mobile. While you wait To do this, log into Titan Mobile and from the main menu, select quick check, then scan the basket label and accept the checks. The label status will immediately be updated and you'll be able to carry on packaging as normal. And that's it. You are all set.

Set up - Pre-pack split label Printer Profile

Split packs will have a label with a barcode that can be scanned back into the robot
Click on settings cog on left hand menu on Titan.
Navigate to Print profiles Tab.
Scroll to Report “PrePack Label” •      Choose correct Profile name from the dropdown.
Save your changes.

Set up - Pre-pack split label Printer Profile

Robots usually have many chutes
You can set which computer is connected to which chute
You can set the priority for picking per chute
Click on setting cog icon in Titan.
Navigate to Dispensing Settings Tab.
In robot setting section sent Chute Number and Pick Priority

Use - Picking and labelling

All processes are the same leading up to labelling—so get picking label and pick non-robot stock​
​Scan the picking label barcode—Titan loads up patient labelling screen​
Labelling the screen displays stock availability on the left-hand side.​
At this point, users can specify the manufacturing details of the item or choose "Any manufacturer.“​
Upon pressing "Request stock," a message is sent to the robot, prompting the deployment of items to the desired Chute.​
Other non-robot stock is now picked​
Proceed with the standard labelling process.​

Use - Labelling and creating a split pack

Scan the product barcode on the labelling screen as normal.​
​If Titan detects that a portion of the quantity needs dispensing, it alerts the user to split the pack. At this point, the user can input the Expiry date and batch number. If an FMD barcode was scanned during the labelling process, this information auto-populates.​
Upon completion, Titan prints a dispensing label, followed by a Split-pack label containing a QR code.​
Users load the split pack into the robot, and upon scanning the QR code on the Split-pack label, all relevant information is transmitted to the robot.

Use – Ad Hoc stock picking from Robot
User can request stock without Rx using Manual stock picking. ​

Press function button F2 which will open a robot pick flyout.​
Start Typing name of the drug and system will preset your available options.​
Choose item to pick and enter required quantity.​
Hit enter.​
Request the stock by pressing “Pick Items”

articles.title: Set Up
articles.content:
This guide walks you through installing the driver, setting up the paper size, and configuring print profiles in Titan for the Brother TD-4420DN label printer.
 
Install the Driver
 

Download and run the Brother TD-4420DN driver.

When prompted:

Model: TD-4420DN

Connection Type: Local Connection (USB)

Follow the installation wizard and click Finish.

The driver is now installed.

 
Configure Paper Size in Windows
 

On your PC, go to: Settings → Printers & Scanners → Brother TD-4420DN → Manage → Printer Properties → Preferences

Select Paper Size Setup → New.

Create a new paper size with the following details and name it Titan:

Width: 77 mm

Length: 39 mm

Label Spacing: 3.8 mm

Margins: Left 1.5 mm | Right 1.5 mm | Top 3.0 mm | Bottom 3.0 mm

Media Sensor: Transmissive/Gap

Detection Sensitivity: 1

Select Add, then Exit.

 
Apply the Titan Paper Size
 

Go back to: Settings → Printers & Scanners → Brother TD-4420DN → Manage → Printer Properties → Preferences

Under Paper Size, select Titan from the dropdown.

Click Apply.

 
Set Up Titan Print Profile
 

Log in to Titan.

Navigate to: Settings → Print Profiles → Create New

Enter the following:

Profile Name: Label – Brother

Printer: Brother TD-4420DN

Margins:

Page Width: 75 or 77

Page Height: 30 or 39 (adjust if needed)

Top: 2 | Bottom: 4 | Left: 0 | Right: 0

Assign Dispensing Labelling to the correct printer.

Click Save Changes.

 
Test the Setup
 

Go back into Print Profiles.

Print a test dispensing label to confirm correct setup.

articles.title: 24/24: Original Pack Dispensing FAQs
articles.content:
CPE Briefing: 24/24: Original Pack Dispensing FAQs
Introduction

1.       What is Original Pack Dispensing +/- 10%?Following a public consultation, the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 (HMRs) were amended in October 2023 to allow Original Pack Dispensing (OPD). OPD allows pharmacists the flexibility to dispense up to 10% more or less than the prescribed quantity if this means that the product can be supplied to the patient in the manufacturer’s original pack (except when dispensing products outside of scope or where this would negatively affect the patient’s clinical treatment regimen).
 

2.       Why were these changes introduced?

 
OPD +/-10% is one of a number of legislative changes intended to transform the supply and delivery of medicines that were envisaged in the 2019, 5-year deal agreed between Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and NHS England (NHSE). The new OPD flexibilities, where they may apply, aim to support increased patient safety by improving patient access to safety information that is included in a medicine’s original packaging. DHSC’s OPD consultation document also states that “by allowing community pharmacies to dispense medicines in their original packs, we believe OPD will help them to become more efficient and to free up their time for other tasks such as providing clinical services to patients” by allowing community pharmacies to dispense medicines in their original packs, we believe OPD will help them to become more efficient and to free up their time for other tasks such as providing clinical services to patients”.
 

3.       When do the OPD +/-10% flexibilities apply to dispensing?

 
For NHS prescriptions: the changes will come into force on 1 January 2025 as laid out in the Terms of Service (in the NHS (Pharmaceutical and Local Pharmaceutical Services) Regulations 2013 (PLPS).
 
For private prescriptions: the OPD regulations came in force in Great Britain as soon as the Human Medicines Amendment Regulations came into force on 11 October 2023.
 

4.       When does OPD +/-10% apply to NHS dispensing in England?

 
When the HMRs were amended in October 2023, there was a transitional provision for OPD +/- 10%, so that the flexibility to dispense 10% more or less than the prescribed quantity did not automatically apply in NHS pharmaceutical services in England. This was to allow DHSC and Community Pharmacy England to find a solution for how OPD +/-10% would apply to NHS dispensing in England.
 
Subject to the availability of supporting PMR systems functionality, from 1 January 2025, pharmacies will have the discretion to apply OPD +/-10% rules to NHS prescriptions. Changes to the PLPS will for NHS dispensing:
 

require the supervising pharmacist to consider OPD +/-10% dispensing for NHS prescriptions, as appropriate, and
give the pharmacist the flexibility to supply up to 10% more or less than the prescribed quantity, if that would mean the medicine could be dispensed in the manufacturer’s original pack, and other prescription requirements are fulfilled.

There will be a requirement for pharmacists to exercise their professional skill and judgement and consider whether it is safe and appropriate to use these flexibilities to supply a different quantity to that ordered on a prescription, having regard to the benefits to patients, IT system readiness, whenever it may be possible to make such supplies etc.
DHSC acknowledges that IT system suppliers may not all be ready to implement OPD functionality into their systems from 1st January 2025. System suppliers had requested at least six months for IT development but were provided the information to support the changes within much shorter timelines.
 

5.       Am I required to use OPD +/- 10% rules for NHS dispensing?

 
The PLPS amendments are enabling to allow the supervising pharmacist to consider using the OPD +/- 10% flexibility for NHS dispensing from 1 January 2025, but there is NO requirement to use it.
 
Pharmacy owners must consider OPD from 1st January, but the DHSC and Community Pharmacy England say that it is reasonable for pharmacists to opt out of using the OPD provisions until the IT  systems  have  been  fully  developed  to  tested  to  support  OPD  functionality.
 

6.       Under what circumstances can I choose not to use OPD +/- 10% rules?

 
Except where a product falls outside the scope of OPD +/-10% rules, professional judgment should be exercised to assess the suitability of applying +/- 10% quantity flexibility for dispensing as it may not be appropriate to use it in all cases.
 
Examples of circumstances where pharmacists may continue to dispense the prescribed quantity even if it requires splitting a pack includes:
 

if the supervising pharmacist considers that the patient should be supplied with the exact quantity prescribed to be able to follow the medication regimen or to support patient safety. For example, antibiotics where it is clinically important for a patient to complete the full course of medicine as prescribed, or for certain pain relief medicines where there is a risk of reliance or addiction.

 

If the pharmacy cannot obtain the whole pack with reasonable promptness or there is a patient need reason e.g. delay to patient treatment.
Where the patient refuses to accept a lesser quantity than the quantity prescribed, e.g. where a patient is required to pay a prescription charge.

IT system suppliers may not introduce the necessary changes to the pharmacy IT system to support OPD until after 1 January 2025.

7.       Some patients are prescribed daily or weekly prescriptions, can OPD +/-10% rules be applied to those prescriptions?

 
Pharmacists should exercise their professional judgment to assess the suitability of applying the OPD +/-10% rules as it may not be appropriate to supply more or less than the prescribed quantity. The supervising pharmacist must consider the patient safety and suitability when applying the OPD +/- 10% rules to eligible products.
 

8.       Are all products in scope of OPD +/-10% rules?

 
All POMs, non-POMs (P medicines, GSL medicines, non-medicines) and Schedule 5 Controlled Drugs (CDs) are within scope of OPD +/-10% rules for supply against NHS prescriptions.
However, there are a number of products excluded from the OPD +/-10% rules for NHS dispensing. For example, all Schedules 1-4 CDs, Part IX appliances, unlicensed specials and products classed as special containers fall outside the scope of OPD +/-10% rules.
See the table below for an overview of products included and excluded under the OPD provisions for NHS dispensing.
 

Product type
Do OPD +/- 10% rules apply?

Yes
No

POMs (see exceptions below)
√
 

Non-POMs including P, GSL and non-medicines (i.e.
ACBS products, food supplements, cosmetics, toiletries etc)

√

√

9.       A prescription requests 84 tablets of a product that is only available in a pack size of

30. Do I calculate +/- 10% based on the prescribed quantity or the pack size?
 
The OPD +/-10% rules apply to the prescribed quantity. 10% of 84 is 8.4, and using the rounding rules a pharmacist can supply either up to 8 more or 8 less tablets (in total between 76 tablets and 92 tablets) if it would allow supply of complete pack(s) only. So, supplying 3 x 30 tablets is permissible under the OPD +/-10% rules.
 

10.   Do the OPD +/-10% rules apply to all NHS prescriptions (electronic and FP10 paper forms)?

 
For NHS dispensing, the OPD +/-10% rules only apply to prescriptions issued electronically via EPS; this includes cross-border Welsh electronic prescriptions. All FP10 paper prescriptions (including any cross-border paper prescriptions issued in Northern Ireland, Scotland or Wales and dispensed in England) are excluded from OPD +/-10% rules so pharmacists will only be able to supply the prescribed quantity (unless the product is classed as a special container). DHSC’s view is that even though the percentage of paper prescriptions is small, it is still a significant volume, and as such would require manual intervention and require a disproportionate amount of resource for the NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) to read the quantity endorsements on paper prescriptions.
 

11.   What quantity do I supply if OPD +/-10% rules applied to the prescribed quantity does not result in a whole number?

 
If when applying the OPD+/-10% rules to the prescribed quantity it does not result in a whole number, pharmacists must round up or down to the nearest whole number. Where the quantity is above halfway pharmacists should round up to the nearest whole number. Where the quantity is exactly halfway or less, pharmacists should round down to the nearest whole number.
Some examples are included in table below:
 

Prescribed quantity

10% of the
prescribed quantity

Rounding rules explained

Solifenacin 5mg tablets x 28 tablets
2.8

2.8 can be rounded up to 3 to enable pharmacists to supply up to three more or three less tablets if it achieves whole pack dispensing. As a pack of 30 is available, the OPD +/-10% rules would allow a pharmacist to supply two extra tablets to supply and claim payment
for a complete pack size of 30 tablets.

Lacosamide 50mg tablets x 15 tablets
1.5

1.5 is exactly halfway therefore it must be rounded down to 1 to enable pharmacists to supply up to one more or one less tablet if it achieves whole pack dispensing. As a pack of 14 is available, the OPD
+/-10% rules would allow a pharmacist to supply one tablet less to
supply and claim payment for a complete pack of 14 tablets.

Fenofibrate micronized 67mg capsules
x 84 tablets

8.4
8.4 must be rounded down to 8 to enable pharmacists to supply up to eight more or eight less tablets if it achieves whole pack dispensing. As a pack of 90 is available, the OPD +/-10% rules would

 
 

 
 

allow a pharmacist to supply six extra tablets to supply and claim for
a complete pack size of 90 tablets.

 

12.   Do I need to notify the prescriber each time I have applied the OPD +/- 10% rules to an item ordered on a prescription?

 
There is no requirement to do so. However, if a patient is receiving up to 10% less than the prescribed quantity on a repeatable prescription item, the patient may need to re-order their next prescription earlier the following month. Good communication between the pharmacist, the GP and the patient will help to avoid any disruption to the patient’s treatment.
 

13.   Do the OPD +/- 10% rules apply to prescriptions issued in Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland and dispensed in England?

 
The +/-10% OPD rules can be applied to electronic prescriptions issued in Wales and dispensed in England. Reimbursement arrangements for Welsh prescriptions will be in line with EPS prescriptions dispensed in England. All NHS paper prescriptions from England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland are excluded from OPD arrangements.
 

14.   Can a patient refuse to accept a smaller quantity if the OPD +/-10% rules mean that the quantity supplied as a complete pack is less than original quantity prescribed?

 
Yes, a patient may refuse a supply under OPD+/-10% rules if it means that they are supplied with lesser quantity than that prescribed. In this case, the patient can be supplied the exact quantity ordered. For example, if the patient is prescribed 30 tablets and refuses to accept 28 tablets in a manufacturer’s original pack, the pharmacist can continue to supply the prescribed quantity.
 

15.   Does a patient still pay prescription charges if OPD +/-10% rules mean that the quantity dispensed as a complete pack is less than the original quantity prescribed?

 
Unless the patient holds a valid exemption reason or the item is free-of-charge on the NHS, prescription charges are payable for supplies made under +/-10% OPD rules even if this means that a patient is supplied with a smaller quantity of a medicine than was originally prescribed. It is only with quantity restriction Serious Shortage Protocols (SSPs) where a patient is exempted from paying prescription charges for receiving less than the original quantity prescribed.
 

16.   Can OPD +/-10% rules be used for prescriptions that are sent to an intra company hub?

 
A pharmacy company that owns a hub pharmacy can apply the OPD +/-10% rules to prescriptions that are sent to the hub (currently, the hub must be part of the same legal entity as the pharmacy).
 
Products not covered by OPD +/-10% rules
 

Are all Controlled Drugs excluded from OPD arrangements?

 
The OPD +/-10% rules can be applied to prescriptions for Schedule 5 Controlled Drugs (CDs), where appropriate. However, the rules do not apply to any CDs in Schedules 1 to 4 Schedules of the Misuse of Drugs Act and Regulations. Any prescriptions for Schedule 1 to 4 CDs will need to be supplied as the exact quantity ordered.
 

18.   Do the OPD +/-10% rules apply to prescriptions for unlicensed medicines?

 
The +/-10% OPD rules do not apply to unlicensed medicines commonly known as “specials”. These must continue to be supplied in the exact quantity ordered (unless the product is classed as a special container).
 

19.   Do the OPD +/-10% rules extend to any supplies made in accordance with a Serious Shortage Protocol (SSP) and Patient Group Directions (PGDs)?

 
For the time being, the OPD +/-10% rules only extend to supplies made against NHS prescriptions. Pending further legislative amendments, products supplied in accordance with Serious Shortage Protocols (SSPs) and Patient Group Directions (PGDs) remain outside the scope of OPD +/-10% rules. Community Pharmacy England will issue any further updates once the necessary changes to legislation are in place to enable pharmacists to apply the OPD +/-10% rules for supplies made against SSPs and PGDs.
 

20.   Do the OPD +/-10% rules apply to prescriptions for valproate-containing products?

 
Following amends to the Human Medicines Regulations 2012, valproate-containing products are subject to separate dispensing rules which came into force in October 2023. Subject to certain exceptions, the changes mandate whole pack dispensing of all valproate-containing products after they were reclassified as special containers. More information on special containers can be found on our special containers page.
 
Reimbursement arrangements
 

How will I be reimbursed for supplies made using the OPD +/- 10% rules for NHS dispensing?

 
Where the OPD +/-10% rules are applied to an eligible prescription item to enable whole pack dispensing, NHS reimbursement will be calculated as follows:
 

where the dispensed quantity matches the prescribed quantity, reimbursement will be calculated based on the prescribed quantity.
where the dispensed quantity is within +/-10% of the prescribed quantity, reimbursement will be calculated based on the dispensed quantity.

 

where the dispensed quantity is less than that prescribed, reimbursement will be calculated based on the dispensed quantity – this may be over 10% less (e.g. 50% less than that prescribed).
where the quantity supplied is greater than 10% (outside of HMR OPD provisions) of the prescribed quantity, reimbursement will be calculated based on the prescribed quantity.
where the product is classed as a special container, reimbursement will continue to be based on the nearest sub-pack/complete pack size.

This is summarised below:
 

Scenario
Reimbursed for

If the dispensed quantity is the same as the prescribed
quantity

Prescribed quantity

If the dispensed quantity is up to and including 10% more
than the prescribed quantity

Dispensed quantity

If the dispensed quantity is more than 10% of the
prescribed quantity

Prescribed quantity

If dispensed quantity is lower than the prescribed
quantity

Dispensed quantity

 
 

22.   How will the NHSBSA know what quantity I supplied in order to calculate reimbursement?

 
For EPS prescriptions dispensed from 1 January 2025, NHSBSA will utilise the existing quantity field in the Electronic Reimbursement Endorsement Message (EREM) or EPS claim message to check for the quantity supplied and reimburse accordingly (provided OPD +/-10% rules have been followed correctly).
 
Before utilising OPD +/-10% rules for NHS dispensing, pharmacy owners are advised to await confirmation from your IT system supplier regarding the availability of OPD functionality in their system.
 
Your PMR system will need to able to reflect the correct quantity dispensed value, which is per your input and expectation, into the EPS claim message (EREM), so that NHSBSA receive the correct dispensed quantity information and reimburse accordingly.
 
IT system suppliers have been encouraged to communicate to their users once the systems are OPD-ready (additional information can be found within the IT FAQs section below).
 

23.   Are any additional dispenser endorsements required on electronic prescriptions to notify NHSBSA of any supplies made using OPD +/- 10% rules?

 
No additional dispenser endorsements are required on electronic prescriptions to indicate to the NHSBSA if OPD +/-10% rules have been utilised. NHSBSA will use the existing quantity field in the Electronic Reimbursement Endorsement Message (EREM) or EPS claim message to check for
 
the quantity supplied and reimburse accordingly (provided OPD +/-10% rules have been followed correctly).
 
However, other existing prescription endorsement requirements remain unchanged. Pharmacy teams must continue to endorse prescriptions as per Clause 9B, Part II of the Drug Tariff for example, to endorse the supplier/brand and/or invoice price if a product is not listed in the Drug Tariff or to specify the pack size of a Category C product if more than one pack size is listed in the Tariff. For more information on prescription endorsements please refer to our Endorsement Guidance.
 

24.   If I do not utilise the OPD +/- 10% rules to supply a complete pack size, can I still make a claim for broken bulk if I need to split a pack to supply the exact quantity ordered?

 
The broken bulk (‘BB’) endorsement enables pharmacy teams to claim payment for a complete pack of an eligible product where only a part-pack has been dispensed and assuming the remaining quantity is unlikely to be dispensed again within the next 6 months. Broken bulk claims (in line with Clause 11, Part II of the Drug Tariff) can carry on as usual for non-OPD supplies. However, broken bulk claims would not be accepted if the dispensed quantity is +/- 10% of the prescribed quantity as this would imply that a complete pack was supplied to the patient.
 

25.   Will the 10p container allowance continue to be paid once the OPD arrangements are implemented?

 
Following the introduction of OPD, pharmacies will no longer receive the 10p container allowance if an original pack is supplied following OPD +/-10% rules. For example, if the dispensed quantity is +/- 10% of the prescribed quantity, then it will be assumed that an original pack was supplied, in which case the container allowance will not be paid. However, the 10p allowance will continue to be paid for all non-OPD supplies – where a split pack quantity is dispensed because the quantity ordered does not correspond to an available pack size.
 

26.   Where a price concession is granted for an item supplied as a complete pack following OPD +/-10% rules, will the improved price apply to the dispensed quantity or the original prescribed quantity?

 
If the OPD +/-10% rules have been correctly applied to an eligible prescription item to enable whole pack dispensing, any monthly price concession granted for this item will be applied to the dispensed quantity.
 

27.   How can I check if the NHSBSA has reimbursed me for the quantity dispensed for supplies made using the OPD +/- 10% rules?

 
Pharmacy owners are encouraged to sign-up and access their prescription item report through NHSBSA’s Information Services Portal. The prescription item report is a monthly data report showing reimbursement and renumeration for each item submitted for payment. The report allows a pharmacy owner to identify any payment discrepancies or endorsements errors. The pharmacy can sign up to access the prescription item report by following the steps in our How
 
to access your Prescription Item Reports factsheet. It would be sensible to consider spot checking that reimbursement is as expected for supplies made using OPD +/-10% rules. See: https://cpe.org.uk/reconciling.
 
IT systems functionality
 

Is there a deadline for IT systems to have functionality in place to support OPD+/- 10% rules?

 
There is no fixed deadline for IT system suppliers to have functionality in place for PMR systems to support utilisation of OPD +/-10% rules. Therefore, all IT system suppliers may not be ready to implement OPD functionality into their systems from 1st January 2025. System suppliers had requested at least six months for IT development but were provided the information to support the changes very late.
 

29.   Should I continue to supply the exact quantity ordered if my system does not yet support 10% +/- OPD rules?

 
Pharmacists must consider OPD but do not have to utilise it if for example, IT systems do not have the functionality in place for allow claiming payment for up to 10% more or less than the prescribed quantity.
 

30.   How will I know once my system supplier has enabled OPD +/- 10% changes?

 
Community Pharmacy England has encouraged all IT system suppliers to inform their customers once OPD functionality has been fully tested and enabled for use by pharmacies.
 

31.   Does my PMR system need to put in place validation to prevent inadvertent selection of products outside the scope of OPD +/-10% rules or a quantity that exceeds 10% of the prescribed quantity (except for special containers)?

 
The EPS dispensing system specification encourages suppliers to introduce validation support, such as warnings for unusual dispensed quantities being input. To help pharmacy teams apply the OPD +/- 10% rules correctly, IT systems can prompt users if the product or quantity selected falls outside the scope of the OPD arrangements. There may be variation in the level of built-in validation offered by different IT systems to support pharmacies in applying the OPD +/- 10% rules correctly. Some IT suppliers may seek to introduce functionality immediately whereas others may choose a later date to release the changes across their estate.
 

32.   How can I check that the correct dispensed quantity values are being submitted in the EPS claim message submitted to the NHSBSA?

 
Line-by-line reconciliation is possible and can be checked on an ad hoc basis by checking the PMR input vs the detailed pricing information available in the Prescription Item Reports. Some pharmacy owners use software to automate this process. More information is available at:
 
cpe.org.uk/reconciling – see related FAQs regarding reconciliation of payments for electronic and paper prescriptions, which references use of the Prescription Item Reports.
 

33.   Do I need to manually input the dispensed quantity each time into the EPS claim message or is the quantity field automatically populated either when I generate the dispensing label or select the product from the dropdown picking list?

 
Many PMR systems do not require for the dispensed quantity to be manually input every time – given the workload implications. Suppliers are aware that most prescriptions (estimates indicate over 95% of prescriptions) the dispensed quantity value will default to the prescribed quantity. However, pharmacy teams will be given the option to manually override this by allowing an input of an alternative dispensed quantity.
 

34.   How would I escalate an EPS or PMR issue regarding OPD?

 
For information on escalation processes of any PMR issues please see our one-page NHS IT/EPS escalation guide.
 
Annex A – Worked examples
 
Products outside the scope of OPD +/- 10% rules
 

I have received a prescription for unlicensed Flunarizine 10mg tablets x 28, however the specials supplier can only supply in pack sizes of 30. Can I use the OPD +/-10% rules to supply and claim for a complete pack of 30 tablets?

 
Flunarizine 10mg tablets is an unlicensed medicine listed in Part VIIID of the Drug Tariff. The OPD
+/-10% rules do not apply to any specials. Unlicensed medicines must continue to be supplied in the exact quantity ordered (unless the product is classed a special container).
 

36.   I have received a prescription for a Schedule 2 Controlled Drug, Dexamfetamine 10mg tablets x 28 tablets. As this product is only available in packs of 30, can I supply and claim for a complete pack of 30 tablets following OPD +/-10% rules?

 
No, a pharmacist can only supply and claim for 28 tablets in accordance with quantity stated on the prescription. This is because Dexamfetamine is a Schedule 2 CD and the OPD +/-10% rules do not apply to any CDs in Schedules 1 to 4 of the Misuse of Drugs Act and Regulations. The OPD +/-10% rules can be applied to prescriptions for Schedule 5 Controlled Drugs (CDs), where appropriate
 

37.   I have received a prescription for BD Viva hypodermic insulin needles for pre-filled / reusable pen injectors screw on 4mm/32gauge x 100 needles. As this product is only available in packs of 90 needles, can I use OPD +/-10% rules supply a complete pack of 90 needles?

 
No, this is because any appliance listed in Part IXA in the Drug Tariff falls outside the scope of OPD arrangements. The OPD +/-10% rules do not apply to Part IX appliances so these must continue to be supplied in the exact quantity ordered, unless the product is classed as a special container. As BD Viva hypodermic insulin needles for pre-filled / reusable pen injectors screw on 4mm/32gauge is not a special container, the pharmacy should supply and be reimbursed for supplying 100 needles as ordered on the prescription.
 
Supplying the exact quantity ordered on the prescription
 

I have received a prescription for Estradiol 500microgram transdermal gel sachets x 14 sachets. As this products come in packs of 28, can I supply and claim for a complete pack of 28 tablets?

 
No, this would fall outside of the OPD +/- 10% rules. Following the rounding down rules a quantity of 14 would only allow for the supply of 1 more or 1 less sachet. This is because 10% of 14 sachet works out to 1.4 tablets and following rounding rules a pharmacist can supply up to 1 more sachet or 3 less sachet than the prescribed quantity if it allows whole pack dispensing. As Estradiol 500microgram transdermal gel sachets are only available in a pack of 28 and the item is not
 
classed as a special container, pharmacists should dispense 14 sachets as prescribed and will be reimbursed accordingly.
 
Supplying up to 10% less of the prescribed quantity
 

I have received a prescription for Paroxetine 40mg tablets x 30. This product comes in packs of 28 and 30. Can I supply a complete pack of 28 tablets using OPD

+/- 10% rules?
 
If a prescription is received for a pack a 30 x Paroxetine 40mg tablets, the pharmacy should supply this pack size if it is readily available. If the 30 pack size is not readily available, a pharmacist can use the +/-10% OPD rules to supply two less tablets in order to provide a complete pack of 28 tablets. Reimbursement would be calculated based on the dispensed quantity using the Part VIII price listed in the Drug Tariff. In some cases where a much lower quantity is supplied (i.e. more than 10% less than the prescribed quantity), for example the patient only needed 14 tablets out of 28 ordered, the pharmacy would be reimbursed for 14 tablets dispensed. Please note, a patient receiving less than the prescribed quantity may need to re-order their next prescription earlier the following month. Good communication between the pharmacist, the GP and the patient will help to avoid any disruption to the patient’s treatment.
 

40.   I have received a prescription for Levothyroxine 50microgram tablets x 30. The only available pack size is 28 tablets. Can I use the OPD +/- 10% rules to supply the patient with a complete pack of 28 tablets?

 
Yes, as a pack of 28 is the only pack size available, the OPD +/-10% rules would allow you to supply and claim for a complete pack size of 28 tablets against a prescription ordering 30 tablets. This is because 10% of 30 tablets works out to 3 tablets to enable a pharmacist to supply up to 3 more tablets or 3 less tablets than the prescribed quantity if it allows whole pack dispensing. Please note, a patient receiving up to 10% less than the prescribed quantity may need to re-order their next prescription earlier the following month. Good communication between the pharmacist, the GP and the patient will help to avoid any disruption to the patient’s treatment.
 
Supplying up to 10% more of the prescribed quantity
 

I have received a prescription for Co-careldopa 12.5mg/50mg tablets x 84. The only available pack size is 90. Can I use the OPD +/-10% rules to supply the patient with a complete pack of 90 tablets?

 
Yes, the OPD +/-10% rules would allow you to supply 6 more tablets and claim for a complete pack size of 90 tablets against a prescription ordering 84 tablets. This is because 10% of 84 tablets works out to 8.4 tablets, which once rounded down would enable a pharmacist to supply up to 8 more tablets or 8 less tablets than the quantity prescribed if it allows whole pack dispensing.
 

42.   I have received a prescription for Evra® transdermal patches x 8 patches. Can I use OPD +/-10% rules to supply and claim for a complete pack size of 9 patches?

 
Yes, as Evra® patches are available in packs of 9, the OPD +/-10% rules would allow pharmacists to supply 1 more patch and claim for a complete pack of 9 patches. 10% of 8 patches works out to 0.8 and following the rounding rules, pharmacists can supply up to 1 more or less patch if it allows whole pack dispensing.
 

43.   I have received a prescription for a Schedule 5 Controlled Drug (CD), Dihydrocodeine 30mg tablets x 28 tablets. Can I apply OPD +/-10% rules to supply and claim for a complete pack size of 30 tablets?

 
Yes, the OPD +/-10% rules can be applied to prescriptions for Schedule 5 Controlled Drugs (CDs), where appropriate. If a prescription orders 28 tablets, the pharmacy should supply this pack size if it is readily available. If the 28 pack size is not readily available, the pharmacist could apply OPD
+/-10% rules to provide 2 extra tablets and claim for a complete pack size of 30 tablets. This is because 10% of 28 tablets works out to 2.8 tablets and following the rounding rules, pharmacists can supply up to 3 more tablets or 3 less tablets if it allows whole pack dispensing. For supplying a pack of 30, the pharmacy would be reimbursed based on Part VIII price listed in the Tariff. Please note as Dihydrocodeine is a Schedule 5 CD, pharmacists must apply their professional judgement to decide if it is clinically appropriate for the patient to receive more than the prescribed quantity particularly if there are any concerns of reliance or addiction.
 

44.   I have received a prescription for Aspirin 300mg tablets x 128. This product comes in packs of 30 and 100. Can I use OPD +/-10% rules to supply and claim payment for a total of 130 tablets using a combination of the two different pack sizes available?

 
Yes, OPD +/-10% rules would allow you to claim for 130 tablets (by supplying two different pack sizes of 30 and 100) against a prescription ordering 128 tablets. This is because 10% of 128 tablets works out to 12.8 tablets, which once rounded up would enable a pharmacist to supply up to 13 more or 13 less tablets than the quantity prescribed if it allows whole pack dispensing.
 
Supplying greater than 10% of the prescribed quantity
 

I have a received prescription for Colecalciferol 10,000units/ml oral drops sugar free x 15ml. This product is a special container in a pack size of 10ml. Can I apply OPD +/-10% rules to supply and claim payment for two complete packs of 10 ml?

 
No, as the prescription orders 15ml x Colecalciferol 10,000units/ml oral drops sugar free, the pharmacy would only be reimbursed for one complete pack of 10ml. This is because Colecalciferol 10,000units/ml oral drops sugar free in 10ml pack size is listed as a special container in Part VIIIA of the Drug Tariff. For Colecalciferol 10,000units/ml oral drops sugar free, payment is based on the 10ml pack size because the quantity ordered of 15ml falls exactly halfway between the two pack sizes. If 16ml was ordered, this would allow a pharmacist to round up to the nearest pack size (or multiples of) to provide 20ml (2 packs of 10ml). Products classed as special containers are excluded from the OPD +/-10% rules so pharmacy owners can supply
 
and will be reimbursed for the nearest pack size (complete pack or sub pack) or combination of containers nearest to the quantity ordered.
 

46.   I have received a prescription for Pyridostigmine bromide 60mg tablets x 168 tablets. This product is a special container in a pack size of 200 tablets. Can I supply and claim payment for a complete pack of 200 tablets against a prescription ordering 168 tablets?

 
Pyridostigmine bromide 60mg tablets in a pack size of 200 is listed as a special container in Part VIIIA of the Drug Tariff. If a prescription orders 168 x Pyridostigmine bromide 60mg tablets, the pharmacy would be reimbursed for a complete pack of 200 tablets. This is because products classed as special containers are excluded from the OPD +/-10% rules so pharmacy owners can supply and will be reimbursed for the nearest pack size (complete pack or sub pack) or combination of containers nearest to the quantity ordered.
For more information on special containers, please see our page Special containers and products requiring reconstitution.

articles.title: 5 Day Claims Window - When Will I Get Paid?
Endorsing
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Endorsements can be added at different stages of the dispensing process. They can be added at clinical check, after labeling, or from the claim screen. To add a prescriber endorsement from the clinical check screen, just edit the item by clicking the edit pencil, and then click additional endorsements. You can then select from any of the relevant endorsements and add the details as needed. You can add either prescriber or dispenser endorsements from the labeling page. Firstly, you'll need to label the item as normal. Once this is done, click edit. Then click on the radial menu button and choose endorsements. From here, you can select the endorsement you want and add the appropriate details. Don't forget to click complete when you're done. Finally, let's look at adding an endorsement from the claim screen. After you hand out a prescription and all items have been accounted for, it will appear on the claim screen. Start by searching for the patient. The easiest way to do this is to click on the filters button in the patient column, turn off case sensitivity, and then set the search type to contains. Now just enter the patient name and click apply. Once you have found the patient, click view details to look at their prescriptions from the flyout. You can click on the item that you want to endorse and select the relevant options as required.

articles.title: Exemptions
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Due to NHS digital guidelines, we are unable to automatically enter an exemption for a patient at handout. This is because they consider the prescription to be exempt rather than the patient. For this reason, you will normally need to enter the exemption at the handout stage. The last known exemption will show on the batch flyout when you click the card. When you click handout, you will also see it at the top of the screen, but it's always recommended that you check the exemption status with the patient before you enter the value here. If the patient is not exempt, use the "Not Exempt" option. Do not click "Skip" only if you failed to capture the exemption at the point of handout. If you need to click the skip button, doing this will add the item to the claim screen as normal, but you will not be able to process the claim until you've entered an exemption. Sometimes when you hand out, you'll see that you have not been asked to enter an exemption at all. This is for one of a few reasons. Either the patient is age-exempt, an exemption was found using the real-time exemption checking app, or the prescription was not an EPS prescription. You can check if the RTEC was done by looking at the batch flyout. Just click on the batch from the prescription board, and you'll see the status near the top. If the RTEC was not done, you can manually do it at this stage. Just make sure that your smart card is authenticated. Select the prescription from the batch flyout and click "Perform RTEC" to see what exemption was entered. After the handout, just go to the claim screen, where you'll be able to see all exemptions recorded for the current month. If you skipped the exemption on handout but had previously captured an exemption on an older prescription, it is possible to automatically copy over the last known exemption from the previous handout. You'll notice that the last exemption column will display the exemption even though there is nothing in the exemption column itself. Just click the "Copy Exemption" button to bring over the old exemptions. Finally, if you want to amend an exemption that was entered incorrectly, just click "View Details." Click on the exemption button, then click "Proceed" or "Edit," depending on whether or not this is the first time an exemption has been entered. Select the new exemption. Don't forget to click "Save." Otherwise, the changes will be lost.

articles.title: Real Time Exemption Checking (RTEC)
articles.content:
Real Time Exemption Service (RTEC)
In collaboration with NHS Digital and NHS Business Services Authority, Titan can check with the RTEC service whether the patient has a known exemption.
 
What is RTEC?
RTEC is an NHS service that allows pharmacies to digitally check whether a patient has any known exemptions. If a known exemption is found for the patient, then Titan will let the user know that the patient is exempt. This would mean that the patient would not need to be asked whether they are exempt as well as not having to provide evidence of their exemption.
 
What are the benefits of RTEC?
There are great benefits to using the RTEC service.

Reduce the risks of contractor loss caused by pharmacy staff inadvertently submitting EPS prescriptions with a paid status when the category should have been exempt
Enable a reduction in the number of EPS tokens which have to be printed, completed by patients and then be sent from pharmacies to the NHSBSA
Provide a more efficient digital process for pharmacy staff, reducing the time spent helping patients complete declarations, checking physical evidence of exemption status and sorting tokens for submission to the NHSBSA
Reduce the risk to the NHS of prescription fraud due to a decrease in false prescription exemption claims
Increase convenience for patients, as there will be less need for them to provide physical proof of exemption from prescription charges

Are there any limitations to RTEC?
There are some limitations to RTEC that users should be aware of.

The RTEC service can only be used for EPS R2 prescriptions and for pharmacies within England
If the RTEC service returns that the patient is exempt for the prescription, Titan cannot tell the user what the specific exemption the patient has for that prescription
RTEC currently recognises five exemptions which are:

Maternity
Prescription prepayment
Tax credits
Medical
HC2 (full help)

In the future, RTEC will also be aware of these exemptions for patients:

Income Support
Income-related Employment & Support Allowance
Universal Credit
Pension Credit Guarantee Credit
Income-based Jobseekers Allowance

Due to the fact that RTEC may not be aware of a particular exemption for a patient, if an RTEC check returns back that no exemptions are known for the patient, staff should continue with the usual process of asking the patient whether they are exempt, capture signature and ask for evidence where appropriate

How do I use RTEC in Titan?
Using RTEC in Titan is very easy. There are three ways of digitally checking the RTEC service to check if any known exemptions are known for the patient. 
Auto RTEC
If this setting is enabled in the Marketplace Settings, then an RTEC check is done automatically once the user presses either the button ‘Complete & exit’ or ‘Do another’ or ‘Label now’ after having completed clinical checks. The Smart Card will need to be in and authenticated at this time for it to work.
The RTEC status of the prescription can be seen by going to the prescription flyout. 
Manually check RTEC
It is also possible to manually check RTEC by going to the flyout for the prescription. From the Pick stage onwards, expand the Prescriptions section, click on the relevant prescription and then press the ‘Perform RTEC’ button at the bottom of the flyout.
There are some scenarios where users are not able to perform an RTEC check. Scenarios such as:

The patient is age exempt, deceased or has a sensitive flag
User not authenticated to a smart card or their smart card user not having the B0570 activity permission
All prescribed items on the EPS R2 prescription have CC or FS prescriber endorsements 

 
Bulk
From the claims screen, tick the patients that you want to check and then click "Perform RTEC"
RTEC audit
 
There is an audit log for RTEC which is accessible by going to the prescription flyout and clicking ‘View full details’ above the prescription image which will display the Prescription/Item Tracker. Go to ‘RTEC Audit’ to see all interactions with RTEC.
 
What about Claims?
If the RTEC response for the patient is exempt for the prescription, then on the Claims screen it will state ‘RTEC - Patient does not need to pay the prescription charge’ as the exemption category for the prescription. This exemption category is not editable. These claims will need to be digitally submitted to NHSBSA by following the usual process in Titan by pressing ‘Save & Claim’.
As the prescription is exempt according to RTEC, the token will not need to be signed by the patient or sent to NHSBSA. The exemption to this is prescriptions with Controlled Drugs (schedule 2 & 3) where the patient is still expected to sign the token and for the token to be sent to NHSBSA.
 
Want to know more?
For more information on RTEC, go to https://psnc.org.uk/dispensing-supply/eps/electronic-prescription-service-eps-sitemap/real-time-exemption-checking-rtec/ or contact the Titan support service desk.

articles.title: What to do if My Patient Disputes the RTEC Status?
articles.content:
We have received an update from the NHS on handling situations where RTEC deems a patient exempt, but the patient disagrees.

In these cases, there's no need to charge the patient. The RTEC exemption ensures their prescription doesn't enter the PCN sample, preventing any fines for the patient.Check out the diagram below to understand how TITAN retrieves the RTEC status. Remember, this process is consistent across all PMRs, and we can't influence RTEC's results.

Transcript (AI Generated):
Titan is complete with many different types of prescription checks that will be presented to you during the initial check stage to ensure that each item on the prescription is both safe and effective for the intended patient's use. Titan will also help you to determine for each patient the suitability of the medication and the quantity. It will highlight possible clinical intervention requirements in different areas based on known drug interactions and the possibility of therapeutic duplication. Titan can also identify if the prescriber is not licensed to prescribe the item, if the patient is allergic to an ingredient, or if the item is inappropriate for the patient's age. Interactions are split into low, medium, high, and severe levels, and when identified, you will normally be given two options. Click accept to permit the dispensing of an item or do not dispense to cancel it. If you decided to not dispense one of the items during the check stage, you'll see a warning on save. Just checking that this was intentional. Other item-level checks that you're likely to see will include discontinued items, NMS checks, pack size checks, duplicate therapy checks, unknown unit of measure checks. You can also see patient-level checks such as the child check, which informs you that the patient is under 12 years old, or allergy checks, where Titan will tell you if one of the items on the prescription contains an ingredient to which the patient is allergic. and there are many more.

articles.title: Duplicate Therapy and Drug Doubling - Exclusions
articles.content:
TITAN Will alert you of potential Duplicate Therapy and Drug Doubling at clinical check.
 
Duplicate Therapy is normally alerted when an item on a Prescription is found in the same BNF category as another item on the prescription or in the patient's dispensing history.
 
Drug Doubling is normally alerted when a item contains the same active ingredient as another item on the prescription or in the patient's dispensing history.
 
Items found in the categories detailed in this list are excluded from these checks. Showing a clinical check for such items is deemed to be either excessive or irrelevant (e.g. catheters). These exclusions have been carefully reviewed by our clinical safety team.
 
To find the category that a drug is in, see the number in brackets after the item name on this website.
 
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vS6eWGiameL9-OAWzQA2dOL14X3qAdxl1yLdSzAbXgPCv0v4djhiAzxAQq42V9qiSdlT5Q1N8nBTYvd/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true

articles.title: Patient Matching
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
When processing a new prescription in Titan, the first thing that we need to do is to clinically check the prescription to make sure that it's safe to dispense. To begin, we'll click the prescription from the inbox and click process. For most prescriptions, as in this example, the prescription will be fully matched to the patient record. Sometimes the data that you hold in your system will be slightly different to that of the prescription. This will result in a partial match. When you see a partial match, just click accept to link the prescription to the recommended patient. When dealing with partial matches, it is possible that there will be more than one similar patient in the Titan database. This poses a risk as the prescription could get matched to the wrong patient. To ensure that this doesn't happen, just click find patient, select the correct patient from the list and click submit. You will see a side-by-side comparison of the Titan patient and the patient on the prescription. Clicking yes will link the prescription to the Titan patient and update the Titan patient's records to match that of the prescription processing. No match prescriptions is very similar to processing the partial match ones. Just click Add Patient to create a new patient record in Titan that matches the prescription. If you want to check if the patient is already in the system, use the find patient button. Similar patients will be presented, which you can use to link the prescription to if necessary.

The Titan Dashboard is a great way to draw in some vital information for your pharmacy in real time. I'm going to take you through each part. articles.title: Prescription Statuses
articles.content:
Inbox = The prescription has just arrived electronically (EPS, bar code scan, Primo or PowerMail)
 
Check = The prescription data has been entered manually but still required a clinical check
 
Parked = The prescription has been checked but has been put into the "parked" column to delay dispensing. Either manually during clinical check or automatically via a tag setting. It will need to be released from parked. Click here for more info.
 
In Progress = This is a high level status that covers multiple stages. The clinical checks have been done but it has not yet been handed out.
 
Returned = The EPS prescription has been returned to the Spine (England only)
 
Withdrawn = The prescription items have been handed out or ND'd and the dispense notification (DN) sent to the Spine, but the user has then "withdrawn" the DN, resetting the prescription to the Inbox (England)
 
Cleansed = The prescription has been automatically removed from the Prescription Board and the Spine due to it's age (England).

This happens 90 days after the prescription expires if not handed out. 
If handed out but not claimed, the cleansing will happened 180 days after hand out (thus removing it from the claim screen)Not Downloaded = TBC

Handed Out = The item has been handed out to the patient and the DN sent if England
 
Archived = A user has archived the prescription, essentially deleting the prescription from the Prescription Board without dispensing it. A record of the archived prescription will remain in the history (non EPS prescriptions only)
 
Expired = The prescription has expired in accordance with NHS rules
 
Complete = All prescription items have been dispensed or ND'd and the claim has been sent

articles.title: Accuracy Checks
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
To access accuracy checks, just scan the picking label. If there are still items in the batch on owing or still to be labeled, you'll be taken to the labeling screen. If this happens, just click "Package Now." You now have two options. You can either do the accuracy check and then bag the items up, ready to be handed out or shelved, or you can do the checks and leave the batch for the dispenser to bag up. Let's start with the all-in-one method. First, at the top of the screen, you can see the items that need to go into the bag, and in the middle, you can see the empty white box that indicates that the bag is empty. To start the checking process, begin by scanning the QR code on the dispensing label. Titan will now tell you why the item actually needs to be checked. For example, you may see "Split pack barcode not scanned," "Controlled drug," or other things depending on your settings. After you have performed the accuracy check, click "Accept Checks" to add it to the bag. If you like, you can also scan the manufacturer's barcode at this stage to verify that the label has been put on the right pack. If you are having trouble scanning the QR code, just click the quantity box on the medicine label card to add it manually. Be careful though, as doing it this way will prevent Titan from checking that you have the right patient's meds in front of you. If you prefer to do the accuracy check and then leave the bagging for the dispenser, rather than scanning the items into the bag yourself, just click "Quick Check." You can now perform all of your checks and then click "Accept Selected Checks," or you can accept all the checks in one go. Once the checks have been done, you can return the batch to the dispenser, who will now be able to quick package the batch from the labeling screen, or access the packaging screen to scan them into the bag one at a time. Incidentally, depending on the role-based access controls that you have given to the particular user, they may not be able to access the packaging screen if there are items that need to be checked. And that's it.

articles.title: Advanced Labelling
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Sometimes Titan won't recognize the manufacturer's barcode when you scan it. Should this happen, you'll need to print the dispensing label manually. To do this, click on the gray dispensing label box. Select the manufacturer and click manually add. When dispensing smaller pack sizes than as written on the prescription, you don't need to worry about it. Just grab the box and scan the manufacturer's barcode as normal. Titan will do the rest. If you want to split a pack, click the split button and enter the quantity that you wish to dispense, followed by a comma and then the quantity remaining. You can enter the batch number and expiry date if you like, and they'll be printed on the dispensing label. To send the remaining quantity to owing, click the blue circle control and select owing. In this example, the prescription is for 7,000 grams, but we don't want to label each box individually. So click the split button and enter "1 x 7,000." This will now give you one dispensing label for 7,000 grams and will prevent you from having to scan each item individually. If during labeling you notice that a dose needs to be changed or the quantity of the item, click the blue circular control and click "Edit Item." From here, you can change the dose or the quantity, and then just click save. Further labels will come out with the updated information. If you spot an item that doesn't need to be dispensed again, click on the blue circle control and click "Do Not Dispense." From here, you'll be presented with a list of all the usual reasons when you can select the most appropriate one and click submit. Endorsements can also be added at this time, although you do need to make sure that you fully labeled the item first. To add an endorsement, click edit, and then the circle. Click endorse and then select the relevant endorsement. When you're done, click submit. And finally, click complete to save everything.
