articles.title: ERD
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Let's take a detailed look at the Titan Electronic Repeat Dispensing process, or ERD for short. When a prescriber writes an ERD prescription, they will upload it to the spine with a given interval and a schedule of release dates for each issue. On these dates, the spine will make sure that the issue is available, and the issues will automatically be downloaded with your nominated downloads. Now, this is fine if you deal with a low number of ERDs or if you're always happy for the issues to just get downloaded as soon as they're ready. But for some pharmacies, you want to manage things a little more closely. You may wish to download all your issues in one go, so you can just manage everything from the board, or you may wish to never download anything at all until the patient requests the medication. Some pharmacies may choose to download all the issues in one go, but to only dispense one at a time as and when they're needed. So all combinations, plus quite a few more, are possible with Titan by using the different download settings or the release and unlock features. We'll not be able to go through all the possible approaches today, but I will try to show you how you can control exactly when items will appear on the board and when you're prompted to check and dispense them. So let's take a look at Titan. The first thing we need to do is to make sure that we've got everything set up properly. Just go into the settings cog and hit the clinical settings tab. To begin with, we're gonna set up the release buffer. This will define when Titan attempts to download your next issue. If you set it to zero, then all issues will come down on the day scheduled by the prescriber. If you set it to one, then Titan will try to pull down the issue one day early. Bear in mind that an issue may only be manually pulled down early if the previous issue dispense notification has been sent. This normally happens at handout, meaning that you need to have handed out the previous issue before you can pull down the next one. Of course, when you're doing clinical checks, you can pull them down in a batch all in one go. We'll look at that in a moment. The next option to decide is if you want to be prompted to set up your ERDs during clinical check. We recommend that you turn this on so that you don't miss anything, and it's during clinical check where you can actually choose to pull down an entire batch of ERDs all in one go. Next is the default auto-release state. Toggle on if you want prescriptions to show on your board as soon as they're downloaded, or leave it off if you want to manually release them when you're ready. Next, we have the ERD date range setting. This setting controls how many ERD prescriptions are displayed on the ERD view when the screen first loads. A wider date range is obviously more convenient, but it will add to screen load times if you've got a lot of ERDs or if you've got a particularly slow internet connection. So it's probably best to leave it as it is for now and adjust it later depending on performance. Then you'll need to go into the dispensing settings tab and decide if you want to automatically print your ERD labels when you close the package. This label will list all the ERD items in your package and will detail the issue number that the item is dispensed on, highlighting if it's the last issue. A great way to let your patients know when it's time to order. We recommend that you turn this on, but if you don't, you can always manually print the label from the packaging screen. Next, if you go over to the miscellaneous section, you'll see a setting called Auto Realign ERD Dates on Handout. Turning this setting on will change the release date of a prescription based on the previous issue's handout date. So, for example, if issue two was handed out on the and the interval is seven days, issue three will be set to the next appropriate date. This way, the issue will appear on the board at the previous handout date plus the interval. And finally, for the setup, it's a good idea to tag all your ERD prescriptions so that you can filter them out on the prescription board.To do this, go down to prescription tags and hit the plus button. Give the new tag a name and toggle on repeat dispensing prescription. This tag will now automatically be applied to any new ERD prescriptions when they get downloaded. Now let's take a look at an incoming ERD prescription. If you have prompt for setup turned on, then you'll see a clinical check like this. For all ERDs, just click the Yes option to open the ERD flyer. If you've had the setting off, then you can still access the flyout manually by clicking on the pencil icon. The first thing to do is check the interval. Just check that it looks correct based on the prescribed quantities, and if not, you can always edit it by hitting the edit pencil and entering the correct value. Next, we can choose whether the prescription should automatically be released on the scheduled release date or not. If you set this to off, then you'll need to manually pull down the issue when it's due from the ERD flyout. Next, we have the option to edit individual issues' release dates. This is the date that the patient requires the medication on and is initially set by the prescriber. Note that both the due date and the release date are displayed on the flyout. The release date is the date that the issue is due to show up on your prescription board. This will normally be the due date minus your buffer setting. You'll also see that both Titan and NHS statuses are displayed on the flyout. This can be useful for identifying when the next issue date is or if it's being dispensed. The NHS status will load automatically if you've got your smart card in when the flyout opens, but if it doesn't load, just pop your smart card in and then click check NHS tracker. At the bottom of the screen, you'll see a dustbin icon. You can use this to cancel all future issues. To cancel on the spine, you will need to contact the prescriber. Also, any other prescriptions in progress on the prescription board will not be affected, so don't forget to find them and then update them as needed. Finally, we have the release issues button. Clicking this button will pull down any issues from the spine that are available. Please note that if there are any issues from the batch already on the board, you will need to hand these out before you can use this function. Once we've set up the ERD as we wish, it's just a case of dispensing the items like normal. Now, let's go and take a look at the ERD view. Go to Views and hit the ERD tab. From here, you can see all the ERDs in your pharmacy within the selected date range. If you wanted to see completed ones too, you can go to Filters and check the Show Completed ERDs box. Clicking on any prescription will open the ERD flyout where you can make all the same alterations as before. Let's say that you're a pharmacy that prefers to turn off auto release and control when the ERDs drop down. What you can do here is filter by due date for the next few days, select all, and click bulk release. If you scroll across to the right, you'll see the auto release status for each prescription. You can change the setting by either clicking into the flyout and changing one prescription at a time, or you can select and set auto release to on or off in bulk. Back to the prescription board, and you'll see a handy feature called "unrelease." To use this feature, click on any card in the inbox or the check column and click unrelease. You'll then be prompted to enter your preferred release date, and the prescription will now be removed from the board until the date that you specified. Finally, if we open a patient's record from Power Search, you'll see that we've included a handy ERD panel. From here, you can see a record of all the active ERDs, their status, the release date, and the due date. If an issue has previously been unreleased, you'll be able to manually release it from here, and you can also click on the chevron to open the ERD flyout if needed. Hopefully, this video gives you an idea of all the different settings that are available within ERD. We hope that we've given you enough options to set up a process that works for you, but please do give the help desk a call if you're struggling with anything at all, and we'll help to find the best implementation of ERD in your pharmacy.

articles.title: Hand Out
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
When handing out a particular package for a patient, the easiest way to do it is to scan the bag label from the power search screen. Just click F9 to access power search and scan the bag label. Titan will return information about the package, and there's a handout button just down the bottom. Clicking handout will send the dispense notification to the spine in England and will record the package as having been given to the patient. It's important that you don't hand out items unless they've actually been given to the patient, as this can cause other problems further down the line. At this point, you can record the exemption or mark them as not exempt if appropriate. Another easy way to hand out an item is to do it from the prescription board. Click the filters button and type the patient's name. Select the patient from the search results. The easy way to do this is to use the down arrow and click enter on your keyboard. Once you filter the prescription board to show the prescriptions for the patient, you'll not only see those prescriptions that are ready to be handed out but also if there are any other items at different stages. In this example, we can see that there's a new prescription in the inbox. We can see that there's a prescription in labeling and also one ready to hand out. So this means that although we can hand out the prescription in the handout column, we may want to ask the patient to wait a moment while we dispense everything else. However, if we're happy to hand out the item in the handout column, all we need to do is click that item and click the handout button. And from here, as before, we just enter the exemptions and click submit. When we refresh the prescription board, you'll see that the item has disappeared from the board and will now be available on the claim screen. We can also hand out immediately after dispensing, for example, from the labeling screen. Once everything's been labeled, we just need to click the handout button. And from the check or packaging screen, it's very similar. Close the package and click handout. Of course, the best way to do the handouts is to use our EDO handout system, but that will be covered in a different video.

articles.title: Instalment Dispensing (MDA)
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Begin by entering the prescription header as normal, but selecting FP 10 MDAS from the prescription types. Search for the patient and select them when you find them. Search for the item name as normal and enter the dose. Enter the total prescribed quantity as permitted by the prescription, and enter the number of installments. From the first calendar control, select the date that the patient will begin taking their medicine. This pharmacy closes on a Sunday, so we'll give that dose on the Saturday, but we'll set it to unsupervised. Then proceed with dispensing the first dose as normal. There's a special screen for installment dispensing, which can be found in the views button, and then clicking the installment dispensing tab at the top. Clicking on the patient's record will show the progress of their prescription. In this case, we can see that one installment has already been handed out. You can look at the filters option to change the next installment due date. And from here, we can click on other items and see their progress. From the flyout, you can click "Go to Labeling" to take you straight into the dispensing screens for that patient. Click on the circle control to add endorsements or to edit the installment dates. And that's all there is to it.

articles.title: Manual Labelling
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Titan's unique barcode product verification system can be bypassed if needed. We call this way of producing a dispensing label manual labeling. The main reason you would want to do this is if neither the FMD nor the product barcode is recognized, or if you want to overrule the system to dispense a slightly different product to that which was prescribed. In this case, the dispenser has decided to dispense some tablets against the prescription for capsules. To manually label this item, just click the label placeholder, select a product, and click manually add. Because Titan can no longer guarantee that the item labeled is the correct item or a suitable replacement, and because the setting "Pharmacist must check non-bar coded items" has been turned on, the dispenser is unable to package this item and it will need a final check.

articles.title: Owings
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Sending an item to owing couldn't be easier. Just hit the radial menu control and click Owings. Depending on your settings, an owing label will be printed automatically. After clicking save and exit, we can see the batch card now shows the Owings badge to indicate that there's an owing within. Now, let's redeem the owing. Just scan the owing label or the picking label to quickly access the labeling page and then scan the product barcode. We can easily combine the Owings process with the split pack process to create a partial owing. Start by splitting the pack as normal. Enter the quantity to dispense, a comma, and then the quantity to send to owing. Scan the manufacturer's barcode to label the split pack quantity, and then send the remainder to Owings as before. Now we will package the split quantity to see what has happened. Back on the prescription board, we can see that the batch has been split into two. The packaged quantity is ready to handout, and the owings quantity remains in labeling, ready to be redeemed when the stock arrives.

articles.title: Packaging
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
There are different ways to access the packaging screen depending on what screen you are on at the time. From the labeling screen, once you've finished with all of the labeling, just click "Package Now." If you're on the prescription board and all of the items have already been labeled, scanning the picking label will take you directly to packaging. If you want to access the packaging screen for a specific patient but you don't have a picking label to scan, start by searching for that patient on the prescription board using the filters. Then click on the batch card and click "Package Now." Adding items to a package is easy. Just scan the barcode on the dispensing label and the item will go straight down into the package. Once you scan the item, pop it into the paper bag. If you can't scan the barcode, just click on the number at the top that represents the required quantity, and the item will move down into the packaging area. Once everything is in the package, you can click "Close Package." After you've closed the package, should you need to edit it again, just click "View and Edit Package." From here, you can delete individual labels from the package, or if you have the dispensing label, just give it a scan and confirm the popup. You can then close the package. Titan will ask you if you want to reprint a package label, and you can make the appropriate decision. You can now create a new package if you want to put the other items into a separate bag. And that's that—your package is now ready to hand out or to put onto the shelf.

articles.title: Print Picking
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Click F three to print the next picking label. To print a specific label for a specific patient, select the card and select print picking. To print in bulk, click bulk. Select the ones that you want to print and click bulk process clicking. Bulk picking print will then print a label for all of the batches that you have selected, and that's all there is to it.

articles.title: Quick Packaging
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Once you have finished labeling all of your items, the easiest way to produce a bag label is to click the quick packaging button. This will give you a bag label, which you can use to seal up the bag ready for shelving or handout. Depending on the settings, Titan may prevent you from clicking quick packaging. If there are items that need to have a final check or accuracy check done, most pharmacies will turn on the need to do an accuracy check. Should the barcode be produced manually? If it's a split pack, if it's a high-risk item, if there's been a dose change, or other such things. If this happens, you'll see the "Check Needed" message appear, and you'll need to put the basket to one side for the accuracy check to be done later. And that's it. Just click "Save and Exit" to get on with something else. Or scan the next picking label to continue labeling the next batch.

articles.title: Split Packs
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
If you want to label a pack which is smaller than the prescription quantity, you only need to scan the product as normal. Titan will automatically detect that you are dispensing a smaller pack size, and the appropriate label will be printed. To manually split a pack, just click the split button and type in the label sizes that you want to produce in the correct order separated by commas. Then scan the pack as normal. Titan will print the labels in the same order that you typed them. In the next example, I have a prescription for centner, but the product comes in a pack of . I want to put all into a single white box, so to make sure I get a label for . When I scan the box, I'll first need to tell Titan what it is that I want to do. Just click the splits button and type one times . And then scan the barcode as normal. We see that a label for tablets has been produced. If you scan a pack which is larger than required, Titan will automatically split it down for you. In this case, we can see we scanned a pack, but the prescription is only for . Because the FMD barcode was scanned, the batch number and expiry date have automatically been entered, and we've checked to make sure that the item is not out of date. If the manufacturer's barcode is used, you'll need to manually enter the expiry date and batch number to make sure that they get printed on the label for the patient. In this scenario, Titan will not be able to alert you if the pack is out of date. Finally, let's look at splitting the pack down into a specific number of labels. The prescriber has written a prescription for bottles, but the pharmacy wants just three labels, one for each case of bottles in milliliters. This works out to three labels for milliliters. If we scan each bottle, we'll have to scan items and we'll get separate labels. So to address this, just click the splits button and type in three times . Now as we scan one bottle from each case, we will see that a label for milliliters is produced.

articles.title: Resource File
articles.content:
Introduction
 
This comprehensive resource pack provides all the necessary information to assist you in preparing for the launch of the Electronic Prescription Service (EPS) in your pharmacy. The tasks are categorised into different sections, and all supporting documentation, links, and contacts for assistance are included within the relevant sections.
 
It is essential to note that all tasks must be completed before implementing EPS. The responsibility lies with the pharmacy to ensure completion of all tasks within the recommended timeframe provided for each task. Once EPS is activated in the pharmacy, prescriptions can be electronically sent to this location, and the site should be capable of dispensing an EPS prescription upon receipt.
 
Enabling EPS without meeting the necessary requirements could pose a risk. Therefore, it is crucial to ensure that all tasks are completed as outlined in the documentation.
 
Glossary

Acronym /Term
Description

EPS
Electronic Prescription service

ETC
Electronic Transfer of Claims

Nomination
With the Electronic Prescription service patients can choose to nominate a pharmacy or another dispenser to receive their electronic prescriptions. Nomination must be the patient’s choice and cannot be altered without their consent.

Registration Authority / RA
A Registration Authority for NHS IT systems manages verification of user identities and provision of smart cards for all staff. 

NWSSP
NHS Wales shared services partnership

Supplier
the system supplier providing the clinical system used in the pharmacy

Token
Paper copies of electronic prescriptions are called tokens. They act as a hard copy of the details contained within an Electronic Prescription

PMR
Patient Medication Record

SOP 
Standard Operating Procedure

Spine
Spine supports IT infrastructure for health and social care including the Electronic Prescription service.

Golden Prescription
A ‘Golden Prescription’ is a dummy EPS prescription it looks like a regular prescription but will be made-up of dummy information and specific codes that when scanned and claimed, the reimbursement authority at N WSSP will recognise the message as a golden prescription and this will trigger the site to become EPS enabled and receive payment as per the drug tariff

 
Immediate action tasks for pharmacy implementation
Must be completed before going live

Action
Description / further info
Links
Completed

Complete Pharmacy profile form     

This ensures current information is held should the pharmacy need to be contacted.

Send completed form to   
 PC.EPS@Wales.nhs.uk

 

Nominate RA Agent – complete form

The Superintendent pharmacist is required to appoint an RA agent. The RA agent will be responsible for ensuring that all staff members have smart cards with the correct access privileges. Additionally, the RA agent will manage smart cards for new employees, leavers, and role changes. The ideal RA agent is a responsible individual, based on site, with good availability during the EPS implementation process.
Staff with RA roles will need to attend relevant training as advised by NWSSP.

Send completed form to NWSPCS.SmartCardProcessing@wales.nhs.uk

 

Identify RA Sponsor / Smartcard unlocker/s

NWSSP will contact  nominated RA to arrange suitable candidate.

 

Identify Privacy Officer

Each organisation is required to designate a Privacy Officer. This individual will be assigned a unique code on their smart card, granting them access to the alert viewer on the Spine system. The purpose of this access is to enable the privacy officer to monitor staff’s record access and ensure that it is done in a legitimate manner.
The Privacy Officer will be notified when the business continuity mode is used within the pharmacy.

Privacy Officer Guidance

For queries email -
NWSPCS.SmartCardProcessing@wales.nhs.uk

 

Identify EPS superuser(s)
An EPS superuser should be a team member who is capable of providing support with troubleshooting and training of new users. The ideal candidate would be someone who has good IT knowledge as well as understanding the pharmacy system, and would be available during core business hours. Possibly consider multiple staff members.
 
 

Identify person(s) responsible for maintaining EPS stock.

Choose a staff member to be responsible for ensuring stock of token paper or printer toner does not run out.
 Please note that tokens can take up to three weeks to be delivered

 
 

Order smartcard readers and token printer.
Smart card readers will be necessary to use with smart cards. Each site will be eligible to receive three free smart card readers. The complimentary readers are allocated only once for the pharmaceutical services rendered at the specific location, regardless of any future mergers or sales. In the event of relocation, there is no entitlement to request additional further free readers for the new premises.

Email pc.eps@wales.nhs.uk to request delivery of your 3 free card readers.

List of recommended printers 
Titan recommended hardware

 

Arrange  smartcards for all staff members.

EPS and other Spine applications require the use of smartcards. Staff must undergo identity verification, which is organised by the nominated RA once they have received their card. 
Please ensure all staff have their cards prior to system upgrade. 
Once obtained, the RA agent will be responsible for managing smartcards for new starters, leavers and role changes. 
Note: NWSSP will provide a template local Registration Authority for the pharmacy. 

The NWSSP will liaise with the RA to arrange.
For queries email-
NWSPCS.SmartCardProcessing@wales.nhs.uk

Please contact Titan when readers arrive for installation – you will require the reader to be functional to apply for smartcards for your staff.
 

 

Order token paper
Tokens are available in boxes of 2000 and are ordered by emailing an order form to the applicable health board. 

    
    

 

Complete IG Toolkit
Before implementing EPS, it is essential to complete the IG toolkit. Please ensure the toolkit is completed, submitted and up to date. If the individual completing the toolkit is responsible for multiple sites a parent-child relationship can be established. This setup should have already been arranged through the Welsh IG toolkit team. Once the person in charge of the admin/account for parent site submits the IG toolkit it will automatically be submitted for all the child sites as well.

Link to Welsh IG Toolkit

For enquiries email-
welshigtoolkit@wales.nhs.uk

Mark Roberts - Cert DPO, Ctr Mktr
Independent Consultant & Certified DPO
MR Associates Ltd
07545423778
Expert Consulting Services, UK | Mark Roberts Associates (mrassociates.uk)

 

Update or create SOPs to include EPS functionality
Comprehensive SOPs must be in place to support the implementation of EPS. Recommendations for SOPs to revise may include business continuity, nomination, dispensing, accuracy check, clinical check, smart cards, claiming / reimbursement, endorsement, exemption.

Please refer to attached SOPs for guidance.

View SOP templates

 

Outline Business Continuity Processes
As outlined in your SOP, ensure staff are aware of the procedure to follow if systems were to fail.
 
 

Familiarise staff with the reimbursement process of EPS scripts

Ensure all staff involved with end of month processes have read the reimbursement guidance and are aware of the circumstances where tokens will need to be submitted. 
Please note there is an updated Declaration form for sites live with EPS (WP34C) and token header for submission.

EPS reimbursement guidance (link)

 

 
Next Steps -Environment changeover
Once all of the above tasks have been completed, we will be able to proceed with upgrading your system to become EPS enabled. This process will involve downloading required software components onto your existing Titan system to be able to use EPS functions, installation of supporting hardware, such as token printers and data transfer.
The upgrade process is expected to span over 2 days. On the first day, we will install the software and hardware, conduct testing, and perform a data transfer which will normally take place after working hours. On day 2, we will verify the successful data transfer and enable all PCs. Although the process extends over 2 days, we aim to minimise disruption to your regular business operations as much as possible and will only require access to one PC at a time
 

Request ‘Golden Prescription

Once system is upgrade date is scheduled, please request a ‘Golden Prescription’ by completing ‘Golden Prescription request’ form
And return to 
https://forms.office.com/e/SEFb1RKjeN

Processing of this dummy prescription will trigger the ‘EPS-enabled’ flag to allow nominations and the drug tariff payment. This will allow the pharmacy to begin receiving EPS prescriptions.

   

 
Request communication materials 
National communication materials are available upon request to support the transition to EPS. These materials include patient facing items such as leaflets posters and videos. To order these materials, please send an email to PC.EPS@wales.nhs.uk. Please note these can only be ordered once per pharmacy.

Start collection nominations
To prepare for the launch of EPS in your pharmacy, you may wish to begin collecting nominations from patients who wish to designate you as their preferred pharmacy. This ensures that once EPS is live in your area, you are fully prepared to begin using the system immediately. Once you are EPS enabled, you will also have the ability to provide dispensing services to patients registered with EPS live surgeries. This includes offering services to holidaymakers or the ability to service care homes and establishments outside your local area, as prescriptions can be securely and efficiently transmitted without the need to visit the surgery. For more information please see attached Nomination policy. It is advisable to verify if a patient still wishes to nominate you as their preferred pharmacy if their nomination was collected well in advance of the surgery’s go-live date.

Contacts

For PMR related queries including both software and hardware
Titan PMR – 0117 325 4755

For smartcard related queries
NWSPCS.SmartCardProcessing@wales.nhs.uk

General token related queries 
nwssp-primarycareservices@wales.nhs.uk

Queries regarding token orders
NWSSP_HCSAdmin@wales.nhs.uk

Reimbursement queries 

prescribing.management@wales.nhs.uk
02921 500 444

Spine issues 

ssd.nationalservicedesk@nhs.net
0300 303 5035
Spine customer portal

articles.title: FAQs
articles.content:
What is ERD?
ERD is a:

System for managing repeat prescriptions electronically.
Prescribers can issue repeat prescriptions for up to 12 months in one go.
Patients can collect medication without needing to request a new prescription each time.
Pharmacies can dispense at set intervals, ensuring continued supply for the patient, without them having to remember to order.

Benefits of ERD
So why did ERD come about in the first place? Well although ERD can mean extra work for pharmacies, there are some definite advantages to ERD for the country as a whole.
For example, ERD will:

Reduce GP Workload – Minimising repeat prescription requests, in theory freeing up GP time for more appointments.

Is ensures continuous medication supply for patients which prevents gaps in treatment

and it

Enhances Patient Convenience –So patients don’t need to request a prescription each time they need their medication.

Receiving an ERD Prescription

Once the prescription is issued, it will appear on the Prescription Board as a nominated download, making it easy to access.
Only the first issue will be available for immediate use, while any future issues will remain stored on the Spine until they are needed.
In most cases, the pharmacist will handle the ERD setup during the clinical check to ensure everything is correctly in place.
However, some sites may choose to delay the setup process, leaving it for a later time when a dispenser or another team member can complete it.

 
Nominated Downloads

Nominated downloads can be triggered manually by clicking the Download button on the Notification Bar.
They can also happen automatically, depending on your polling settings.

ERDs will be downloaded along with nominated downloads if the Spine has made the prescription available—this process cannot be prevented.
The prescription will be considered available for download if:

The scheduled release date is today or any date before today

The Dispense Notification for the previous issue has already been sent, confirming that the last issue has been dispensed
The issue has not been returned by any pharmacy or cancelled by the prescriber.

Sometimes, after the nominated download picks up the prescription, it might not appear on the board right away and will instead show as “Awaiting Release.” This usually happens for one of the following reasons:

Auto Release was turned off, preventing the prescription from being released automatically.
The due date was manually adjusted by a TITAN user to a date later than the doctor's original scheduled date.
The item was unreleased from the board, removing it from immediate visibility.

 
The ERD Service
The ERD service runs every day to automatically download any prescriptions that are due.

The ERD service runs daily between 7 AM and 8 AM.
It automatically retrieves any prescriptions that are due but unreleased today.
It manually downloads any prescriptions where the scheduled release date id today or prior.
This process is equivalent to using the /eps command manually.

By due, we mean

If the due date was set to today by the pharmacist on the ERD flyout
or if the release date was set as today when manually unreleased

First Dispense Timing (Issue 1)
Non-controlled drugs & Schedule 5 CDs: must be dispensed within 6 months of the prescription’s start or signed date.
Schedule 4 CDs: must be dispensed within 28 days.
Subsequent Repeats: Can be dispensed up to 12 months from the appropriate date.
Controlled Drugs:

Schedules 2 & 3 – not permitted on eRD.

Schedule 4 – permitted; first issue within 28 days, repeats up to 12 months.

Schedule 5 & non-CDs – standard rules (first dispense 6 months, repeats up to 12 months).

 
Unrelease and Release
Unrelease
Unrelease is the process where prescriptions are hidden from the prescription board until the date that they are needed. This can happen manually by using the Unrelease button on the prescription flyout or automatically when a prescription is downloaded that is not due yet, based on user edited release dates.

Prescriptions may be unreleased from the board 

when in the Inbox or Checks columns

After selecting Unrelease, the user will be prompted to set a new "Issue Due Date" before proceeding

This is the date that the prescriptions will reappear on the Board

The tracker is not updated. 

The prescription is just hidden from the board.

Release

When releasing, we could be talking about an “un-unrelease” (that would otherwise happen automatically on the due date) or a download.
Prescriptions can be released from the ERD flyout, which is accessible from:

Power Search
The ERD View 
Clinical Check

They can be released individually or in bulk from the ERD view.
Prescriptions may only be released if the previous issue’s DN has been sent.

The ERD View
The ERD view is designed to be a central management screen for your ERDs, especially useful if you do not auto-download your issues. 

Filter options allow you to:

Show ERDs with a next issue date due between specific dates.
You can filter by patient to focus on individual cases.
And you can filter by tag for better organisation.

You can manage your Auto Release Settings too:

View the auto-release status of prescriptions.
Adjust auto-release settings in bulk if needed.

I saw a site in Bristol that said they always auto release everything. When I checked on the view, only about half were set to auto release. This is why the ERD clinical check is so important.

You can also access the ERD flyout.

And review progress percentage of each batch to track completion and workflow efficiency.

The PowerSearch Panel

Displays all ERDs for the selected patient in one central view.
Shows important details, including release dates, due dates, and the issue status of each prescription.
Provides quick access to the ERD flyout for further management and adjustments.

 
The Flyout
On the flyout, you can:

Release one or multiple prescription issues at once.
View the status of each issue to track its progress.
Check the NHS status to ensure the prescription is properly processed - this will need a smart card
See Release and Due dates.
Edit the Due date if adjustments are needed.
Cancel items if they are no longer required.
View the Timeline to track key actions and changes. This is the first place to go if you are experiencing any problems.

How to setup an ERD
There are three main approaches to handling ERDs, and it's essential to understand how a site wants to manage them before setting them up.
If we let them, most sites will typically choose one of a few different methods to manage their ERDs.

Automatically release prescriptions as soon as they become available.
Manually release prescriptions only when needed.
Download all prescriptions at once for bulk processing or storing in Parked until needed.

Some sites may use a combination of these approaches, depending on their workflow and preferences.
 
Configured for Automatic Release
The recommended setup for ERDs is to have them configured for Automatic Release. This ensures that prescriptions are released as soon as they become available, reducing manual effort and keeping the workflow efficient. When assisting users with setup, it’s best to encourage them to adopt this approach from the outset rather than attempting to replicate their old system within TITAN. Embracing TITAN’s optimised process from the beginning helps to avoid unnecessary complications and makes prescription management more streamlined and effective.

Buffer: 3 days will ensure that there is enough time to process the prescription before the patient comes in.
Prompt for setup: Turning this on will mean that the users is alerted to the fact that the rx is an ERD. This will stop them from forgetting to set it up if needed
Default Auto Release Date: Set this to On to make sure that the prescription comes down on the Release date automatically.
Auto Print ERD label: Turn this on to ensure an ERD label is printed with the package label. Great fo letting the patient know if they need to reorder.
Auto realign ERD dates on handout: If on, then when you have out an ERD, the next issue release date will be changed to the hand out date, plus the interval.
Prescription tags: I would always recommend setting up an ERD tag at a prescription level rather than patient level, as some patients will receive both ERD and non ERD prescriptionS.

Settings>Dispensing Settings

With Auto Release, it is crucial to hand out each issue as it becomes available. If an issue is not handed out, the next release cannot be downloaded
 
Manual release
Manual release is normally used when pharmacies prefer to wait for the patient to request the prescription before they download it.
It is also used if a pharmacy likes to manually bulk release, say the following week's prescriptions, all in one go.

Consider your “Prompt for ERD setup” setting. 

You can probably leave this off as the sire will not need to access the flyout during check

Ensure “Default auto release state for new ERS records” is OFF

This will ensure that prescriptions will not appear on the board until requested. 
Important to understand - scripts are still downloaded on the scheduled release date, but will be “unreleased” by the ERD service.

Consider modifying the ERD view date range, as this screen will be used a lot, especially if bulk releasing.

If lots or ERDs or slow connection, shorten.
If few ERDs or fast connection, you can lengthen

Download all in one go
This is often used for sites that receive 7 day trays prescriptions on ERD, as they will want to have enough scripts to fill 4 dossetts boxes at a time.
It is also used if a site prefers to manage the ERD queue from the Parked column.

Turn on the “Prompt for ERD setup” setting

Sites will need this to be able to request all issues at clinical check

Consider modifying the ERD view date range, as this screen will be used a lot, especially if bulk releasing.

If lots or ERDs or slow connection, shorten.
If few ERDs or fast connection, you can lengthen

A combination of the three
This is likely to be the most common approach.
For example, sites will often want to download all their trays in one go but leave the non-tray ERDs to be downloaded automatically one at a time.

Set your release buffer
Turn on “Prompt for ERD setup”

As users will need to do different things depending on the prescription

Consider the “Default auto release state for new ERS records”. 

Normally on, but it depends what the site want

Optimal Setup for ERD - Settings Recap
Users should aim to let TITAN manage their ERDs.
The only exception to this is 7-day trays.
 
Settings
Buffer: 3 daysPrompt for setup: OnDefault Auto Release State: OnAuto print ERD Package label: OnPrescription Tags: Make one called ERD. Toggle on Repeat Dispensing Prescription
 
Process
At clinical check, click yes to access the flyout.Confirm that you are happy with all settings.When the patient comes in, the rx should already have been downloaded and dispensed.If not, release it and dispenseTo pull down specific releases, do this from Power SearchTo pull down in bulk, do this from the ERD view

articles.title: Issues not Coming Down After an Issue is Returned
articles.content:
When you return and ERD to the spine (or any other script for that matter), the nomination is removed for all subsequent issues of that batch by the NHS Spine and this will prevent them from being downloads again via the nominated downloads check.
The fix is to re-nominate the patient
 
Patient fly out>PDS Sync>Nominate this pharmacy
 
All recently returned prescriptions will then be downloaded, including the eRDs
 
Please note that this issue is due to a NHS Spine anomaly and as such TITAN PMR are unable to prevent this from happening.

articles.title: Processing ERDs
articles.content:
Choose ‘Setup as 7 Day Tray ERD’ or ‘Setup as Monthly ERD’ to set up ERD. When you do this this ERDwill appear in the ERD screen in views. You can track the status of each issue and release issues from here. If one of these options is not available this is because of how this has been set up by the prescriber. 7 Day Tray ERD allows the dispense of all issues before they are received from the spine by creating Manual copies of future electronic issues which are then reconciled when the electronic issue is received on the day it is due, and this will send all dispense notifications to the spine. This reconciliation happens automatically in the background and requires no user input. Once set up as ERD you can’t reconcile emergency supplies against any of these issues. Monthly ERD Does not allow all issues to be dispensed all at once and does not create manual placeholder issues. It keeps track of the issues in the ERD module and releases them to the inbox 7 days before the due date for the issue, provided the previous issue has been handed out. 
Choose ‘Ignore’ to keep as standard RD. This will mean issues automatically come through on due date and can’t be released in advance. You will not be able to track the status of issues in the ERD module in views. 7 Day Tray ERD: After you finish entry/checking press save and exit, this will typically send this prescription to “parked”  (depending on tag settings and the parked toggle in the checks screen). Refresh the prescription board to see this. It will send all issues together as a batch so if there are for example 3 items on the script and 8 issues there will be 24 items to label. You can label all 8 issues at once or only 4 if you just want to issue 28 days worth for example, however the remaining issues will stay on the board in this situation. To do this release the scripts from parked and print picking labels, then label the prescription as normal. This prescription will be split into 7 day groups of tablets so you will need to scan or manually select the same amount of times as the number of issues required. Monthly ERD:By contrast these will arrive on or before the due date for the next script and the ERD module will release these automatically on the due date, but they can be released any time after arrival by going to the ERD module and pressing the "release next issue" button from the ERD flyout. After you have processed these issues you will be able to see the status in the Views>ERD screen. Filter by patient name to find your patient’s ERDs. If you can’t see the ERD, try expanding the date range under “next issue date” in the filter. Click anywhere on the ERD but the patient’s name (this always takes you to the patient flyout) to take you to the ERD flyout. Here you can see the status of each issue. If you have set up as a 7 Day Tray ERD you will see all future issues are “MDS Placeholders” and when the electronic issue has been received you will be able to see that it has been reconciled here. If you have set up as monthly ERD you can see when issues have arrived and release them to the inbox from here for processing. If it gets to the due date for the issue it will release by itself, provided the previous issue has been fully dispensed.

articles.title: Contraceptives and Antivirals (CC, FS )
articles.content:
TITAN follows the best practise guidelines for endorsing Free of Charge (FoC) medication as outlined by the NHS and the CPE. You can read about these here.
Exemptions are automatically added to your claims for prescriptions that carry the appropriate Prescriber Endorsements. 

Prescriber Endorsement

Exemption

CC

X

FS

Y

TITAN will automatically record a prescription as exempt and will not ask you if the patient pays if the following tests are all met:

The item has the appropriate prescriber endorsement applied (CC or FS).

All items on the prescription must carry the same endorsement (as per the above link)

The same logic dictates how the final fee is calculated on TITAN Mobile.
Note that the actual items on the rx are not taken into account. The decision to charge or not is based solely on the presence of the Prescriber Endorsements.
Also note that we can only automatically mark the prescription as exempt if ALL items on the prescription have a relevant prescriber endorsement. As such, either the whole prescription is exempt or it is not.
However, if only one of two items have a FoC endorsement, the BSA will still ensure you are reimbursed appropriately.
Please see the following statement from the BSA:
     "We automatically handle all FOC items regardless of the charge or exempt status inthe EPS claim." (Link: https://tinyurl.com/3v6sv3xa )
As such, you will always be paid the correct amount, regardless of the endorsement or exemption status recorded. The key thing is that you charge your patient the correct fee.

articles.title: Charges Label Printing
articles.content:
Printing Charges Label
Printing a charges label when closing a package shows what should be charged to the patient. It details any private fees, NHS charges and provides a total amount.
The label assumes the patient pays for their prescriptions. If the patient declares exemption at handout, NHS charges should be ignored.
There are four options under Settings → Dispensing Settings → Dispensing → Auto Print Charges Label:

Off (Manual Print Only)     The label can only be printed manually from the Packaging screen.
Private Only     The label prints only if there are private fees.
All     The label prints automatically if there are any NHS or private charges within the package.
All (including when no charge)     The label always prints, regardless of whether any fees are due.

Fee calculation
Private fees are calculated using your configuration in Settings → System Settings → Private Prescription Settings, based on the Drug Tariff price. Click here for more information
NHS fees are set at the current prescription charge in England and are free in Wales. In England, adjustments for items such as free contraceptives and HRT are included. Exemptions and RTEC are not applied automatically and must be confirmed at handout as normal.

articles.title: Original Pack Dispensing
articles.content:
New legislation is coming soon that will mandate original pack dispensing for valproate containing medicines.
You will also be encouraged to dispense all other items in the original pack if the prescribed quantity is plus or minus 10% or the original pack size. The aim of this is to reduce errors and to help increase pharmacy efficiency.TITAN is now able to support this process and we are fully ready to go live with the new functionality required to allow you to do this. However, we are currently waiting on the NHS to finalise the technical requirements and to approve our changes in TITAN before we can roll out.
 
You can read about the changed at the following addresses:
GPhC: https://www.pharmacyregulation.org/regulate/article/new-legislation-original-pack-dispensing
 
gov.uk: https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/original-pack-dispensing-and-supply-of-medicines-containing-sodium-valproate/original-pack-dispensing-and-supply-of-medicines-containing-sodium-valproate
  Below is a summary of what is happening:

 

Legislation Changes (Effective from 23 October 2023):

Amendments to the Human Medicines Regulations 2012.
Mandate original full pack dispensing of valproate-containing medicines by manufacturers.
Grant pharmacists flexibility (up to ±10%) for other medicines, using the original manufacturer's pack.

Objectives of Changes:

Enhance patient safety by including the patient information leaflet.
Improve pharmacy efficiency by reducing the need for repackaging.

Limitations on Dispensing Flexibility:

Does not apply to Controlled Drugs or medicines with impractical dispensing forms/containers.
Pharmacists to use professional judgment, prioritising patient's best interests, and document decisions.

Transition Period for NHS Prescriptions (England and Wales):

Application of amendments depends on NHS terms of service.

Implementation in Scotland:

Original pack dispensing flexibility implemented immediately.

Valproate-Containing Medicines (Effective from 11 October 2023):

Must always be dispensed in manufacturer's original full pack.
Ensures women receive information about risks of valproate during pregnancy.
Exceptions possible with justified risk assessment, but patient must still receive the Patient Information Leaflet.

articles.title: VOP 5 - Community MDS Dispensing
articles.content:
Introduction
Patients often request to have their medication put into Monitored Dosage Systems (MDS) rather than the Original Packs (OP). By its very nature MDS mixes multiple items into a single package making it difficult to reconcile and manage the associated prescriptions and follow the standard flow and maintain the integrity of barcoding and FMD. 
This SOP sets out the procedure to follow for managing MDS patients in the community.
Scope
Community MDS Packs, MAR chart printing
Key Steps
BEFORE YOU START
Tag Set Up

Ensure you have a Managed Patient Tag set up for this MDS service
Define the MDS service in respect of the system used and the times of the day medication is slotted

Patient Set Up

Ensure the relevant patients are linked to this Managed Patient Tag. This will also enable the view of their Repeat file
From the Repeat File of each patient, enter their current therapy including all items which go into MDS as well as those which are to be dispensed in OP.

MANAGING MDS PATIENTS
Management Screen

You can see all the MDS patients by going into the Managed Patient section. Use this screen for viewing;
The status of prescriptions available compared to the Repeat Therapy they are on.
What items need to be ordered
What MDS trays need to be dispensed

Ordering Prescriptions

Follow the usual process for ordering prescriptions

DISPENSING PROCESS
Checking Prescriptions

This is a variation of SOP 3: Clinical Checks
For Managed Patients additional checks will be shown. These alert on any variations on the incoming prescription against the Repeat File to allow an opportunity to either reject the prescription or update the patient’s file accordingly
After prescriptions have been checked all items will go into the Parked section on the Titan Kanban board

Picking Labels

This is a variation of SOP 4: Picking Stock
Go to the Parked section of the Kanban board
Select the patient you wish to pick stock for and print
A standard picking label will be produced for OP stock
Print the MDS backing sheets 

Pick the stock for OP items and MDS items

Making MDS trays

Use the MDS backing sheet to make up each MDS tray ensuring the right drug and right quantity goes into each tray
Put all the completed MDS cards and the medication used for dispensing them into a tray

Dispensing and Reconciliation

This is a variation to SOP 5: Labelling Stock
Take the basket containing the completed MDS card and any picked OP items to Titan station
Scan the Picking label to bring up the transaction
Scan the OP items to produce dispensing labels in the usual way
Scan the MDS items. A label will not be produced but the barcode will be validated and FMD verification will be carried out

When all MDS items have been scanned, a single MDS label will be produced which you must attach to the MDS card

Packaging

This is a variation to SOP 6: Final Check and Packaging
Perform any accuracy checks and then scan the OP dispensing labels and the MDS card label
Put the MDS card and the original packs into a bag
Produce the Package Label

Allocation and Handout

Complete the process of allocation and handout in the usual way

Tips and Advice

If prescription arrive late and you need to get MDS trays ready in advance, you can print MDS backing cards (Step 14 above)  from the Patient Therapy screen. This will allow you to pick the stock, make up the tray and have it ready for Dispensing and Reconciliation step above. Whilst this is perfectly acceptable, there is a risk that the therapy may change when the prescription arrives and your prepared MDS tray is incorrect.

Here is a link to a video showing the process:  
https://vimeo.com/388690572/c6c51eeba5
The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here: 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1w5HeQYoPCQGD12kjhGW35pSSpjb73xut4CnFXml_o3c/edit

Click into the power search or click F nine to search for a patient. Type in their forename, followed by the surname— the first three letters of each are usually enough to find the correct patient. Alternatively, you can search using the NHS number, and if you don't have that, just enter the date of birth. Click Enter on your keyboard to view the full patient record. To search for a patient on the prescription board, click the filters button and enter their name. Select their name from the dropdown box and click enter.

articles.title: Prescription Board
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
The prescription board is used to display all items in your pharmacy. Prescriptions will be batched together according to the patient name and will be displayed in different columns depending on where they are in the dispensing process. Batches of prescriptions are displayed in the columns in chronological order. This can also be changed to alphabetical. The prescriptions are grouped according to priority, with unallocated at the bottom, today in the middle, and waiting at the top. On each prescription card, you can see the patient name, their address, the time and date that the prescription was received, and the number of items. Patient tags are also displayed in blue, and prescription level tags are displayed in red. New prescriptions will appear in the inbox. Newly entered prescriptions by a non-pharmacist staff member would appear in the check column. Both of these two columns are used by the pharmacist to do the initial clinical check, where the prescription will be made safe to dispense and all inappropriate doses will be fixed. The parked column is used for prescriptions that you want to hold up and not dispense straight away. Typically, this will be for your MDS or dot patients or for your care homes. The picking column is where the dispenser starts the process. From this column, a picking list can be printed that will list all of the items that need to be picked for that batch of prescriptions. The label column displays all of the batches of prescriptions that need to be labeled. Batches of prescriptions in the package column still need to be put into the bag, and they may need to have accuracy checks done. The handout column is for prescriptions ready to be handed out. If you are an Eddo user, you'll see the shelf name on the card as well. The prescription board can be filtered using the filter button in the top left corner. From here, you can type in a patient's name, select them from the search results, hit enter, and that patient's prescriptions will be filtered on the prescription board. You can also make custom filters based on patient tags, when the prescription was received, or other things. Once you've created your filter, you can save it for quick access at a later date. Use the reset button to clear the filter. The prescription board can be refreshed with the refresh button or the F five button on your keyboard. Prescriptions can be moved up and down in the columns by dragging and dropping them, or by clicking the three dots and clicking center to top, center to bottom, or changing the priority altogether from today, waiting, or unallocated. Clicking on a card will open the prescription or batch fly-out. From here, you can access the dispensing screens, or you can click on the patient's name to access their records.

articles.title: Prescription Board Filters
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
The new prescription board filters help you to organize your prescriptions in a quick, easy, and intuitive way. They'll allow you to focus on what matters most to you. Simply choose what you want to see or hide what you don't. Filters let you narrow down the view by different attributes, such as patient tag, prescription tag, expiry status, arrival time, and many more things. You can also use the quick patient name filter to find a particular patient instantly. You can combine multiple filters together. For example, you may want to see any prescription for a given care home with the acute tag. Once you've built your filter, you can save it for quick access later on. So to use filters, just click the filter icon in the top corner and then pick the filter category that you want. Once you choose a filter, you can enter specific values to see or hide what it is that you are interested in. Please note that if any value is not currently shown on the board, you will not be able to filter it. So if you have nothing on the delivery shelf, you will not be able to filter out your deliveries. If you need to be even more specific or use multiple filters, you can do this using filter groups. Just click on add group in the filter menu to create them. You can choose to show tasks that meet all your filter criteria with "and" or any of them with "or". If you prefer, you can simply search for a prescription by using the patient's first or last name. This search is through all the prescriptions and batches to show you all the cards linked to the patient in question. By using filters, filter groups, or patient search, you can quickly find the prescriptions that matter to you, making your work more efficient by focusing on what's important and ignoring what's not. For more help, just click the help button to drop us a message.

articles.title: SSP
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
If the Department for Health and Social Care identifies that there is a shortage of a specific medicine or appliance, an SSP may be issued. SSPs allow you to use your professional skill and judgment to decide whether it is responsible and appropriate to substitute a patient's prescribed item for the active SSP. Patients will also need to agree to the alternative supply for that dispensing month before you can complete the handout. When doing your clinical checks, if a prescribed item is on the SSP list as published on the NHS BSA website, you will see the SSP badge next to the item during your clinical check. To set up the SSP, just click on this badge. From the screen that pops up, you'll be able to see a copy of the endorsement guidelines document for the specific SSP, which will also tell you which items may be used as substitutions, as well as offering other supporting documentation. On the right-hand side of the screen, just scroll down to the item that you want to use and enter the dose and quantity. You are also able to use multiple items to make up the required dose if needed. Once fully entered, just click OK. You will then see that the items that you've entered will show on the clinical check screen. Then you just dispense as normal. When you get to the handout stage, you'll see a pop-up informing you that an SSP has been dispensed. This pop-up is designed to remind you to check with the patient that they agree to the alternative supply being made for that dispensing month. To keep things really simple, Titan has automatically applied the required endorsements for you, so you don't need to do anything.

articles.content:

Adding a new supplier to Titan is easy. Just go to the marketplace. Click the supplier that you wish to add. Click the price button and accept the license agreement. The new app will show under the installed app section over on the right. Next, we'll need to configure the app. Click the installed app, enter your account number, and click save. You will also want to set your default supplier. This will define which supplier non-configured items are set to when they go onto the order pad. To do this, go to settings, and then into the dispensing settings tab. Then just click on the default supplier dropdown list and choose from the list of installed supplier ordering apps. And that's it.
