articles.title: Pharmacy and TITAN Terminology
articles.content:
Acronym/ Term
Meaning
Notes

ACBS
Advisory Committee on Borderline Substances

Provides guidance on the classification of medicines that may be considered borderline products, affecting their availability.

ACDA
Accuracy Checking Dispensing Assistant

An Accuracy Checking Dispensing Assistant (ACDA) is a trained pharmacy professional who verifies the accuracy of dispensed medications. They ensure that the right medicine, dosage, and instructions match the prescription.
To become an ACDA, individuals typically need to complete additional training and certification beyond standard dispensing roles. This includes passing specific courses and assessments to ensure competency in accuracy checking. ACDAs work under the supervision of a pharmacist and adhere to regulatory standards.

ACT
Accuracy Checking Technician
An Accuracy Checking Technician (ACT) is a pharmacy professional who ensures that dispensed medications are correct. They must complete specialised training and certification. ACTs work under a pharmacist’s supervision to verify the accuracy of prescriptions.

BSA
Business Services Authority
The NHS Business Services Authority (NHS BSA) manages NHS prescription services, including processing claims and payments for pharmacies.

BNF 
British National Formulary 
A reference book / website listing medicines, their uses, dosages, and side effects, widely used by healthcare professionals. TITAN uses their APIs to determine item classifications, warnings amongst other things.

 
Callendar Pack
A type of packaging where tablets are labelled with the days of the week.

 
Canny 
Where Pharmacies can request new features.titanpmr.canny.io/feature-requests 

CD
Control Drug

Classified into schedules based on their potential for misuse and medical use:

Schedule 1: No medical use (e.g. LSD).
Schedule 2: High misuse potential but medical use (e.g.,higher strength morphine).
Schedule 3: Lower misuse potential (e.g. some benzodiazepines).
Schedule 4: Part 1 (e.g. anabolic steroids), Part 2 (e.g. certain benzodiazepines).
Schedule 5: Very low misuse potential (e.g. codeine in small amounts).

Each schedule dictates how these drugs can be prescribed, stored, and handled.

CQC
Care Quality Commission
Regulates and inspects health and social care services in England to ensure they meet quality and safety standards, including care homes and surgeries.

DN
Dispense Notification
Link

DSP
Distance selling pharmacy
A distance selling pharmacy in the UK is a pharmacy that operates primarily online or via mail order rather than from a traditional physical location. Customers can order medications, over-the-counter products, and health services through the pharmacy’s website or by phone, and the products are then delivered to their address. These pharmacies must adhere to strict regulations set by the General Pharmaceutical Council (GPhC) to ensure safety, privacy, and quality of care.

EMIS
 
Provider of electronic medical records systems used by Pharmacies, GP practices and other healthcare services.ProScript: PMREMIS: Prescribing System

EPS
Electronic Prescription Service
AKA ETP (electronic transfer of prescriptions).Allows prescriptions to be sent electronically from a GP to a pharmacy. This system streamlines the process, reducing paperwork and improving efficiency. Patients can choose a pharmacy to receive their electronic prescriptions and collect their medication without needing a paper prescription.

ERD
Electronic Repeat Dispensing
A process that allows the prescriber to authorise and issue a batch of repeat prescriptions for up to 12 months with just one digital signature. 

ETC
Electronic Transfer of Claims
The Electronic Transfer of Claims (ETC) is a system that enables pharmacies to submit and process NHS prescription claims electronically. It streamlines the reimbursement process, reducing administrative tasks and ensuring quicker and more accurate claims handling.

ETP
Electronic Transfer Prescription
AKA EPS

FMD
Falsified Medicines Directive
European regulation requiring verification of the authenticity of medicines to prevent counterfeit products.No longer used in the UK, however TITAN still used the FMD QR codes for product recognition and expiry checks and batch number logging in case of recall. 

 
 Golden Prescription
A ‘Golden Prescription’ is a dummy EPS prescription it looks like a regular prescription but will be made-up of dummy information and specific codes that when scanned and claimed, the reimbursement authority at N WSSP will recognise the message as a golden prescription and this will trigger the site to become EPS enabled and receive payment as per the drug tariff

GPhC
General Pharmaceutical Council
The General Pharmaceutical Council is the body responsible for the independent regulation of the pharmacy profession within England, Scotland and Wales, responsible for the regulation of pharmacists, pharmacy technicians and pharmacy premises.

HSCN / N3
Health and Social Care Network 
N3 is the broadband network for the NHS which connects all NHS locations and over a million employees. It connects hospitals, GP surgeries, pharmacies and many other service providers to securely facilitate sharing of healthcare data including sensitive patient records.

HV
High Volume
Large TITAN sites where certain features, such as some views and the prescription board,  may have been disabled as there would be so much data returned that the screens would not be able to load. e.g. Lloyds Direct, Pill Time etc

MCS
Manufacturing Can't Supply
Production problems, shortages, or supply chain disruptions. This status may affect the availability of the medication in pharmacies or healthcare settings.

MDA
Monitored Dosage Administration
AKA "Blue scripts". Used for prescribing daily doses of monitored doses normally Methadone.

MDS
Monitored Dosage System
Usually used in care homes. AKA trays, dosettes etc. Compartmentalised trays, which are very easy to open, that have days of the week and time of the day labelled on them. Different to dossetts.

MHRA
Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency

Regulates medicines and medical devices to ensure safety and efficacy in the UK.

MUR
Medicines Use Review

A service where pharmacists holistically review a patient’s use of medication to improve adherence and outcomes. This service is now withdrawn. 

NAS
National Administrative System for Wales

An IT system used to support administrative functions within the NHS in Wales. It includes:

Patient Administration: Manages patient information and records.
Appointments: Handles scheduling and tracking.
Clinical Data: Supports various clinical and administrative processes.

NAS Wales helps streamline NHS operations and improve efficiency in patient management and care.

NCRS
National Care Records Service

Part of the NHS Portal where medical history is kept.

Personal Details: Name, date of birth.
Medical History: Illnesses, conditions, treatments.
Medication Records: Current and past prescriptions.
Allergies: Known allergies.
Test Results: Lab and diagnostic results.
Immunisations: Vaccine records.
Treatment Plans: Ongoing or planned treatments.

NICS
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
Provides evidence-based guidance and recommendations for healthcare practices and treatments.

NMS
New Medicines Services

A set of support services provided by pharmacies to help patients manage new prescriptions. They include:

Medication Reviews: Discussing how to take the new medication.
Adherence Support: Helping patients stick to their medication regimen.
Side Effects: Identifying and managing any side effects.

NMS aim to improve patient outcomes and ensure effective use of new medications.
Link

 
 Nomination
With the Electronic Prescription service patients can choose to nominate a pharmacy to receive their electronic prescriptions. Nomination must be the patient’s choice and cannot be altered without their consent.

NWSSP
NHS Wales shared services partnership

It provides various support services to NHS organizations in Wales, including:

Payroll and HR Services
Procurement and Supply Chain Management
Finance and Accounting
Legal and IT Services

NWSSP aims to streamline operations and improve efficiency across the NHS in Wales.

ODS
Organisation Data Service
(unique Identification given to pharmacy on the spine) eg.FAA000

OTC
Over The Counter
Medications and products that can be purchased without a prescription. OTC items include common treatments for minor ailments, such as pain relievers, cough and cold remedies, and antacids.

Owing
 
In a pharmacy context, "owing" typically refers to a situation where a patient or customer has an outstanding balance or a medication that has not yet been collected. For example, if a patient has partially paid for their prescription or if a part of their medication is not available immediately, it may be marked as "owing" until it is resolved.

PCN

Primary Care Network

Groups of GP practices working together to provide coordinated care to their local population.

PDS
Personal Demographic Service

The part of the Spine that holds and manages demographic information about individuals registered with the NHS. It includes:

Personal Details: Name, date of birth, address.
NHS Number: Unique identifier for accessing NHS services.
Registration Status: Information on current NHS registration.

The PDS helps ensure accurate and up-to-date records for NHS services and interactions.

PMR
Patient Medical Record
TITAN; ProScript; RxWeb; Pharmacy Manager

POD
 
TITAN uses separate PODs to separate pharmacy databases into separate areas. This process limits the potential impact of service outages, data breaches etc and provides a means of load balancing to help prevent any single server from becoming overloaded, improving overall system performance and reliability.

POM
Prescription Only Medicine
A medication that can only be obtained with a valid prescription from a healthcare professional. These medicines are regulated to ensure they are used safely and appropriately, and they often require monitoring due to their potential side effects or interactions.

PPA

Prescription Pricing Authority
Now part of NHS BSA, previously handled NHS prescription pricing and reimbursement.

PS
Power Search
The TITAN search bar. Search anything - type or scan.

RA
Registration Authority
A Registration Authority for NHS IT systems manages verification of user identities and provision of smart cards for all staff.

RD
Repeat Dispensing
AKA ERD.

RTEC
Real Time Exemption Checking
Used to verify a patient's entitlement to free NHS prescriptions at the point of dispensing. This system checks if the patient qualifies for an exemption from prescription charges, such as due to age, income, or medical conditions, instantly when the prescription is presented.

SCR
Summary Care record
Part of the NHS Portal where medical history is kept. Users can view prescribing history, vaccination history etc. Replaced with the NCRS.

SPINE
Spine

The central IT system used by the NHS in England and Wales to manage and share patient information. It stores:

Patient Records: Personal and medical details.
NHS Numbers: Unique identifiers for patients.
Prescription Information: Details of prescriptions.
Care Records: Information from various healthcare interactions.

It ensures that authorised healthcare professionals have access to up-to-date patient data, facilitating coordinated and efficient care.

SSP
Serious Shortage Protocol

A system used in the UK to manage and respond to significant shortages of specific medicines. When a serious shortage is identified, an SSP allows pharmacists to supply alternative medicines or treatments to ensure patients continue to receive essential care despite the shortage. The protocol includes guidance on:

Alternative Medicines: Approved substitutions for the unavailable drug.
Supply Arrangements: Procedures for dispensing alternatives.
Record-Keeping: Documentation requirements for the alternatives provided.

The SSP aims to minimise disruption to patient care and ensure access to necessary medications during shortages.

 
SystmOne

Electronic patient record system used by GP practices and other healthcare providers to manage patient data.

 
TITAN Mobile (was EDO)

A mobile app used for handout and retrieval. Shelves packages, sends SMS to patients, helps ID patients at hand out, captures exemptions in England, auto claims, ordering, product barcode registration and more

 
Token
Paper copies of electronic prescriptions are called tokens. They act as a hard copy of the details contained within an Electronic Prescription. Useful for giving to patients when returning an rx to the Spine so that another pharmacy can scan it into their PMR and download.

articles.title: Antivirus Compatibility with Titan
articles.content:
Having a good grasp on Information Security is essential in the modern world. A key part of this is having a robust approach to protecting your network from viruses and malware.
 
Securing your network is your responsibility and as such, we do not make any recommendations about what 3rd party apps, if any, you choose to use.
 
That said, we have tested TITAN with lots of different products, and we have found no issues when using the native Microsoft Antivirus - Windows Defender, or OpenText's Webroot.
 

Some users choose solutions from other companies, which can be a practical option in many cases. However, we’ve found that certain third-party tools may disrupt TITAN’s functionality or affect the support we can offer. Below are some of our key findings.

 

Microsoft Windows Defender
No known issues
 
Webroot
No Known Issues
 
McAfee
We have found that the McAfee antivirus program incorrectly identifies our remote access software as a virus. This means that if you choose to use McAfee, we will be unable to connect to your PC to assist with any inquiries you may have. If you prefer, you can temporarily suspend your McAfee protection to allow us to connect, but you will need to make sure that all of your staff are able to do this. 

Open your McAfee software.
On the left menu, click the My Protection tab.
Click Real-Time Scanning.
Click Turn off.
In the Turn off dialog, select when you want Real-Time Scanning to resume, then click Turn off:

 
Norton
The Norton antivirus suite includes and activates a VPN by default to hide your identity from would be trackers. Unfortunately, this also prevents TITAN from connecting to our servers. When you load TITAN, you will see the following message: "Titan has failed to start - Unable to connect to Titan cloud platform".
If you use Norton, you will need to switch this setting off before you can run TITAN.
 

 
Bitdefender
Bitdefender may actually prevent you from Installing TITAN. To turn this off, do the following:

Protection
Antivirus
Advanced
Toggle off Bitdefender Shield

articles.title: CD Register Integrations
articles.content:
OverviewTitan integrates with CD Registers to automatically record Controlled Drug (CD) dispensing events. 
When a site hands out a CD script in Titan, an event is generated and sent to the CD Register queue for that POD.
You can monitor these queues in #uptime_queues in Slack if you suspect an outage for a POD.
Each event is a payload containing the full script details, including prescription information, item label details, and dispensing data.
 Payload StructureThe payload generated by Titan includes: 

Prescription Information

Patient details
Prescriber details
Prescription date
Organisation and pharmacy identifiers 

Item Label Information

Each dispensed item contains one or more Dispense Item Labels.
Each label has a unique Dispense Item Label ID.
This ID is used by the CD Register to determine whether a record has already been created. 

Drug & Dispense Details

Drug name and DMD code
Quantity prescribed and dispensed
Unit of measure (e.g. ml, tablets)
Dosage instructions

 Key Rules for CD Register Unique Entry Check:CD Register must use the Dispense Item Label ID to decide if an entry is new.
If the ID has already been seen, disregard it (duplicate).
If the ID is new, create a register entry. 
Item Details Source:CD Register should pull drug and quantity details directly from the item payload (not from prescription text). Buffer Page:New entries first appear in the CD Register buffer.The site must review, accept, and add them into the official CD Register. Handling Methadone & Instalment ScriptsMethadone and similar instalment-based scripts work the same way, but Titan sends all label information each time.Example: 
Day 1: Site hands out 1 label with Dispense Item Label ID: a844b55b-a820-405a-8b1a-9674f4bda9f8CD Register creates a record for this ID. 

Day 2: Site hands out the second instalment. Titan sends both labels: a844b55b-a820-405a-8b1a-9674f4bda9f8f689f0b7-d8b4-463a-b8c0-9ff032ae5d7d 

IGNORE the first ID (already recorded).
ADD the second ID (new instalment) to the register. 

This ensures duplication never occurs, while all instalments are correctly logged. articles.title: Titan Speed Issues and Support Process
articles.content:
If you are experiencing speed issues with TITAN, it is really important that you report them to the Help Desk. 
 
The ticket will then be included in our monthly Help Desk report that contributes to our development team’s resource planning for the following month.
 
What do we need from you to progress this issue:
We understand that speed issues are frustrating. Unfortunately, there is no way to improve the “general speed” of the app and as such our developers need to be able to zero in on specific functions, buttons and screens to make incremental improvements. As such, it is really important that if you are experiencing speed issues, you are able to give us examples of specific problems. If possible, sending us a video of the issue is best. You can do this with screen capture software such as ShareX (free download here) or you can make a recording on your phone.What can we do for you now to improve things from our end?
We are able to give your systems a reboot which will most likely speed things up on a short-term basis. If we do this, you will be unable to use TITAN for about 30 seconds while the system comes back online. Please let us know if and when you would like us to do this.
 
What can you do to improve things?
PC

Close and open TITAN. This will clear down any excess memory being used and will normally make things a little faster.
Ensure that only required applications are being used. Having multiple apps open on your PC (including multiple browser tabs) can slow things down considerably.
Ensure that large jobs such as bulk claiming and bulk handout are not done during busy periods. These can cause excess load on infrastructure, leading to slow speeds while the job executes.
Check that your PC is not running any large jobs automatically, such as virus scans during busy periods.

Network

Ensure you have a cabled connection to your PC. Wi-Fi will limit the amount of speed that you are able to get.
Reset your router: This will often speed your connection up if your internet is running slowly (if this is the case, this will have a big effect on TITAN speeds). Unplug your router for 10 seconds, then plug it back in again. Bear in mind that this could cause its own problems if you have any special settings on your router. Only do this if you are confident that it will be OK.
Prevent any unwanted apps starting on your PC at start-up that may be slowing things down. Do a Windows search for “Start-up apps” and disable anything that is not needed. This will normally improve PC boot up times and often performance, as it will prevent unnecessary apps running in the background.

What happens after you raise a ticket?
If you phoned us, we will try to resolve any PC related issues that may help and also offer the server restart if we think this will help. If you messaged us, we will try to contact you via your original contact method, be it email, WhatsApp or quick chat.
 
If you raise a non phone call ticket, then after each response, we will keep the ticket open until we hear back from you. If we do not hear from you after 5 working days it will be closed. 
 
If there are particular screens that are running slowly, and you provided supporting videos, your videos will help us help diagnose and fix the issues. The ticket will be classified accordingly, which will help out senior team to understand the scale of the problem.
 
Once specific technical issues are identified, fixes will be written up and scheduled for development. Once coded, the fix will go through testing and will then go out to our Pioneer pharmacies for User Acceptance Testing. The fixes will then be released to our early release pharmacies and then the general release ones.
 
The development and release process can take some time as it is vital that new issues are not introduced into the population.
 
Please understand that we are now looking at speed issues with the utmost priority but that addressing them is a technical challenge that will take us a little time to resolve.

articles.title: Understanding Bulk Claims and Why They Should Be Run Out of Hours
articles.content:
Overview When processing NHS claims in Titan, we recommend running large bulk claims outside of working hours. This guide explains why, and what changes are coming to make this smoother in the future. How the NHS EPS Claim Process Works The NHS Electronic Prescription Service (EPS) handles claims in two stages: 
Sending ClaimsWhen Titan sends claims to the NHS, it does so quickly and efficiently. Even large batches (for example, 1,000 items) are sent without any delay or slowdown. 
Receiving ConfirmationsAfter claims are sent, the NHS sends back a separate confirmation message for each claim.So, if you send 1,000 claims, Titan will suddenly receive 1,000 individual confirmation messages in a short period of time.
 Why This Can Affect Performance This rapid influx of confirmation messages can temporarily increase system activity in Titan.While these confirmations are processed in the background, Titan is also maintaining normal day-to-day operations in your pharmacy, such as dispensing, labelling, and managing prescriptions. Running large bulk claims during working hours can therefore cause the system to slow down for a short period while these confirmations are handled. Best Practice Recommendation To avoid any potential slowdown for your staff, we recommend running large bulk claims out of hours. For example, after the pharmacy has closed or during quieter periods.This ensures that Titan can process all incoming confirmations smoothly without affecting your team’s workflow. What’s Changing in the Future The NHS is moving to a new claim handling process.Instead of sending a claim and waiting for a separate confirmation later, each claim will receive an instant response at the time it’s sent. This means: 
No backlog or flood of follow-up messages
No additional strain on Titan
Faster and more efficient claim processing overall
 Titan is already part of the NHS onboarding programme for this new system, which is expected to roll out next year once approved. Summary Running bulk claims out of hours is purely a performance safeguard. It ensures your day-to-day operations stay smooth while Titan processes a high volume of confirmations in the background. The good news: this limitation is temporary, and the upcoming NHS claim changes will remove the need for out-of-hours bulk claiming altogether.

articles.title: Writing Effective Knowledge Chat Messages
articles.content:
Overview Clear, structured knowledge messages help your colleagues understand the issue quickly and provide accurate support.  Use the following format every time you post in #titan_knowledge or your squad group chat. 1. Friendly GreetingNot required, but it makes the chat more approachable.Example:"Hi Team! Hope you’re all well." 2. Introduce the Site or UserAlways state who you are talking about. 
Include site name and ODS code.
Include the user's name if relevant. 
Example:"A user at [Site Name] – [ODS Code] has contacted us…" 3. Provide the BackstorySummarise what happened before the issue occurred. 
Keep it short and factual.
Include any relevant history. 
Example:"The user previously used another version of a system before switching to Titan." 4. Explain the Current SituationDescribe what is happening right now. 
Explain what the user is seeing.
Include any troubleshooting already done. 
Example:"They have received an unexpected charge and believe it may be related to a recent integration setup." 5. Add ContextInclude anything that helps others understand the scenario. 
Policies
Recent changes
Processes
Clarifications you’re unsure about 
Example:"My understanding is that this type of setup should not generate additional costs for the customer." 6. Ask Clear QuestionsMake it obvious what help you need. 
Write questions clearly.
Bullet points are ideal. 
Example: 
Can someone confirm the correct process?
Do we need to take any further action?
 7. Friendly Sign-OffNot required, but it makes the chat more approachable.Example:"Many thanks in advance all!" ✨ Generic Example TemplateHi Team!I’ve had [Site Name] – [ODS Code] get in touch regarding [brief description of issue].Backstory:[Summary of events before the issue]Current Situation:
[What the user is currently seeing]
[Troubleshooting already completed]
Context:[Any additional helpful detail]Questions:
[What do you need to know?]
[List questions separately]
Many thanks! Tips for Clear Messaging 
Keep paragraphs short (1–2 lines).
Use bullet points for clarity.
Avoid long blocks of text.
Stick to facts; avoid assumptions.
Keep formatting consistent so messages are easy to skim.

articles.title: What is a Dispense Notification (DN)?
articles.content:
What is a Dispense Notification?

A Dispense Notification (DN) is a special message that TITAN sends to the prescription tracker.
It is the message that updates the prescription tracker to show that the prescription has been "dispensed"
It is also the message that updates the prescription tracker to show that the items have been "not dispensed (ND'ed)" 

 
Why are Dispense Notifications sent?

To tell the Spine and other Portal users that the prescription has been dispensed
To permit subsequent eRD prescriptions to be downloaded when needed 
To permit you to claim for the the prescription

 
When is a Dispense Notification sent?
For a DN to be sent, a Smart Card must first be inserted and authenticated.
If this is not done, that DN will be queued until the a Smart Card is authenticated, at which point the queue will start to be processed.
Assuming the Card is authenticated, the following triggers will send a DN:

When you hand out an item/package an item (depending on your setting in Dispensing Settings>Miscellaneous>Trigger DN when closing package)
When you mark an item as Not Dispensed
When downloading multiple eRD prescription issues at the same time

articles.title: Requirements
articles.content:
This guide outlines the recommended PC specifications, hardware, and configuration settings to ensure Titan runs smoothly. Following these guidelines will help avoid performance issues and ensure your setup is supported by Titan’s support team.
 
Computer Requirements

Processor: Intel i5 or Ryzen 5 (or above)

6 cores or more recommended

Architecture: 64-bit only (NOT ARM64) – Smartcard readers will not work on ARM64

Windows Version: Windows 11 Pro only

RAM: 16GB minimum (more preferred)

Internet Speed: Minimum 70 Mbps download / 17 Mbps upload

Updates: Keep Windows fully up to date (minimum build 1903)

Hardware Compatibility: Only use tested hardware listed below. Non-listed items may not work and will not be supported.

Most recommended items are available via Amazon, but other suppliers may also stock them.

 
PC Configuration Recommendations
1. Power Options

Go to Control Panel → Power Options.

Select High (or Best) Performance instead of Balanced.

Prevents throttling of CPU, memory, and graphics, improving Titan load times by up to 100%.

2. Keep Windows Updated

Always install updates for performance and security.

Schedule updates outside core operational hours to avoid disruption.

3. Wired Network Connectivity

Titan works on Wi-Fi, but a wired LAN connection ensures stable performance.

Avoid variable connection speeds or intermittent dropouts.

4. Avoid Intensive Processes During Core Hours

Schedule anti-virus scans, Windows updates, video streaming, or bulk claim activity outside operational hours.

For bulk claims, run at end of day.

Set anti-virus scans to overnight if possible.

🔗 See Optimising Performance for Titan – Titan PMR for detailed instructions.

articles.title: Brother A4 & Token Printer Installation
articles.content:
A4 & Token Set Up  Ensure the printer is on our Supported Printers list: Access the Support Website 
Go to the manufacturers website (eg setup.brother.com)
Search for your printer model (e.g. HL-L5100DN). 
Download the Full Driver & Software package for your operating system.
 Run the Installer and Connect the Printer 
Open the downloaded installer.

Follow the on‑screen instructions to:

Choose connection type (USB, Ethernet or Wi‑Fi).
Connect the printer when prompted.

Once installed, open the printer properties and name the printer (e.g. Brother HL-L5100DN series A4).
 Setting Up the A4/Token Printing  In order to set up the A4 printing, follow these steps:  
In printer properties, go to the 'Advanced' tab, and ensure the Driver is correct.
Click on 'Printing Defaults'.
Select the A4 paper size.
On the same tab, under 'Paper Source', set the 'First Page' and 'Other Pages' to the relevant A4 tray.
Hit 'Apply' then 'OK'. 
Open the 'Ports' tab and take note of the port used for this printer. In order to set up the Token printer, follow these steps:  
Click 'Add device' and then select 'Add a new device manually'.
Select 'Add a local printer or network printer with manual settings' and click 'Next'.
Select 'Use an existing port', and select the port you noted down earlier. Hit 'Next'.
Find the relevant driver from the list, select it and hit 'Next'.
Select 'Use the driver that is currently installed' and hit 'Next'.
Name the printer (e.g. 'Brother HL-L5100DN series Token')
 Setting up the Token Functionality  In order to set up the Token printing and set the trays, follow these steps:  
Find the new printer and hit 'Printer properties'.
Go to the 'Device Settings' tab. Ensure all trays are listed. If not, add the tray as required.
Navigate to the 'Advanced' tab, then hit 'Printing Defaults'.
From the drop down under 'Paper size' hit 'User Defined'.

articles.title: Change Titan Environment Using a Licence
articles.content:
Overview Titan licences are issued per terminal per site.For pharmacy owners or users who manage more than one site, licences can be swapped to allow access to different Titan environments. Each licence is provided as a QR-code-style file, which can be dragged and dropped onto the Titan login screen to change the active environment. Correctly changing the environment is essential to ensure you are accessing the correct site and to avoid system issues. When You Would Use This You would need to change your Titan environment if you: 
Manage or own multiple pharmacy sites
Have more than one Titan licence
Need to switch between different site environments on the same terminal
 Steps to Change Titan Environment 1. Locate Your Licence File Find the licence file for the site you wish to access. This will usually appear as a QR-code-style image file provided by Titan. It is usually saved on your desktop or C:Drive>Users>Public>TitanLicences 2. Open the Titan Login Screen Ensure Titan is open and you are on the login screen (not logged in).  3. Drag & Drop the Licence Drag the licence file and drop it directly onto the Titan login screen. 4. Confirm the Environment Has Changed Wait for the login screen to update. You should see: 
The pharmacy name change
The ODS code change
A different list of users
   ⚠️ If these details do not change, the licence has not applied correctly. 5. Close Titan Completely Once the environment has updated: 
Close Titan fully
Do not log in yet
  This step is vital. 6. Reopen Titan Reopen Titan and only then proceed to log in as normal. This ensures the new environment loads correctly and prevents: 
Database glitches
Site crossover issues
Login or data sync bugs
 Important Notes 
Always close and reopen Titan after applying a licence
Skipping this step can cause system instability and incorrect site data
Only use licences provided for your sites
Licences are terminal-specific and site-specific
 Common Issues The site hasn’t changed after applying the licence 
Ensure you are dropping the licence onto the login screen
Try closing Titan and repeating the process
Confirm you are using the correct licence file
Ensure the VPN is connected if you use one
 I forgot to restart Titan 
Close Titan immediately
Reopen and log in again before continuing any work
If any changes were made, ensure that these have not been wiped

Sometimes, tokens may print in the wrong orientation. For example, if the paper only loads into the tray one way, you might need the token to appear in portrait rather than landscape.
 
Important to Know
 
Titan does not currently support flipping token printouts between landscape and portrait directly.
To change the orientation, you’ll need to adjust the printer setup instead.
 
Rotate the Paper in the Printer
 
If the tokens are coming out the wrong way around, the simplest solution is to rotate the paper inside the printer tray.
 
If One PC Prints Differently to Others
 
If you notice that one PC is printing tokens in a different orientation compared to others:

Uninstall the printer from that PC.

Reboot the PC.

Re-install the printer.

Reconfigure the printer settings for Titan.

 
Tips
 

Always check whether the issue is with all PCs or just one. This will save time before reinstalling.

If reinstalling the printer doesn’t resolve the issue, double-check the printer’s paper tray setup.

articles.title: Factory Reset a Zebra ZD420 Printer
articles.content:
If your Zebra ZD420 printer isn’t working as expected, a factory reset may resolve the issue. Follow the steps below carefully.
 
 What You’ll Need

A paper clip (or a similar thin, sturdy tool)- this will be used to press the reset button.

 
Power Cycle with Button Combination
 

Turn the printer OFF.

Press and hold the Pause and Feed buttons.

While holding both buttons, turn the printer back ON.

Continue holding until only the Status light (a square with a diamond, above the Pause button) is green.

Release the buttons.

 
Locate the Reset Button
 

Turn the printer over.

On the underside, look for a groove/channel in the bottom plate with a small hole. This is the reset button.

 
Perform the Reset
 

Insert the paper clip into the hole and press the reset button.

⚠️ Hold it for no longer than 5 seconds.

The printer will reset and feed out some labels automatically.

 
Confirm the Reset
 

The indicator light should remain green.

Test by printing from Titan to confirm the reset was successful.

articles.title: Fully Amend a Claimed Prescription
articles.content:
Overview "Fully Amend" is NHS Digital terminology for the process of partially 'resetting' a prescription that has already been claimed. After the prescription has been Amended, it will show on the prescription board in the Labelling column. The original claim will still exist, but will be updated when you resubmit the claim for the second time. Amended prescriptions may not be returned. Claims never actually get "withdrawn" - they will still exist on the Spine after you click Fully Amend, but will be superseded by your secondary claim.Once amended, you can redo the dispensing process, allowing you to alter what you did last time. On handout/Packaging, an Update DN will be sent to confirm what was done. When you send the second claim, this will reflect these actions.Note that if you just want to change the exemption or endorsement in the same cycle that the claim was sent, you can do this in the Claimed tab of the Claims screen and then click Save. In this scenario, the below process is not needed. Steps: 
Ensure you have logged into your Smart Card

Go to the Claims screen
Click the Claimed tab

Search for the prescriptions using the column filters

Select the prescription you want to amend
Click Fully Amend

  Tips:If you have handed out the prescription but not yet claimed it, you will need to Withdraw the prescription.

articles.title: Install and Configure Datalogic Scanners for Titan
articles.content:
If a site uses DATALOGIC scanners, the setup/reconfigure process is a little different to the standard Zebra/Symbol scanner setup.
 
When troubleshooting a Datalogic scanner please use the following steps.
 
Step by Step Process:
 

Unplug all scanner hardware (think they only have the Datalogic there)
Uninstall ALL scanner software on the PC (Zebra, Honeywell, Symbol, Datalogic etc...)
Restart PC.

 
Scan barcode 1 - Reset defaults
 

 
Scan barcode 2 - USB-COM (OPOS)
 

 
Copy over zipped folder '610005422'
 
(NOTE: All suppport team members should have this file, if you do not, please reach out to myself or Raf and we will email it over to you)
 

Unzip somewhere and run Setup as Admin

articles.title: Optimise PC Performance for TITAN
articles.content:
Downloadable Link

 

Optimising Performance for TITAN
For the best experience, follow these guidelines:
1. Set Power Plan to "Best Performance"

Go to Settings > System > Power & Sleep
Click Additional power settings
Select High Performance or Best Performance

2. Keep Windows Updated

Open Settings > Update & Security
Click Check for updates and install any available updates (do this out of hours)

3. Keep TITAN Updated

Always install updates when prompted
To manually check for updates, go to Settings > System Settings > Check for New Install Package

4. Use a Wired Internet Connection

Wi-Fi is slower and less reliable than a wired (Ethernet) connection. Using a cable ensures a more stable connection for TITAN

5. Use an HSCN Connection When Possible

While TITAN provides a secure VPN, an HSCN connection is recommended for better reliability and security

6. Avoid Intensive Processes During Trading Hours

Tasks like virus scans, updates, or video streaming can slow down your connection

7. Schedule Bulk Processes Wisely

Bulk claims and large bulk handouts can slow TITAN down—run them outside peak hours when possible

 
Additional Tips for Keeping Your PC Running Fast
1. Restart Your Computer Regularly

Restarting clears temporary files and frees up system resources.

2. Close Unnecessary Programs

Running too many applications in the background can slow performance—close unused programs and browser tabs.

3. Manage Startup Programs

Disable unnecessary apps from launching at startup:

Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager
Go to the Startup tab
Disable programs that you don’t need on startup (if you aren't sure, leave it running!)

4. Keep Storage Space Free

A nearly full hard drive can slow your PC—delete unnecessary files and use cloud storage when possible.

5. Run Disk Cleanup & Defragmentation

Open Disk Cleanup (Windows key + type "Disk Cleanup") to remove temporary files.

If using an HDD, run Defragment and Optimise Drives:

Open File Explorer > Right-click the drive > Properties
Go to the Tools tab > Click Optimise

6. Run TRIM for SSDs & Enable Automatic Optimisation
TRIM helps keep your SSD running efficiently by clearing unused data blocks.

To manually run TRIM:

Open File Explorer, right-click on your SSD (e.g., C:), and select Properties.
Go to the Tools tab and click Optimise.
Select your SSD and click Optimise to run TRIM.

To enable automatic TRIM (Scheduled Optimisation):

In the Optimise Drives window, click Change settings.
Ensure Run on a schedule is checked.
Set the frequency to Weekly (recommended).
Check Increase task priority if three consecutive scheduled runs are missed to ensure TRIM runs regularly.

7. Scan for Malware & Viruses

Run regular scans using Windows Defender or trusted antivirus software.

8. Adjust Visual Effects for Performance

Open Settings > System > Advanced system settings > Performance Settings > Select Adjust for best performance.

By following these steps, you can keep your PC running efficiently and ensure TITAN operates at peak performance.

articles.title: Reinstall Desktop Services
articles.content:
Sometimes sites will report their scanners or printers not working, this will usually be represented by the Titan Peripheral Service (TPS) not being connected.
We should start any diagnostic by confirming that the client PC has been updated to the latest version of TITAN. You can check this in the settings window:

You can check TPS by logging in to TITAN and pressing F9 to go to the power search window, in here you will see some indicator lights, the one we are interested in says 'Printing' if it is Red - this is what's causing the issue.

To resolve this, we have built a fix into TITAN itself, which you or the user can do to resolve the issue.
There are specific steps to this process to be followed in order for the fix to take effect...

Reinstalling Desktop Services:

Log in to TITAN 
Go to Settings
Go to System Info
You will see the following screen:

Press the button that says 'Reinstall Desktop Services'
You will then see a number of windows appear running script (DOS prompt windows)
Let these windows run until you are left with two windows open, the last line of text on them should say 'Close console to Exit' - at this point, close both windows

Now logout of TITAN and close the app completely (do not just 'X' the window)
It is important that the user session is logged out fully, then close TITAN, reopen the app and log back in
It this point the icons should now be all Green - if they are not simply logout and back in again
This will resolve most, if not all issues

If this does not fix the issue you can follow extra diagnostics here:
https://titanhelp.zendesk.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4405984019346-Zebra-Scanner-Troubleshooting-Steps
https://titanhelp.zendesk.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4403680605458-Delete-Titan-Peripheral-Service-Fix

articles.title: Resolve VPN Disconnection Issues on TITAN Mobile
articles.content:
If your TITAN Mobile device keeps dropping its VPN connection, the most likely cause is brief interruptions in your Wi-Fi connection. Even a short drop in Wi-Fi can disconnect the VPN — and it often doesn’t reconnect automatically.
Below is a list of practical steps you can try to improve Wi-Fi stability and help your VPN stay connected:
1. Turn Off Battery Optimisation for the VPN App
Battery optimisation settings can restrict background activity for apps, including your VPN, which may cause it to disconnect.
To disable battery optimisation for a specific app:

Open the Settings app.
Scroll down and tap Battery (or it may be called Battery & performance).
Tap Battery optimisation – you may need to tap the three-dot menu or More settings first.
Tap the dropdown at the top and select All apps.
Find the VPN app in the list and tap it.
Select Don’t optimise, then confirm.

2. Try Setting Your Router to 2.4GHz Only
Advantages of 2.4GHz:

Better range and wall penetration.
Ideal for larger homes or areas with thick walls where signal might drop.

This can be helpful if your device keeps losing signal due to range issues.
3. Try Setting Your Router to 5GHz Only
Advantages of 5GHz:

Faster speeds.
Less interference from other devices.

This setting might be more effective if speed or congestion is the issue.

⚠️ Yes, these two tips are technically contradictory — but either could help, depending on your environment. It’s worth testing both.

4. Allow Unrestricted Data Usage for the VPN App
This ensures your VPN isn’t limited by data-saving settings.
Steps:

Open the Settings app.
Tap Network & Internet (or just Connections).
Tap Data Saver.
Ensure Data Saver is switched on (this reveals the exception list).
Tap Unrestricted data access.
Find the VPN app in the list and toggle it on.

5. Change Your Wi-Fi Password
If there are too many devices on your network — or if unauthorised users are connected — this can reduce stability.

Ask yourself: Are staff watching Netflix during lunch? Do the neighbours have your password?

Changing your password limits access to essential users only.

6. Check if Your Wi-Fi Channel Is Too Crowded
Nearby networks may be using the same channel as yours, causing interference.
On Android:

Download a free Wi-Fi analyser app, such as:

WiFi Analyzer (by farproc)
NetSpot

WiFiman (by Ubiquiti)

Open the app and scan your area.
Look for overlapping channels – especially on 2.4GHz (commonly 1, 6, and 11).
Switch your router to a less crowded channel if necessary.

7. Optimise Your Router Placement
The physical location of your router can greatly affect signal strength.
Best practices:

Place it centrally in your home or workplace.
Keep it off the floor.
Avoid thick walls, cupboards, corners, and metal objects.
Keep it away from microwaves and cordless phones.

8. Watch Out for Interference
Some household items can interfere with your Wi-Fi:

Microwaves: Use the 2.4GHz band and can disrupt nearby signals. Avoid placing your router near the kitchen.

Bluetooth Devices: Speakers, controllers, keyboards, etc., also use 2.4GHz and can cause interference if heavily used.

Radios: Older or industrial models can occasionally emit interference.

Need More Help?
If you’ve tried these tips and are still experiencing issues, please contact the Help Desk for further assistance.

articles.title: Return an ERD prescription
articles.content:
The NHS Spine will not allow you to download a Batch Prescription issue if the Dispense Notification (DN) for the preceding issue has not yet been sent.
 
Furthermore, the NHS Spine does not allow you to return an ERD prescription if the DN has already been sent, even after withdrawal (as such, the TITAN Helpdesk is unfortunately unable to help with this).
If you want to download multiple ERDs at the same time, TITAN has to cycle through the batch one issue at a time. It will send the DN for issue 1, then download issue 2, then it will send the DN for issue 2 and download issue 3 and so on.
You will need to make sure that your Smart Card is authenticated before you can download any issues, as interaction with the Spine is required.
 
As you cannot return prescriptions if the DN has already been sent , you may find that you are unable to return ERDs to the Spine in certain scenarios.
 
Scenario 1You download issues 1 of 4 only of a 28 day ERD prescription. You have done the clinical check and labelled the items without downloading any more, then you decide that you want to return the prescription. This is fine as no DN is sent.
 
Scenario 2
You download issues 1 and 2 of a batch of 4 prescriptions. As the DNs are auto sent as part of the bulk download process, you are no longer able to return issue 1 or 2.
Scenario 3You download issue 1 of 4 of a 28 day ERD prescription. From the clinical check screen, you click the pencil icon, select issues 2, 3 and 4 and click Release Issues. This automatically sends the DNs for issues 1, 2, 3 and 4 and downloads 2, 3 and 4.
It is no longer possible to return issues 1, 2, 3 or 4 as the DNs have been sent.
 

 Tips: 

If you need to send an ERD prescription to a different pharmacy after handing out, as this is not possible, you may need to contact the prescriber to arrange for a new prescription to be written.

When you return a prescription, the nomination is removed for that prescription (not the patient) by The Spine to prevent it coming down with the next nominated download. With ERD, the nomination is returned from the whole batch, so this will prevent future issue from being automatically released. To work around this, re-nominate the patient. More info available here

This helps pharmacies communicate efficiently and ensure messages are only sent to relevant patients. This guide uses patients aged 75 and over as an example, but the same process can be applied to any campaign criteria available within Managed Patients. Campaigns can be used for: 
Health awareness or eligibility reminders
Service updates or pharmacy communications
Targeted messaging for specific patient groups
 Messages are sent only to the patients selected by you, giving you control over who receives the campaign. What this guide covers This helpfile explains how to: 
Filter active patients using age-based criteria
Select all patients returned by the filter
Create and send a campaign message to the selected patients
 Before you start Before creating a campaign, ensure that: 
The correct filters are applied to avoid messaging unintended patients
We strongly recommend you are aware of any character limits and billing implications
You can read about the character limits and billing information here before you get started
 Example: Creating a Campaign for Patients Aged 75 and Over This example demonstrates how to create a campaign targeting patients aged 75 and over: 
Click Managed Patients.
Select the Active Patients tab.
In the Age column, click the Filter icon.
Set the criteria to “is greater than or equal to 75”.
Click Apply.
Select all filtered patients by ticking the checkbox next to Patient.
Click Campaign.
Enter your campaign message.
Click Next, then Submit to send the campaign.
  Tips

Use {patientName} to automatically insert the patient’s name into the message.
For more information on supported message syntax, click here.

articles.content:
How to use OPD

Ensure OPD is turned on in Settings>Dispensing.
When dispensing, scan the pack as normal.
If the pack quantity scanned is plus or minus 10% of the prescription quantity, a label will be printed for the pack size, as opposed to the prescribed quantity.

An "OP" badge will display on the screen to confirm this:

NB: There is no clinical or final check required for OPD.
Exclusions
OPD applies to all EPS prescriptions, except:

Schedule 1–4 Controlled Drugs (CDs).
Sodium Valproate-containing medications (unless a risk assessment allows otherwise).
Unlicensed medications, special containers, products under Serious Shortage Protocol (SSP), PGDs, appliances, and sub-packs.
Patients with a Patient Tag set to exclude OPD.
 

Items where "Exclude from OPD has" been set in Patient Therapy.

Full walkthrough:Original Pack Dispensing (OPD)
 
Important Note
Although regulations state that OPD should not be used for SSP items, TITAN will allow the dispensing of +/- 10% for SSPs. This will be patched in an upcoming release.

articles.title: Use Swagger to Test Validation Errors for API Integrations
articles.content:
This guide explains how to use Swagger to test API keys and validate error responses when integrating with third-party systems like CD Smart and Camascope. Accessing Swagger
You will be provided with a Swagger URL.

Note: The port number in the URL is crucial – it must be correct to access the environment successfully.
Ensure that your IP address is whitelisted against the specific port number.This mirrors the same method third parties use to access the system.

 Authentication StepsClick on /api/Authentication.

Click "Try it out"..
Replace the text “string” with the actual API key (keep the ““).
Click Execute. Understanding Responses

200 – Success

400 – Call issue (e.g. validation error, incorrect data, missing info)

500 – Server-side error
After executing the call:
The Response Header will provide details on what went wrong.
You will find an Access Token in the response header if the call is successful.
 Authorising with the Access TokenClick the "Authorise" button in the Swagger interface.Enter: Bearer*space*access token(Replace access token with the token from the response header.)
Click Authorise to save the token for further calls.  Testing Events (e.g. message ID events)
Navigate to the /api/Events/{eventmessageid} section in Swagger.
Click "Try it out".
Enter a valid Event ID (this can be obtained from the ‘Events’ section in TC).Click Execute.Look for a 200 status code indicating success.

articles.title: Use the Print Token Override Tag Setting
articles.content:
The “Print Token Override” setting in tags lets you override the global setting for token printing:
 
Global setting location: Settings → Dispensing Settings → Miscellaneous → Avoid token printing when packaging
 
How It Works
 

Global setting ON (avoid token printing)

If you usually avoid printing tokens but want to print tokens for a specific patient or home, assign them a tag with Print Token Override on and set it to “Print tokens”.

This will prompt the system to print tokens only for patients with that tag.

Global setting OFF (tokens print by default)

If tokens normally print, but a patient or care home doesn’t want them, assign a tag and set it to “Do not print tokens”.

If you normally print tokens but have a care home or patient who specifically requires tokens, you can use the same tag and set it to “Print Tokens” to ensure they receive them consistently.

 
The override tag always takes priority over the global setting, making it a flexible way to manage token printing for individual patients or care homes.
 

 

 Tips: 
Remember that Titan will not actually auto print your tokens. It will only ask you if you want them to be printed in the following scenarios:

There are items on the repeat side
There is a CD on the prescription
The patient has not had an RTEC exemption found
The patient is age exempt

articles.title: Video
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
What we have here is, uh, the prescription board of Titan. Now this shows us a flattened out view of absolutely everything that's going on in the pharmacy. So the plan here is to really break down the workflow into the different key areas. So I can see, for example, I've got the inbox where my prescriptions first arrive into Titan. These could be, um, EPS downloaded prescriptions. They could be manually entered prescriptions, whatever they are, it doesn't really matter to the user. They will appear in this first column here, and that's for the pharmacist to deal with the checks and the entry. After that point, the pharmacist is free to continue with the rest of their work. So they can now, instead of having to be stuck doing the more menial and physical sides of the dispensing process, uh, using the system that we have, uh, we're able to then free them up to be able to give, um, the services to the patients. So the first thing I'll show you is what happens when we click into a prescription and start dealing with the clinical checks. So I'll click into this first one, uh, Leon Felix. Um, and first thing we see is we've got an image of the prescription that has been generated, uh, based on, in this case, the ETP message. So we'll click process and straight away. Um, again, we've got this image. Uh, we'll see also that in this case, this patient has got four prescriptions in total. They've been grouped together, meaning that the user is able to look at all different prescriptions for the same patient, um, at the same time. Um, and we can also now just see this basic information here. So in this case, this patient is already in the system, uh, and we can see that we have a full match here for this patient. Um, now my main job here as a pharmacist is just to make all of these red dots go green. So in this case, I can see there's something to do for this patient. Um, and at the prescription level, I can see that there's some more information on side two of the prescription. So all I need to do, if I click on view, um, it's now going to automatically go over to side two of the prescription. And I can see that in this case I've got some information from the GP saying to the patient, please call the practice. And now, um, as a pharmacist, I can now pass that onto the GP. Um, and at this point I can go in and just add another comment if I wanted to here, um, I can type a message in and then that will then show at handout as well. Okay. So the next step now, now that I've got the prescription level checks done, um, I can see that's now gone green to tell me I can move down. And now I'm looking at the clinical checks themselves, the interactions. This is where I would be able to see all the BNF-style interactions saying that this item perhaps interacts with another item on this prescription or another item in the patient's dispensing history. Um, we also put in our own checks as well as all the normal BNF-style checks that you get all your interactions. Uh, we've also got other checks that over the years we found can be very useful. So in this case, I can see we've got a seven-day check, which means that this exact item has been prescribed for this patient within the last seven days. So potentially there could be a prescribing error there as well. So it gives the pharmacist a chance to step in there. Uh, so all I need to do is accept that check and it's now gone green. And also here we've got, um, again, the seven-day check and also I've got another additional information here as well. So I can see in this case, levothyroxine, we've got the main dose of take one a day and additional information from the GP of take with water. articles.title: "Copy Exemption" Button Not Consistently Applying Exemptions
articles.content:
IssueExemptions are not reliably copied when using the Copy Exemption button. The system shows a "Copied exemptions" toast, but the exemptions do not apply, and the prescriptions do not move to the correct exemption section.
 
ImpactUsers are unable to copy medical exemptions as expected. This leads to exemptions having to be manually added per prescription.
 
WorkaroundInstead of using the Copy Exemption button, users can manually add exemptions to the prescriptions.

articles.title: "Manual Order Only" Items Added Automatically To Order Pad When "Auto-order On Wales Barcode Scan Is On"
articles.content: IssueItems set to "manual order only" are added automatically to the order pad when scanning Welsh prescriptions if "Auto-order on Welsh barcode scan" is on.  ImpactItems intended for manual ordering are added automatically, which can lead to unintended orders and override site settings. WorkaroundDisable "Auto-order on Welsh barcode scan" and enable "Auto-order at Clinical Check" instead.

articles.title: "Prevent Batch Lock Bypass" Not Preventing Multiple Users Processing Same Prescription
articles.content:
ISSUEThe "Prevent Batch Lock Bypass" setting is not preventing multiple users from processing the same prescription simultaneously.Sites have reported instances where two pharmacists have been able to process the same prescription at the same time. IMPACT
Multiple users can access and process the same prescription concurrently.
Increased risk of duplicate processing or workflow confusion.

WORKAROUNDAfter the relevant setting has been changed: All users must fully close and reopen Titan (restart the client). This ensures the updated setting applies correctly and enforces the batch lock as expected.

articles.title: ADHOC Orders Sent to Future Orders Due to Tag Turnaround Settings
articles.content: IssueADHOC orders are moving into Future Orders instead of being sent immediately when the patient has a tag with additional turnaround days applied. ImpactPharmacies may see ADHOC orders held in the Future Orders column unexpectedly, even when they expect the order to bypass future scheduling and send straight away. This can cause confusion and potential delays in processing if not noticed. WorkaroundCreate the order with the due date set to today, and the order will send immediately as intended.

articles.title: ATLAS "complete" Events not Sending if User Used Bulk Handout
articles.content:
IssueUsing Bulk Handout will prevent the "complete" event from being sent to ATLAS.
 
ImpactThis will prevent ATLAS users from booking in new items and prevent them from scanning the dispensing label at administration.
 
WorkaroundHand out prescriptions individually.
If a Bulk Handout has already been performed, please contact our Integrations team for further assistance.
You can contact them through the following means:

Call: 0117 325 4755 option 3
Email: integrations@titanpmr.com

Chat In App
Message on WhatsApp: 0117 325 4755

Fix The fix has been developed and implemented in version 2.42.18.

articles.title: Accuracy Check Permission Not Enforced on Titan Mobile for Self-Labelled Items
articles.content: IssueUsers without the permission “Can package needs check items labelled by the user” are able to complete accuracy checks on items they labelled when using Titan Mobile.  ImpactThis allows users to bypass intended permission restrictions when accuracy checking on Titan Mobile, potentially affecting accuracy and compliance processes. WorkaroundIf a user does not have the permission to accuracy check items they have labelled, the user should perform all accuracy checks on Titan Desktop instead of Titan Mobile.

articles.title: Attempting to Download an Issue Dispensed by Another Pharmacy Triggers all Further Issues to Show on the Board with Status Released
articles.content:
Issue
Attempting to download an issue dispensed by another pharmacy triggers all further issues to show on the board with status Released. The issue itself will show as Pending Download.
 
Impact
All issues will now be downloaded to your pharmacy and cannot be returned. The patient will need a new prescription if they need to to be dispensed by another pharmacy.
 
Workaround
Before clicking "Release Next Issue" from the ERD Flyout, click "Check NHS Tracker". This will set any issues dispensed by another pharmacy to "Skipped" and will prevent further issues from being dispensed
 
Fix
This issue has been fixed in version 2.37.

articles.title: Auto-Claim At Handout Not Triggering When 'Trigger DN When Closing Package' Is Enabled
articles.content: IssueWhen the “Trigger DN when closing package” setting is enabled, even when “Auto Claim on Titan Mobile” is turned on, prescriptions handed out via Titan Mobile are not auto-claiming. The scripts remain in Dispensed, instead of moving to Claimed. ImpactSites using both settings together may have prescriptions that appear handed out but have not been claimed, leading to potential claim discrepancies. WorkaroundUntil resolved, use ‘Claim All’ in the Claims screen at the end of each day to ensure all eligible scripts are claimed.

articles.title: Bag Labels Printed via Power Search (Drug Search) Missing Patient Address
articles.content: IssueWhen a user prints a bag label through a drug search in Power Search, the patient address does not display on the label. ImpactUsers printing bag labels via Power Search may find the labels missing the patient’s address, which could cause workflow disruption or require reprinting. WorkaroundUse the Patient Search function to print bag labels, as this correctly includes the patient’s address.

articles.title: Barcode Not Found Error When Labelling Dexcom One+ Sensor
articles.content: IssueWhen scanning the barcode 00386270005106 for the Dexcom One+ Sensor in the Labelling module, Titan displays a “Barcode not found” error.However, scanning the same barcode in Power Search correctly retrieves the item details, and it’s also recognised via /barcode and Barcode Checker on Titan Mobile. The item exists in the system with multiple barcodes, all of which scan successfully except this one. ImpactSites are unable to label the Dexcom One+ Sensor using barcode scanning. This can slow down the dispensing process due to having to manually add the product. WorkaroundManually add the Dexcom One+ Sensor item during labelling until the barcode mapping issue is resolved.

articles.title: Batch Flow Auto-Scrolling on Basket Change
articles.content: IssueWhen switching between baskets in Batch Flow, the scroll bar automatically moves without any user input. This occurs when a patient within the basket has 10+ tray items. Clicking on that patient causes the Batch Flow list to scroll unpredictably to various points. The behaviour is consistent across all baskets and all PCs. ImpactUsers may lose their place when navigating between baskets, causing delays and confusion during dispensing. It may appear as though items are being skipped or the screen is jumping, affecting workflow efficiency. WorkaroundUsers may need to manually reposition the scroll bar after switching baskets.

articles.title: Board Allocation Changes to Unallocated When Navigating Prescriptions
articles.content: IssueWhen opening a waiting prescription from the Inbox and navigating between prescriptions using the barcode at the top left of the Clinical Check screen, the board allocation changes from ‘Waiting’ to ‘Unallocated’. ImpactScripts that should remain in the Waiting column are automatically moved to Unallocated, potentially causing workflow confusion and incorrect board status tracking. WorkaroundA workaround is to allocate the prescription again from the Clinical Check screen.

articles.title: Board Column Disappears
articles.content:
IssueWe are aware of an issue which sometimes causes a column on the prescription board to cease to load. 
This can affect any column and regardless of whether you click refresh or load another menu and then return, the column does not load and remains empty.
 
ImpactThis prevents the column loading at all so users are unable to see prescriptions card in that status.
 
WorkaroundThe workaround is to close and reopen Titan which resolves the issue and successfully populates all columns.

articles.title: Bulk Handout Processing Failures Affecting Event and Audit Records
articles.content:
Problem StatementWe’ve observed a rise in tickets where bulk handouts are completed, but events are not sent. Prescriptions show as handed out, but their active status remains 3, and occasionally the handout audit is missing. The issue may be related to timeouts caused by processing large volumes of prescriptions in a single bulk handout. Impact
Events not being sent, causing workflow issues and potential discrepancies in care home or CD reporting.
Audit records potentially can be missed. 
Almost always requires Engineer escalation.
 Status Investigating - We are currently investigating the root cause of this problem. CauseSpecific technical cause under investigation; may involve how the system handles bulk write operations and event generation. Interim Action
Engineers will need to resend all handout events for prescriptions that were not successfully updated during bulk handout.
Root cause is being investigated in the meantime.
 Support GuidanceEscalate your ticket to the Engineers with at least one prescription example.

articles.title: Bulk Print Picking Labels
articles.content:
IssueWe have detected an issue when attempting to print a large number of picking labels in one go, typically more than 30 at a time.
 
Impact
When selecting a large number, the first 30 or so will print, and the cards will move to the label column, however, customers can experience an issue where this process halts and does not complete the bulk job.
 
Workaround
Our recommended workaround is to limit the number of batches you process in one go, and we recommend doing this in batches of 20-30 to avoid this scenario.
 
You can reprint bulk print jobs from the cog in the top right corner of the Prescription Board.

Click the cog
Click Re-print Bulk Picking Labels
Select the job you want to reprint
Click Re-Print

 
If you are no longer able to print at all after experiencing this issue, you may need to clear your print queue. To clear your print queue, please follow the steps below:

Settings
System Info
Clear Print Jobs

articles.title: Cambrian Alliance Orders Over 100 Lines are Split and Show Incorrect Status
articles.content:
IssueOrders placed to Cambrian Alliance through TITAN are automatically split if they exceed 100 lines. For example, an order with 179 lines will be split into two separate orders:

100 lines

79 lines

 
ImpactOne of the split orders may incorrectly show as "Failed" in TITAN, even though it has successfully reached the supplier.Example:

100 lines – shows as Failed

79 lines – shows as Complete

 
WorkaroundPlace orders with fewer than 100 lines to avoid automatic splitting.

articles.title: Clinical Check Audit on Prescription Timeline Shows American Formatted Dates
articles.content: ISSUEPrescription audit entries for Check Process Start and Check Process End may display incorrect future dates. These audit messages appear to use an American date format (MM/DD/YY) instead of the expected UK format (DD/MM/YY), causing dates such as 5/1/26 to appear as 1st May 2026 rather than 5th January 2026. IMPACTAudit trails can appear misleading or incorrect, showing actions dated in the future. This may cause confusion for pharmacy staff reviewing prescription history and audit accuracy. WORKAROUNDFor affected audit entries, read the date as American format and mentally swap the day and month (MM/DD instead of DD/MM). All other audit timestamps remain correct.

articles.title: Clinical Dashboard Shows No Prescriptions to Check
articles.content: IssueThe Clinical Dashboard displays no prescriptions available for checking, despite prescriptions being present in the Inbox. ImpactPharmacy staff may believe there is no clinical work to complete, which can delay processing even though prescriptions are ready in the Inbox. WorkaroundStart clinical checks directly from the Inbox instead of the Clinical Dashboard.

articles.title: Communication Error When Scanning FMD Code for Losartan 100mg tablets 28 (2 x 14 tablets) Healthcare Pharma Ltd
articles.content:
IssueWhen scanning the FMD (QR) code for Losartan 100mg tablets 28 (2 x 14 tablets) Healthcare Pharma Ltd at the labelling stage, the system shows a red toast:“Communication error. There was an error updating an item on the Titan server.”Although the label briefly appears fulfilled (green), once leaving and re-entering the labelling page, the item is no longer recognised as scanned. This prevents the prescription from being packaged, as the system does not retain the label. Impact
Known to affect: Losartan 100mg tablets 28 (2 x 14 tablets) Healthcare Pharma Ltd.
FMD scan does not complete correctly, blocking dispensing workflow for prescriptions containing this product.
Causes mismatch between physical label (printed) and digital record.
 WorkaroundUse the 1D barcode instead of the FMD QR code when scanning this product. This avoids the communication error and allows the prescription to complete as expected.You can add the batch number and expiry date manually by clicking on the green label and entering the required information.  FixThis was found to be a manufacturer issue.

articles.title: Communication Error When Scanning Losartan Potassium Film-Coated Tablets 100mg (Healthcare Pharma)
articles.content:
IssueWhen scanning the FMD barcode for Losartan Potassium Film-Coated Tablets 100mg – Healthcare Pharma brand (barcode: 05060013779947), the system produces a "Communication Error" message. This prevents the item from being recognised correctly.This has been identified as an FMD barcode error, not Titan specific.  Impact
The medication cannot be scanned into Titan when using this brand’s packaging.
The error occurs on all PCs, across all patients.
Other brands of Losartan 100mg scan successfully, so this issue is isolated to Healthcare Pharma stock.
 WorkaroundUse the 1D barcode instead of the FMD.Alternatively, scan this version of the FMD barcode:  This barcode will work to scan the medication in the labelling screen.  FixThis was found to be a manufacturer issue.

articles.title: Completed Repeat Dispensing Orders Stay In Chasing Admin
articles.content: IssueCompleted repeat dispensing orders remain in Chasing Admin instead of moving to Completed. ImpactOrders do not auto-complete once processed, leaving them in the Actions/Chasing Admin column and requiring manual completion. WorkaroundManually mark affected orders as Completed.

articles.title: Contraceptive Exemption can be Copied to Non-Contraceptive Prescriptions
articles.content:
IssueThe ‘Copy Exemption’ button allows users to copy a contraceptive exemption from a previous prescription onto a non-contraceptive item.
 
ImpactThis can result in invalid exemption claims, as contraceptive exemptions should only be applied to items listed under a specific Drug Tariff category or endorsed with ‘CC’.
 
WorkaroundAvoid using the ‘Copy Exemption’ button for these cases. Instead, manually apply the correct exemption based on the prescription item.
 
FixThe fix for this issue will be included in TITAN version 2.47.

articles.title: Crash at Clinical Check After Token Print > Save and Exit
articles.content:
IssueWhen you click the blue Print EPS token button, the button will go grey while the print job is processed. After the job has been sent to the printer, it will go blue again. We currently have an issue where clicking Save and Exit while the print button is grey will cause TITAN to crash.
 
ImpactThis issue will slow you down as you will have to reopen TITAN following the crash.
 
WorkaroundAfter clicking print, wait for the button to go blue again before clicking Save and Exit, as below.
 

 
FixWe have fixed this issue in 2.42.10. TITAN no longer crashes, and the tokens print fine. You will now be able to press Save & exit while printing EPS tokens. However, it does cause a red error message to appear.

articles.title: Dose Times are Removed
articles.content:
Issue
Dose times are getting removed seemingly automatically from some patients records. Users are then not able to re-enter the required times as the time fields are missing.
 
Impact
This can happen to any patient who has been setup with dose times in Patient Therapy and can cause a big issue as users often need to contact their patients or care homes to find out what times certain items need to be administered. 
 
Workaround
Removing and tag and reapplying often brings back the time fields, however the administration quantities will have been lost.
While we understand that this is a big inconvenience, you may wish to take a backup of the medication times by printing a backing cards/MAR charts to PDF.
This will allow you to re-enter the data should you need to without having to contact your patients.

articles.title: Duplicate CD Handout Events Created When Using Bulk Handout
articles.content: ISSUEWhen a Controlled Drug (CD) item is handed out using bulk handout, a duplicate handout event can be created. This results in multiple handout records for the same item. IMPACTThis can cause duplicate audit entries on the CD Registers, leading to discrepancies in Controlled Drug records and potential compliance concerns. It can also create confusion during audits and disrupt accurate tracking of CD handouts. WORKAROUNDDo not use bulk handout when Controlled Drug items are present.Hand out CD items individually, then use bulk handout for any remaining non-CD items.

articles.title: Duplicate EPS Prescriptions Created Due to SMH Retry After Server Timeout
articles.content:
Problem StatementDuplicate prescriptions are occasionally created in Titan when a backend server timeout causes SMH to retry sending an EPS prescription that has already been persisted. This can result in the same prescription being processed twice. Impact
Rare occurrence (approx. 0–1 per 10,000 prescriptions), but has been observed at multiple sites.
The same prescription may be dispensed twice if not spotted.
Risk is limited to a supply issue rather than a clinical safety issue, as the patient can only receive the same drug, potentially in higher quantity.
 Status Investigating - Root cause being investigated. Cause
Titan successfully saves the prescription data when received via the Spine message handler (Caremotive).
If a subsequent activity fails, Titan incorrectly reports a failure back to CareMotive, even though the prescription is already persisted.
SMH interprets this failure as a need to retry sending the prescription, creating a duplicate record.
Root cause is a backend server performance issue causing timeouts or failed responses, which trigger unnecessary SMH retries.
 Interim Action
Continue monitoring and collecting examples of duplicate prescriptions.
Investigation ongoing to implement a fix that prevents a second record from persisting if the prescription already exists.
 Support GuidanceContinue to escalate all duplicate prescription examples to the Clinical Risk team using the Zendesk macro.

articles.title: Duplicate Events Sent to CD Smart When “Trigger DN When Closing Package” Is Enabled
articles.content:
Issue When the "Trigger DN when closing package" setting is enabled in TITAN, Controlled Drug (CD) prescriptions may send duplicate events to CD Smart.
 
ImpactThis results in duplicate entries appearing in CD Smart, which may cause confusion or errors when reviewing CD records.
 
Workaround If CD Smart is installed, toggle off the “Trigger DN when closing package” setting to prevent duplicate event sends.
 
FixThis issue has been resolved in TITAN version 2.44.2.

articles.title: Duplicate Interim Therapy Item Added to Patient Record
articles.content:
ISSUEAn interim medication may be automatically added to a patient’s therapy record, even though the same medication already exists.The issue is not specific to one drug and can occur intermittently across different medications.
IMPACT

Duplicate medication appears on the patient’s therapy.
Confusion for sites regarding the source of the additional item.
Sites may need to manually correct patient therapy records.

WORKAROUNDManually delete the incorrect or duplicate therapy item from the patient’s record.

articles.title: Duplicate or Cleared Prescriptions in Claimed View After Failed Claims Fix
articles.content:
IssueAfter a failed-claims batch automatically is corrected, some prescriptions appear as Cleared in the Claimed view even though they’re successfully claimed on the Spine. If these Cleared prescriptions are uncleared, duplicate entries of the same prescription ID will appear in the Claimed tab.
 Impact
Sites may think prescriptions have been removed or not claimed.
Unclearing causes visible duplicates and confusion in claim totals.
No payment or Spine impact. This is a display issue only. 

Support Guidance

Do not instruct sites to Unclear Cleared prescriptions.
Collect examples (screenshots + Spine checks) as evidence.
Escalate to Engineering for review.
Reassure the site that claims are valid and payments are unaffected.

articles.title: ERD Auto-Download Failure
articles.content:
Problem StatementSome ERD prescriptions are not downloading automatically via the scheduled daily ERD service. ImpactPrescriptions eligible for automatic ERD release remain undownloaded, causing delays for the site and requiring manual intervention. StatusResolved – All ERD services have been upgraded and are now working as intended. New occurrences should not be happening. CauseThe ERD service was failing to make the required release calls to the Titan API during its daily schedule.
