Interim ActionAll ERD services were upgraded overnight on 11/07 across all Pods to the April 2025 ERD release, following successful testing on Pod 99.Post-upgrade checks confirm services are running as expected and ERDs are now downloading correctly. Support GuidanceIf a site reports this issue: 
Escalate to the engineering team immediately.
This issue should not recur post-upgrade, so any new cases require investigation.
 Related Resources 
ERD: FAQs
Dispensing Video: ERD
How to: Edit a Single ERD Release Date
How to: Release All (or some) Issues in One Go at Any Time
How to: Modify/Set Up an ERD Release Schedule

articles.title: ERD Download Fail if Previous Issue Date >30 Days ago
articles.content:
Issue
Prescriptions will not be downloaded automatically if the previous Issue Date is greater than 30 days ago.
ERDs are not automatically releasing when expected. Some of the ERDs move to awaiting release, however do not drop down to the board. Some remain as not started. Auto-release is turned on for these scripts.
 
This is causing site a lot of problems with their patients, as scripts are not dropping down when expected.
 
Impact
Prescriptions will not appear on the board when expected.
This is making it difficult for users to manage their ERDs and could cause users to dispense items too late.
 
Workaround
Please try the following issues the sequence to get your prescription

From the ERD Flyout, select Release Next Issue
If this does not bring it down, copy the prescription from the top and from PowerSearch write "/eps {copied rx number}" and hit enter.
Contact the Help Desk for assistance.

Fix
We believe that we have already fixed this issue in 2.37 (March), but will not be able to verify this after testing is complete.

articles.title: ERD Issue Incorrectly Marked as “Skipped”
articles.content:
Problem StatementSome ERD (Electronic Repeat Dispensing) issues are appearing in Titan as “Skipped”, even though they look like they should be available for dispensing. There is no clear audit trail explaining why they’ve been skipped, and checking the spine confirms the prescription is available for download. Impact 
Pharmacies are unable to dispense prescriptions that should be available.
Support are unable to provide a clear explanation for the skipped status, creating confusion and frustration.
Delays in dispensing may impact patient care or workflow.
 Status Investigating - The evening update for "ERD skipped without an audit" has been introduced and will take effect from 13/7 21:45. CauseThe root cause is currently unknown, but is suspected to be related to a bug in the ERD view or flyout logic within Titan. When users view an ERD prescription, an unintended process may be incorrectly triggering the “Skipped” status. No audit trail is currently left behind. Interim Action A nightly automated process now runs to detect and re-process incorrectly skipped ERD issues. This process looks for ERD issues that meet all the following criteria: 
The ERD issue is marked as Skipped

The ERD issue does not have any of the following audits:

Returned to the spine
Prescription is archived
Dispensing at another site
Prescription expired
Prescription cancelled on the spine

The issue is due within the last 30 days or in the future 
If a script meets this criteria, it is queued to be processed as part of the next ERD service run the following morning. Support Guidance If a customer reports an ERD issue incorrectly marked as Skipped, first check the prescription status on the spine to confirm it is available. 

Check how long this status has shown as Skipped for:

If it’s been less than a day, advise them the overnight fix (see below) should correct it by the next morning.
If it’s been more than a day and the issue is still Skipped, proceed to step 3.

Escalate to Engineering via Click Up.
Tip: If the audit trail shows any of the excluded events (returned, archived, expired, etc.), this is not considered part of this known problem. Related Resources 
ERD: FAQs
Dispensing Video: ERD

articles.title: ERD Issues Stuck in "Pending Download"
articles.content:
Problem StatementSome ERD issues get stuck in a "Pending Download" status after the site attempts to download multiple ERD prescriptions. ImpactUsers are unable to download the affected ERD issues, blocking prescription processing. StatusMonitoring – Fix deployed on 10/07. Behaviour is being observed to confirm long-term stability. CauseERD issues get marked as Pending Download by the ERD service that runs each morning. They also get triggered by the user or when accessing the ERD view/flyout.A failure during the ERD multi-release process can also cause a script to remain in a Pending Download state.This typically occurs when a request to the Spine Message Handler (SMH) fails silently, leaving the issue in limbo. Interim Action A new overnight job has been implemented which: 
Detects ERD issues stuck in Pending Download for over 2 hours
Resets them back to "Not Started", allowing retry via the ERD service or user interaction
Runs every evening
 Support GuidanceWhen receiving a ticket related to a Pending Download ERD script: 
If the issue has been in Pending Download for less than 1 day, advise the site to try again the following morning after the nightly reset job.
If the issue has been in Pending Download for more than 1 day, and your troubleshooting is unsuccessful, escalate to Engineering via Click Up for further investigation.
 Related Resources 
ERD: FAQs
Dispensing Video: ERD

articles.title: Error at Claim: "Error creating a bulk claim - v2"
articles.content:
Issue
"Error creating a bulk claim - v2" message displayed when attempting to submit a claim.
 

 
Impact
This issue will prevent you from claiming one or more individual prescriptions. Bulk claims will also not be possible if the prescription(s) with the issue are part of the batch.
 
Workaround
Follow these steps to resolve the issue:

Identify Problematic Prescription(s)

The error is likely caused by one or more individual prescriptions. Start by claiming 20-30 prescriptions at a time to identify the problematic ones.

Locate Prescription(s) in Power Search

Once identified, use Power Search to find the problematic prescription(s).

Withdraw or Return Problem Prescription(s)

Depending on the options available in Power Search, either withdraw or return the problematic prescription(s).
Re-process the prescription(s), ensuring that this is done from the inbox stage so that they are fully re-processed from start to finish.

Hand Out Prescription(s)

Dispense the prescription(s) accordingly.

Retry the Claim

Attempt to submit the claim again. The claim should now be processed successfully.

If the problem persists, please contact our Support team for further assistance:
 
If you are a Community or Premium site, please contact our Software team.
You can contact them through the following means:

Call: 0117 325 4755 option 1
Email: support@titanpmr.com 
Chat In App
Message on WhatsApp: 0117 325 4755

 
If you are an Enterprise site, please contact our Integrations team. 
You can contact them through the following means:

Call: 0117 325 4755 option 3
Email: integrations@titanpmr.com

Chat In App
Message on WhatsApp: 0117 325 4755

 
FixThis issue is fixed in Titan version 2.45.2.

articles.title: Expensive Items Missing From Report (£100+)
articles.content: IssueExpensive items (£100+) sometimes do not appear on the Expensive Items Report. ImpactItems claimed near endorsement period boundaries may be missing, causing reports to show incomplete data for expensive items. WorkaroundSelect the 3rd day of the month when running the report to include the intended endorsement period.

articles.title: Export to .csv - "Save file error"
articles.content:
IssueWhen attempting to export a .csv file, an error message appears, and the export does not complete successfully.
 

 
ImpactThe .csv file cannot be exported or downloaded to your PC, preventing access to the data in spreadsheet format.
 
Workaround

Open Windows File Explorer and navigate to your Downloads folder.
Locate the TITAN folder.
(Optional) Copy the contents of the Titan folder to a new location as a backup.

Delete the TITAN folder from the Downloads directory.

You should now be able to export .csv files without encountering the error.

articles.title: Extra Package Created When Dispenser Quick Packages Mixed Prep Types
articles.content:
IssueWhen a dispenser uses quick package with multiple preparation types (e.g., a normal item, a fridge line, and a Needs Check item), TITAN creates 3 packages — two closed and one open — even though only two items are valid for packaging. An empty third package is created unnecessarily.In contrast, when a pharmacist (who has the "Can package 'Needs Check' items" permission enabled) quick packages the same order, only 2 packages are created as expected.Additionally, the expected warning that a Needs Check item hasn’t been packaged is not shown for dispensers. Impact
Dispensers see an unnecessary extra (empty) package on the system.
There's no warning that a Needs Check item hasn’t been packaged.
This could lead to confusion, extra package labels being printed, and missed items during dispatch.
Inconsistent experience between user roles may lead to errors in the packaging process.
 WorkaroundDispenser should click 'Package now' rather than 'Quick Package' when multiple preparation types are involved.

articles.title: First Character Not Captured in Search Fields
articles.content: IssueThe first key press in Power Search, Filters, and similar search fields does not register. Users must delete and retype the initial character when searching. ImpactThis slows down searching for patients and other items.  WorkaroundAfter loading or refreshing the board, wait 1-2 seconds before typing into the search field. FixThis issue is fixed in Titan version 2.48.

articles.title: Future Repeat Flow Order Date Not Set When Prescription Was Handed Out via Shelf Audit
articles.content: IssueWhen handing out a prescription via the Shelf Audit, the future order in repeat flow will not populate a next order date. Even if the site's settings are configured to calculate based on the previous handout date. ImpactRepeat Flow future orders do not update correctly when packages are handed out via Shelf Audit, potentially causing missed or delayed future orders if staff don’t notice the missing Next Order Date.  WorkaroundEnsure all prescriptions for Repeat Flow patients are traditionally handed out via Titan Mobile or Desktop (not the Shelf Audit page) to ensure the Next Order Date is correctly calculated and populated. FixWe have fixed this issue and the fix will be applied to Titan version 2.45.4.

articles.title: Handout Column Sometimes Shows Incorrect Shelf Location
articles.content: IssuePrescription shows as being on a shelf in the Handout column when it is not.Power Search shows no shelf location. ImpactPrescriptions appear misplaced, causing confusion when locating items and concern that items are missing. WorkaroundRe-handout the prescription to update the handout status correctly.

articles.title: Incorrect Contact Numbers After PDS Sync
articles.content:
IssueWhen completing a PDS sync, Titan may not pull the most up-to-date patient contact number.If a patient has historical phone numbers on their NHS record, Titan may sync an older mobile number or, in some cases, a landline instead of the most recent mobile number. Impact
Patient contact details in Titan may be incorrect after a PDS sync
Recently updated mobile numbers may revert to an older number
Pharmacies may be unable to reliably contact patients using the details shown in Titan
Manual checks may be required to confirm correct patient contact information
 Workaround
Use NCRS (National Care Records Service) to view the patient’s most up-to-date contact details
Do not rely solely on the contact number pulled into Titan following a PDS sync

articles.title: Incorrect Label Split for Monthly Tray Patients When Item Quantity Exceeds 112
articles.content:
IssueIncorrect label split for monthly tray patients when the split quantity exceeds 28, and the full item quantity is over 112.  Impact
When scanning a tray item for a quantity of over 112, labels may split incorrectly. (e.g. 116 splits as 4×28 + 4 instead of 4×29).
Affects multiple items across different quantities & monthly tray patients.
Labels only split correctly after manual reset. 
WorkaroundIf the quantity exceeds 112, remove the item from the tray and add it back before scanning. It will then split as expected.

articles.title: Incorrect Number of Card Labels Print for Trays with Cancelled/Not Dispensed Items or Non-Dividable Quantities
articles.content:
Issue
Only one card label prints if an item is cancelled or marked as not dispensed at the clinical check stage. This can also occur if an item's quantity is not divisible by four.Not dispensed items at clinical check are not removed from the tray at labelling, which causes the system to miscalculate the number of labels required.
 
Impact
Pharmacies receive an incorrect number of card labels when:

An item in a tray has been cancelled or marked as not dispensed at the clinical check stage

An item's quantity cannot be divided evenly into four weekly splits

This leads to only one card label printing when four are expected, affecting workflow and clarity in dispensing.
 
Workaround
Print the remaining tray card labels manually to ensure all required labels are available.

articles.title: Incorrect Pack Size Added to Order Pad When Scanning Barcode In TITAN Mobile
articles.content:
IssueWhen scanning barcode 5054563094056 in TITAN Mobile, the item is initially added to the order pad as a 20-sachet pack. However, the associated PIP code (2218469) corresponds to a 10-sachet pack.  Impact
Incorrect pack size may be added to the order pad
Sites may receive a 10-sachet pack instead of the expected 20-sachet pack
This can lead to ordering errors and delays in stock management
 WorkaroundManually add the item to the order pad by searching for it, rather than scanning the barcode

articles.title: Incorrect Quantity on Backing Card When Using Multi-Print Function
articles.content: IssueWhen printing backing cards using the ‘Number to Print’ feature, TITAN is incorrectly dividing the item quantity by the number of sheets/cards selected, rather than following the tag split settings.For example, if the therapy quantity is 7, and the user selects to print 4 cards, each card currently shows 1.75 — even if the tag is set to weekly, which should not divide the quantity at all. ImpactThis results in incorrect quantities on the backing cards, which could mislead pharmacy teams during checking or dispensing, and potentially cause dosing confusion. WorkaroundUntil resolved, print backing cards individually to ensure the printed quantity reflects the tag settings correctly. FixThis issue is resolved in version 2.44.5.1.

articles.title: Inner Labels Not Printing for Some Subpack Special Containers
articles.content:
IssueFor special container medications supplied in subpacks, not all required inner labels are generated during the labelling process.
 
ImpactMissing inner labels may lead to incomplete packaging or confusion during dispensing.
 
WorkaroundManually create and apply labels for each subpack as needed.

articles.title: Instalment Quantity Not Updating Correctly When Entering Multi-Digit Instalments
articles.content:
IssueWhen creating an instalment script and entering the number of instalments, TITAN incorrectly updates the first instalment quantity. If the total prescribed quantity is entered (e.g. 420) and the user sets the number of instalments to a two-digit number (e.g. 14), TITAN initially registers the first digit only, assigns the full quantity (420) to the first instalment, and does not adjust it once the full number of instalments is entered. ImpactPharmacy staff may see an incorrect quantity on the first instalment, which could cause confusion or errors in dispensing if unnoticed.  Workaround
Enter the correct number of instalments in one action (typing quickly without pause).
If the first instalment quantity does not update correctly, manually adjust the quantity in the first instalment row to reflect the correct division.

articles.title: Intermittent Issue with Picking Labels Showing the Wrong Page Numbers
articles.content:
IssueWe have identified an intermittent issue where picking labels can display incorrect page numbers when printed in bulk. For example, if you bulk print picking labels for 2 patients, where Patient 1 has 2 labels and Patient 2 has 1 label, all labels print as “x of 3,” with 3 being the total number of labels. However, the expected numbering should be “1 of 2,” “2 of 2,” and “1 of 1.”
 

Example:

Patient
Incorrect Printed Page Number
Correct Page Number

John Smith
1 of 3
1 of 2

John Smith
2 of 3
2 of 2

Jack Jones
3 of 3
1 of 1

 

ImpactThis can lead to confusion when printing batches of picking labels, making it difficult to determine which labels belong in which baskets.
 
WorkaroundThere is no straightforward workaround for this, other than printing picking labels individually. If, for example, you wanted to print 10 picking labels, one option would be to press F3 ten times. However, please note that F3 does not adhere to board filters and will always print the oldest, highest-priority label first.

articles.title: Intervention Booking Date Auto-Changing
articles.content: IssueWhen setting a date for an intervention booking, the appointment date automatically changes when the card moves to the intervention section. For example, a user sets the appointment date as 21/11/2025 at 11:07 AM, but after completing the engagement and moving the card to the intervention stage, the date changes to 14/11/2025 at 11:07 AM.  ImpactUsers may have incorrect appointment dates displayed, which could lead to confusion or missed interventions if not manually corrected. Workaround Sites can manually adjust the date to correct the incorrectly auto-set appointment date. Fix This issue has been fixed in TV v2.3 Beta.

articles.title: Interventions Not Saving or Progressing When Patient Tag Contains Special Characters
articles.content: IssueIn TITANVERSE, Interventions will not save or move to the Follow Up column if the TITAN patient tag has special characters in it, even when all required information has been entered. ImpactPharmacy staff are unable to save interventions or progress them through the NMS workflow if the tag includes unsupported characters. This may lead to duplicated effort or delays in completing NMS interventions. WorkaroundRemove any special characters or symbols from the patient tag in TITAN. Once these are removed, the intervention can be saved and will move correctly to the Follow Up stage. FixThe fix for this issue is included in v1.8.

articles.title: Issues of an ERD With the Status "Awaiting Release" Will not "Auto Realign ERD Dates on Handout"
articles.content:
IssueWe have identified an issue where ERD issues with the status “Awaiting Release” do not correctly auto-realign their dates at handout.For example, when handing out Issue 1 of an ERD, if Issue 2 is still in Awaiting Release, TITAN will realign Issue 3 based on the handout date, skipping over Issue 2.
 
ImpactThis can cause confusion around dispense dates and when the patient is next due for their medication, potentially leading to misalignment in the dispensing cycle.
 
Workaround For now, we recommend disabling the “auto realign ERD dates on handout” setting to avoid unexpected date adjustments.

articles.title: Items Not Added to Order Pad When Adjusting Green Basket Quantities
articles.content: IssueWhen altering quantities in a green basket (often from the label screen) to add items to the order pad, the basket indicators change from green (already ordered) to yellow (to be added). However, after saving and exiting, the items do not appear in the order pad as expected. ImpactItems that users believe have been added to the order pad are not actually added. This can lead to missing orders and disrupt workflow, as staff assume the order pad has been updated when it has not. WorkaroundAdd the item to the order pad manually.

articles.title: Items Recognised In Titan Not Recognised By Robot
articles.content: IssueCertain items are not recognised by the robot when loading stock, despite the barcode being recognised in Titan’s Barcode Checker. Occurs randomly for different items. ImpactSites cannot load affected items into the robot, preventing automated dispensing for those products and causing disruption and frustration. WorkaroundCreate a pre-pack label and record for the drug in Titan so it can be loaded into the robot.

articles.title: Items Set To Owing May Still Be Marked As Handed Out When Included In A Package
articles.content: ISSUEIf an item is added to a package and then later removed from package and set to owing, it can still be marked as handed out when the package is completed. This results in the item appearing as handed out despite being set to owing. IMPACTThis may cause confusion for users, as items that should remain owing can appear as completed and handed out. This can lead to incorrect assumptions about whether medication has been supplied to the patient. WORKAROUNDIf you need to set an item to owing, do not include it in a package.If the item has already been added to a package, delete the package before setting the item to owing.

articles.title: Items not Getting Added to Order pad by TITAN AI
articles.content:
Issue
An intermittent issue has been identified with ordering for TITAN AI customers. If you have the "Auto order after clinical check" setting turned on, with the "R2 Download" setting off, items will sometimes fail to get added to the order pad.

 
Impact 
If items fail to add to the order pad, stock may be missed from the order leading to a shortage of stock. 
 
Workaround
Change your settings "Auto order on R2 Download". This will mean that items will get added to the pad as soon as they are downloaded and will not wait until the pharmacist or TITAN AI does the check.

Please note that the item will not actually be auto ordered, it will simply be added to the pad, so you can still choose not to order the item before submitting the order. You can also choose to leave both settings on to ensure that manual prescriptions still go to the pad.

This workaround has been thoroughly tested and no ordering issues have been identified with this setup.

articles.title: Items on ERD Flyout Will not Show While Prescription is in Inbox or Check
articles.content: IssueItems on the ERD (Electronic Repeat Dispensing) view are not displayed while the script is in Inbox or Check stages. The items only become visible from Pick stage onwards. ImpactThis causes delays for pharmacy teams, as they must manually navigate to PowerSearch or the patient’s profile to locate and verify the medication. It reduces the efficiency of managing ERDs and increases handling time. WorkaroundUse PowerSearch or access the patient’s profile directly to view the medication details while the script is still in Inbox or Check.

articles.title: Labels Split When Scanning Special Containers with Subpacks
articles.content:
IssueWhen scanning the 1D barcode of a special container that has subpacks, the system incorrectly allows the labels to split. No over-allocation warning or dialogue is triggered.
 
Impact Despite being marked as a special container, the system does not prevent splitting, and no warning or over-allocation message is shown.
 
WorkaroundManually entering these products (instead of scanning) will prevent the labels from splitting and will correctly trigger the over-allocation dialogue.

articles.title: Landline Numbers Can Be Saved As Mobile Type On Titan Mobile
articles.content: IssueTitan Mobile allows users to input and save landline numbers under the Mobile category. These numbers then sync to desktop Titan, despite validation that should prevent landlines being set as mobile numbers. ImpactThis can result in incorrect contact details being stored for patients, such as landlines being used for SMS notifications, leading to communication issues and potential confusion. WorkaroundIf adding a landline on Titan Mobile, ensure to select Phone rather than Mobile.

articles.title: Limited Display Capacity for Allergies on MAR Chart
articles.content:
Issue
Currently, the Medication Administration Record (MAR) chart is constrained in its capacity to display allergies, with a limitation of approximately 15-20 words (depending on the length of words). This restricts the number of allergies that can be shown on the MAR charts.
 
Impact

This limitation may result in incomplete allergy listings for patients with a high number of recorded allergies.In such cases, there is an associated clinical risk: a care provider may administer medication to which the patient is allergic if the allergy is not visible on the MAR chart.It is important to note that TITAN will still alert users at the Clinical Check stage if a prescription includes a substance to which the patient is known to be allergic.
 
WorkaroundAt present, there is no available workaround.

articles.title: MAR (Portrait) Standard & V3 Cut Off Warning Text
articles.content:
IssueWhen using the MAR (Portrait) Standard or V3 format, warning text may be cut off at the bottom of the chart.
 
ImpactImportant warning information may be partially or completely missing from the MAR, which could lead to missed clinical notes or instructions.
 
WorkaroundUse the Portrait V2 or Landscape MAR formats instead, as these correctly display all warning text.

articles.title: Manually Split Labels are Ignored When Drug is Scanned in Batchflow
articles.content:
Issue When manually splitting a label in the labelling screen while using Batchflow, the split is applied. However, if you then scan the drug, TITAN fulfils it as a full, unsplit label.
For example, if you manually split a pack of 28 into 2 × 14 labels, but then scan the 28-pack, the system ignores the manual split and produces a single label for 28.
 
ImpactThis may result in dispensing errors, with split packs not being labelled as required, potentially leading to incorrect supply to the patient.
 
Workaround  To ensure the split is respected, manually add the split labels instead of scanning the drug.
 
FixWe have found the cause for this issue, and the fix is in version 2.44.

articles.title: Marketplace – Alliance Ordering Field Mislabelled
articles.content: IssueIn Marketplace, the Alliance ordering option is incorrectly labelled as “Account Number”. This should display as “Terminal ID”. ImpactIf the Account Number is entered, the order will fail and will not be sent to Alliance. WorkaroundPlease ensure you enter your Terminal ID in this field. Using the Terminal ID will allow your orders to be processed successfully.

articles.title: Medication "Show on Report" Status Incorrectly Displayed Without Applying Changes
articles.content:
Issue When editing a patient’s therapy, if a user selects "Show on Report" but does not click "Apply" and instead clicks "Save," the medication appears as "Yes" for "On Report" in the flyout view. However, the medication does not appear on the printed MAR chart. If the flyout is closed and reopened, the "On Report" status correctly reverts to "No." Impact
Users may be misled by the flyout view, believing a medication will appear on the MAR chart when it will not.
This discrepancy could cause confusion until the flyout is refreshed.
 WorkaroundAlways click "Apply" after changing the "Show on Report" status before saving the therapy changes. This ensures the correct status is reflected in both the Medication tab and the MAR chart. FixThe fix for this is in Titan version 2.45.2.

articles.title: Meditech Robot Rejecting Some Drugs via Autoloader
articles.content: IssueMeditech robots are rejecting random drugs when attempting to load them via the autoloader. ImpactAffected drugs cannot be loaded into the robot using the autoloader, which may delay stock loading and dispensing workflows. WorkaroundLoad the affected drugs manually into the robot instead of using the autoloader.

articles.title: Missing Animal Address at Clinical Check and on Prescription Labels
articles.content: IssueAnimal addresses are missing at Clinical Check and on prescription labels, even though the owner has an address recorded. ImpactPrescription labels do not display the animal address, which is a legal requirement. This can result in non-compliant labels and delays in dispensing. WorkaroundBefore adding a new animal, ensure the owner has the correct full address recorded. If the animal was added before the owner’s address was entered, the animal will need to be re-added after the address is in place.

articles.title: Montelukast 5mg (Sugar Free) – 2D Scan Fails to Populate Label
articles.content:
IssueScanning the 2D barcode (5055144202846—Montelukast 5mg chewable tablets sugar free) during labelling does not populate the label as expected.
 
ImpactWhen the 2D barcode (otherwise known as FMD barcode) is scanned, the label does not populate, and the expiry date and batch number do not auto-fill.
 
WorkaroundUse the 1D barcode instead, and manually enter the batch number and expiry date if required.
 
FixWe have investigated this issue and it appears to have been a manufacturer issue with the generated barcode. The global separator is located in the wrong position. The manufacturer ended up including it after EP400 when it should be after EP4009 to include the whole batch number.
This barcode will not scan intentionally as it is invalid.

articles.title: NMS Declined Cards Delayed in Leaving Board
articles.content: IssueWhen declining an NMS on TitanVerse, the card may take several attempts to disappear. In some cases, the card will remain visible for a few extra seconds before the board refreshes. ImpactUsers may think the decline action hasn’t been registered, leading to repeated attempts or confusion. WorkaroundWait a few seconds for the board to refresh and the declined card to disappear. Fix This issue has been fixed in TV v2.3 Beta.

articles.title: NMS Prompt Triggering Incorrectly for Different Strengths of Same Drug
articles.content:
IssueNMS prompts incorrectly for different strengths of the same medication. Impact
Titan displays an NMS prompt at clinical check even if the patient has previously had a different strength of the same item (e.g. 5mg previously, now 10mg).
This contradicts CPE guidelines and may lead to invalid NMS claims. 
WorkaroundPharmacists should manually check the patient’s history before proceeding with NMS. Do not accept the prompt if a different strength has already been prescribed previously.

articles.title: NMS Setting Defaults to 'Off' After Log Out/In
articles.content: IssueWhen the NMS setting is enabled and set to "on without pharmacist check", logging out and back in causes the setting to reset to "off". ImpactThis can result in NMS not being properly logged during clinical checks and potentially affecting records.  WorkaroundBefore starting clinical checks, ensure the correct NMS setting is selected and click “Save Changes.” Do not log out until all clinical checks are completed. FixThe fix for this issue has been assigned to version 2.45.1.

articles.title: No Exemption Options on TITAN Mobile When Package Includes Prescription with Automatic Exemption
articles.content: IssueWhen a package contains multiple prescriptions and at least one has an automatic exemption (e.g., RTEC/FS), the TITAN Mobile does not offer the exemption choice for the others that still require it. ImpactPharmacy staff are unable to apply exemptions when handing out via TITAN Mobile for prescriptions that require manual exemption entry. This results in extra steps, increases the chance of errors, and can delay the handout. WorkaroundConfirm the patient's exemption, then select Skip on the Mobile device. Locate the script in TITAN from a PC and manually amend the exemption on the individual item(s) that do not have automatic exemptions applied.

articles.title: Order Basket Update Button Hidden At Clinical Check When Item Is Already On The Order Pad
articles.content: IssueOrder basket update button is cut off for items already on the order pad on Clinical Check pop-outs. ImpactUsers cannot access the Update button for certain items, even at recommended 1920×1080 resolution, making it difficult to update baskets for items further down the list. WorkaroundPress F6 to open the order pad directly and update the item.

articles.title: Order Pads Are Hidden or Inaccessible When a Large Number Exist
articles.content:
IssueSites with a high number of order pads (typically over 85) are unable to view or access all of them depending on what view you chose.In small view, the rightmost pads disappear.In large view (after expanding the screen), the leftmost pads disappear.  Impact
Pharmacies with a large number of order pads cannot easily access or use all of them.
This may disrupt ordering workflows, especially if key pads are hidden or unreachable.
Standard resizing (small or full-screen) only reveals parts of the list; users may miss pads entirely.
 WorkaroundUse the relevant view (small or large) to view the desired order pad.

articles.title: Out of Dispensing Window can Show for non-EPS
articles.content:
Issue
We are aware of an issue which affects some types of non-EPS prescriptions, namely prescriptions that have arrived via PowerMail or Primo.
 

 
Impact
This warning won't prevent you from checking the prescription, but it should not show. 
 
Workaround
The workaround is to click Accept and continue checking the prescription.

articles.title: Owing Batch – Basket Labels Print Incorrect Number of Labels/Items
articles.content: IssueWhen printing basket labels for an owing batch, the labels may show more items than is currently in the batch if items have since been dispensed or marked as ND. Labels are also still generated for patients who were originally in the basket, even if their items have since been dispensed or marked as ND. ImpactCreates confusion between the basket label and the actual owing batch status. WorkaroundUse the picking list instead of basket labels for an accurate count of outstanding items. The picking list correctly updates to reflect dispensed or ND’d items, whereas basket labels do not.

articles.title: Owing Screen Appears Blank When Using Non-Default Filters
articles.content:
IssueWhen adjusting the filter dropdown on the Owing screen, the screen displays a blank white panel concealing the grid. Items are still present (can be selected, notes/status changes still apply) but are not visible. ImpactUsers cannot visually see items on the Owing screen if they select any filter other than the default. This may cause confusion and extra time spent verifying status or details. Workaround
Leave the Owing screen on the default filter to view items.
If sorting is required, use the column headers (alphabetical, date, etc.) - sorting works correctly.
Alternatively, export to CSV for a complete view.
 FixThis issue has been fixed following a fix applied to all PODs. You should no longer see this issue anymore.

articles.title: Owing Status Cannot Be Reapplied via Tick Box
articles.content: IssueUsing the tick box to update owing statuses prevents selecting the same status consecutively. All statuses, including “No status,” are affected. The “click to change status” option works correctly. ImpactStatuses may not apply as expected when reapplying the same status, causing confusion and extra refreshes. WorkaroundUse the status filter row to change statuses instead of the tick box.

articles.title: PDS Search By NHS Number Fails When Spaces Are Included
articles.content: IssueWhen searching for a patient via the PDS flyout using an NHS number that contains spaces, the search does not return a match. The search only works if the NHS number is entered without spaces. ImpactUsers commonly copy the NHS number directly from the patient profile, where it is displayed with spaces by default. This results in failed PDS searches, causing confusion and delays while users manually remove spaces and retry the search. WorkaroundBefore searching via the PDS flyout, manually remove all spaces from the NHS number so it is entered as a continuous string of digits. FixThis issue is fixed in Titan version 2.47.3.

articles.title: PDS Sync Fails When NHS Number Contains Spaces
articles.content: IssueWhen attempting to PDS Sync a patient, the sync may fail if the NHS number contains spaces. This commonly occurs when the NHS number has been copied and pasted into TITAN, as it is saved with spaces. ImpactSites are unable to PDS Sync the patient unless the NHS number is manually edited. This can cause delays when updating patient details and may lead to confusion, as the NHS number may still be recognised elsewhere in the system. WorkaroundRemove all spaces from the NHS number in the patient record, then attempt the PDS Sync again. FixThis issue is fixed in Titan version 2.47.3.

articles.title: Package Status Inconsistencies Causing Labels to Remain in Packaging
articles.content:
Problem StatementPackages are sometimes closed, but remain in the Packaging column instead of moving to Handout. Labels appear as “ready to package” even though they are physically in a package and linked to the label ID. They should appear as "ready fto handout".This issue can be easy to miss and prevents packages from being handed out successfully without intervention. Impact
Slows workflow for sites as affected packages cannot be handed out.
Slows down operations, particularly at busy or high volume sites.
Requires manual intervention to fix.
 Status
Monitoring - Interim monitoring and auto-fix in place (5-min auto-correction for 3 sites). 
Investigation into secondary causes and full resolution ongoing.
 Cause
Likely a race condition between API calls: the second API (closing the package) may finish before the first API (moving the label into the package).
Timeouts and high load on busy pods (e.g., FR664) may exacerbate the issue.
The orange toast warning on “close package” may mitigate the issue but slows processing.
 Interim Action
Open the bag in Titan.
Edit and delete the item in the bag.
Repackage.
Close the bag.
Save and Exit.
A temporary 5-minute auto-fix and auditing is in place at 3 sites to automatically correct affected packages and assess scope.
 Support Guidance
If a package remains in Packaging despite completion, follow the workaround above.
Inform sites of potential delays and temporary fixes.
Engineering will continue to monitor, run auto-fixes, and prepare a permanent resolution.

articles.title: Package Still Showing on Board After Handout
articles.content: IssueSometimes when handing out a package, the handout does not register.The package stays on the board, even though the handout has been completed.This is occurring across multiple patients and package types. ImpactPackages appear not handed out, causing confusion for staff.Sites may believe items are missing or still on the shelf.Risk of financial loss, especially for CDs that may expire. WorkaroundPerform the handout a second time, which completes the handout successfully.You can verify that the package was actually handed out by checking the item/prescription audit if you are not sure.

articles.title: Package not Closing Correctly – Items not Marked as 'Ready to Hand Out'
articles.content: IssueWhen closing a package, some items within it do not display the "Ready to Hand Out" banner. This causes the package to remain in the Packaging column, even though it appears to have been closed. ImpactPackages get stuck in the workflow, requiring manual intervention. Sites may experience this issue multiple times a day, leading to frustration and delays. WorkaroundSites can manually open the affected package, delete the problematic item(s), re-add them, and then re-close the package. This will typically trigger the correct status. FixThis issue is fixed in Titan version 2.46.3.

articles.title: Patient Mobile Number & Alerts Updated in Titan Mobile Not Syncing to Titan Desktop
articles.content:
ISSUEWhen adding or updating a patient’s mobile number and enabling alerts within Titan Mobile, the changes do not update in Titan Desktop.
IMPACT

Patient contact details and alert preferences entered via Titan Mobile are not reflected in Titan Desktop.
Risk of incorrect or missing SMS alerts.
Duplicate data entry required if not identified.
 
WORKAROUNDAdd or update the patient’s mobile number and alert preferences via Titan Desktop (PC) instead of Titan Mobile.

articles.title: Patient Tags Not Displaying When Scanning Package Labels on Titan Mobile
articles.content: IssueWhen scanning a package label in Titan Mobile, the patient’s assigned tags do not load. The app offers the option to add a new tag, but existing tags are not displayed. Tags do appear correctly if the user searches for the patient by manually typing their name. ImpactUsers may assume the patient has no tags assigned, leading to potential missed important information during handouts. WorkaroundSearch for the patient by name instead of scanning the package label to view existing tags.

articles.title: Picking Robot Skips Some Items In Batch Picking
articles.content: IssuePicking robot sometimes does not pick all requested items in batch dispensing. ImpactSome items with available stock are not dispensed, resulting in incomplete batches and requiring additional manual intervention. WorkaroundRequest missing items manually at label stage using the F2 flyout. FixWe have added improvements to the picking logic and auditing of this action in Titan v. 2.49.

articles.title: Prescriber Field Incorrectly Required for PGD Prescriptions
articles.content: IssueWhen creating a PGD (Patient Group Direction) prescription in TITAN, the system currently requires a prescriber to be entered, even in scenarios where a prescriber is not clinically necessary. ImpactThis causes delays and confusion when processing PGD prescriptions, as users are unable to complete the prescription unless a prescriber is added, even when this step is not appropriate for the type of script being issued. WorkaroundUntil the issue is resolved, users should enter the pharmacist as the prescriber to proceed with PGD prescription processing.

articles.title: Prescriptions Processed Through Titan AI Partial Automation Skipping Parked
articles.content:
IssueSome prescriptions with the send to parked toggle ON in the patient tag are skipping parked and going straight to label/pick (depending on your Dispensing Settings).This occurs when the prescriptions go through partial automation on Titan AI, which incorrectly turns off the toggle in the clinical check screen, preventing them from being routed to parked. Impact
Prescriptions intended for parked may go straight to label or pick.
Manual intervention needed to correct workflow if missed, especially for care home or other parked patients.
 WorkaroundDuring clinical check, verify that the send to parked toggle is ON for patients whose prescriptions should go to parked.Care home patients can be identified via their patient tag on the clinical check screen.

articles.title: Private PGD Prescriptions Prompting NHS Charge On Titan Mobile
articles.content: Issue When handing out a Private PGD prescription (for example, Mounjaro 2.5mg), Titan Mobile prompts for a £9.90 NHS charge instead of a private charge. ImpactPrivate PGD prescriptions are technically private items, so prompting an NHS charge can cause confusion at handout and may result in incorrect charging unless manually corrected. WorkaroundAt handout, ignore the NHS charge prompt and manually take the appropriate private payment for the prescription. FixThis issue is fixed in Titan version 2.47.3.

articles.title: Private Prescriptions View Times Out After 30 Seconds
articles.content: IssueWe have identified an issue with the Private Prescriptions view, where it times out after 30 seconds. When this happens, the screen will display previously loaded data, which can be misleading as it appears the filter has been applied successfully, even though the updated results have not loaded.ImpactThis issue does not affect most sites; however, larger sites or those with slower internet connections may experience failed data loads, leading to inaccurate or outdated information being displayed.WorkaroundUse the "Rx  Arrival" filter to narrow the time window to just a couple of days. This reduces the amount of data being pulled and ensures the results load accurately without timing out.

articles.title: Progress Bar Displays 0/0 in Tagged Patients View
articles.content: IssueIn the Tagged Patients View, the progress bar for some patients displays 0/0 items in progress, even when the prescriptions include multiple items progressing through the workflow. ImpactUsers cannot rely on the progress bar in the Tagged Patients View to understand when items and prescriptions are currently in progress. This reduces visibility of workflow status and may lead to unnecessary checks across multiple screens. WorkaroundUsers should refer to the Prescription Board to accurately view the progress of the patient’s prescriptions and items.

articles.title: Progress Bar in Parked View Shows Incorrect Totals if Prescriptions Are Released from Board
articles.content:
IssueThe progress bar displayed on the 'Parked Patients' view becomes inaccurate when prescriptions are released from the board (via the prescription flyout), rather than from the Managed Patients screen.The progress bar is meant to show (per patient):

First number = how many prescriptions are currently in Parked

Second number = total number of prescriptions on the board 
However, releasing prescriptions via the board removes the prescription from the total count, which causes the progress bar to display incorrect information. ImpactStaff using the progress bar to assess how many prescriptions remain for a patient may be misled by incorrect figures. This can result in missed items, delayed processing, or unnecessary follow-up, particularly in busy environments. WorkaroundTo maintain accurate progress bar stats:
Always release parked prescriptions via the Managed Patients view.
If a prescription has already been released via the board and the numbers seem incorrect, refer to the main prescription board for a more reliable count.

articles.title: Quick Packaging Fails After Labelling Instalments
articles.content:
IssueAfter updating to 2.45.1, when a site labels instalments (e.g. Methadone), attempting to use Quick Package immediately after results in the error:“Label not complete. Quick packaging not possible because there are no complete labels.”This is incorrect, as there are clean (green) completed labels available. Impact
Sites cannot immediately quick package instalments after labelling them.
Increases dispensing time as staff must leave/re-enter the labelling screen before packaging.
Could cause workflow disruption during high-volume dispensing.
 Workaround
Label the instalments.
Select Package Now and package one instalment.
Return to the labelling screen.
Quick Packaging will then be available for the remaining clean labels.

articles.title: RP Logs Incorrectly Displaying Red Rows For Users To Add Missing Hours
articles.content: IssueDue to the transition on 26th October 2025 from BST to GMT, this has caused RP logs to incorrectly display red rows for users to add missing hours. ImpactThis is a display issue. The missing hours being displayed are for example from 18:00 to 19:00, when the pharmacy business hours state they close at 18:00, therefore missing hours should not be detected, as there are not any missing hours. WorkaroundAt present, there is no available workaround.  FixThis issue has been fixed in Titan version 2.46.3.

articles.title: Repeat Flow Orders Placed on Titan Mobile Set Incorrect Future Due Date
articles.content:
IssueWhen creating a Repeat Flow order in Titan Mobile, selecting a due date and then adding an item causes the due date to jump forward by one month. Even if the date is corrected before processing, the order is saved with the incorrect future date. No current order is created, only a future one. Impact
Repeat orders cannot be reliably created from Titan Mobile.
Pharmacies may think an order has been placed when it hasn’t.
This may lead to missed medication deliveries or confusion with scheduled dispensing.
 WorkaroundCreate Repeat Flow orders using Titan on a PC rather than the mobile app.

articles.title: Repeat Request Emails Remain in “Pending” Status Without Notification
articles.content:
Problem StatementRepeat request emails sent via NHS Mail from TITAN remain in a "Pending" status and do not update to "Sent" or "Failed", leaving pharmacies without visibility into whether emails have successfully reached GP surgeries. 
Impact 
Pharmacies may assume emails have been sent when they have actually failed.
This can result in delayed or missed repeat prescriptions for multiple patients.
The absence of proactive alerts means days of failures may go unnoticed, disrupting workflow and patient care.
Support teams may receive high volumes of follow-up queries about missing or unprocessed repeats.
 StatusDiagnosed - We are currently looking at potential fixes for this problem. CauseThe NHS mail status update service in TITAN is not consistently processing status updates after an email is triggered, so the email remains marked as "Pending" indefinitely.Additionally, TITAN does not currently alert users when multiple email failures occur, making the issue harder to spot. 
Interim Action 
Support teams should advise customers to manually check with GP surgeries if an email remains in a "Pending" state for an extended period (e.g. more than an hour).
If customers experience multiple Pending emails in a day, especially across multiple patients or surgeries, they should report to Support so logs can be reviewed and escalated to the engineers.
Encourage pharmacies to periodically verify NHS Mail credentials to reduce the risk of failures.
 Support Guidance 
Check status of repeat request emails: Go to the patient’s flyout → Order History tab → Confirm if email remains "Pending".
If multiple 'Pending' entries are reported across patients/sites, escalate to Engineering referencing problem ticket: Pending emails.
Inform customer the issue is diagnosed and being worked on, and that a future enhancement of this service is planned.
Confirm that the customer can log in to their NHS mail account.
If customer reports issues with NHS Mail credentials, verify spelling, special characters, and password length. 
 Related Resources 
NHS Email SMTP & Application Account Process
How to: View the History of Email Orders Sent to GP Surgeries

articles.title: Robot Unable to Load Stock for Some Recognised Barcodes
articles.content:
Problem StatementWhen a customer attempts to load stock into the robot, some products fail to load despite their barcodes being recognised in Titan. Other items are loaded successfully, leading to inconsistent behaviour. Upon investigation, the affected barcodes are present in Titan and available for labelling, but the robot refuses to accept them. Impact 
Robot stock loading is partially blocked, reducing its usefulness.
Affected pharmacies must resort to manual processes, which slows workflow and increases frustration.
Can create uncertainty around what the robot will or won't accept.
 Status Identified - Root cause not investigated yet. CauseThe root cause is currently unknown, but is suspected to be related to one of the following issues:  Primary CauseThe drug in question is missing a Stock Item record in Titan. Without this, the robot cannot match the barcode to a loadable product even if it's recognised for labelling. Secondary Cause (Less Common)Occasionally, this may be linked to FMD barcode discrepancies. Some FMD barcodes begin with a leading zero (e.g., 0123456789), but Titan may store the version without the zero (123456789). This is treated as a separate issue but can appear similar. Interim ActionCustomers should: 
Manually print and apply labels via Titan Assembled Packs screen for the affected items.
Continue to use the robot for items that are loading successfully.
This allows dispensing to continue but does not resolve the missing linkage between the barcode and robot stock record.  
Support Guidance Ask the customer to confirm whether the barcode can be used for labelling in Titan.If the barcode is recognised by Titan, follow these steps: 
Open Titan Console > Missing Stock Records (see Titan Console: Known Issues for guide).
Search for the items in the Missing Stock Records tool. 
If it appears: Add the stock record. The drug should now be scannable into the robot.If it does not appear: Escalate the incident to Engineering team.Provide the manual labelling interim action while waiting for an engineer-side resolution. If the barcode is not recognised by Titan, ask the customer to upload the barcode via the Barcode Checker on Titan Mobile.  Tip: If in doubt, always try the drug in Missing Stock Records before escalating. Related Resources 
Titan Console: Known Issues
TITAN Mobile: Registering a New Product Barcode
Robot Integration: Overview

articles.title: SLS Prompting in Error in Wales
articles.content:
IssueSome items that need an SLS endorsement in England but not Wales are still prompting for an SLS in Wales.
 
ImpactYou will not be able to progress to dispensing until the SLS has been added.
 
Workaround

Click on the edit pencil

Click Additional Endorsements

Choose the SLS endorsement from the list
Click Submit

Click Add Item

articles.title: Scanning FMD Barcode for Trajenta 5mg Tablets Causes Errors and Crashes
articles.content: IssueScanning the FMD barcode on Trajenta 5mg tablets (05060412243278) results in an ‘Unknown FMD barcode – Null FMDBarcodeModel’ error on the Labelling screen.When scanning the same barcode on the Assembled Pack screen to add a pre-pack, Titan may crash after multiple scans.The barcode scans successfully in Power Search. ImpactPharmacy teams may be unable to label Trajenta 5mg tablets using the FMD barcode.Attempts to add a pre-pack by scanning this barcode can cause Titan to become unresponsive or crash, disrupting the workflow. WorkaroundFor now, manually label the product in the Labelling or Assembled Pack workflows or scan the 1D barcode instead of scanning the FMD barcode.Avoid repeated scanning attempts in the Assembled Pack screen to prevent Titan from crashing.

articles.title: Scanning an Item Removed From Tray Will Account for the Full Quantity
articles.content:
IssueScanning an item removed from the tray will account for the full quantity, even if you have only scanned a portion of the required quantity.

ImpactThis could cause you to inadvertently dispense less that the required quantity. WorkaroundRemove the item from the tray in Patient Therapy, then reload the labelling screen.

articles.title: Shared Address Incorrectly Updated Across Multiple Patients
articles.content:
Problem Statement A patient's address is incorrectly changed to another patient's new address, typically seen in Care Home scenarios. The issue arises when one patient moves out and their address is updated. This change then applies to multiple other patients who never moved. Impact 
Multiple patient records are updated with an incorrect address.
Pharmacies lose visibility on the correct current address for Care Home patients.
There is risk of miscommunication, delivery errors, and patient safety concerns.
Confusion for support and pharmacies when troubleshooting patient history or residency.
 Status Diagnosed - The night time fix has been implemented for Pod 1 as of 14/7, and following a period of monitoring, we will extend it to the remaining Pods. Cause This problem occurs due to how Titan handles address records when registering patients: 
A new patient is added to Titan.
Their address matches an existing record already in the system (e.g. a Care Home).
Titan links the patient to the existing address, instead of generating a unique copy.
As other Care Home residents are registered, this shared address usage grows.
When one patient moves out and the address is updated, the linked record is edited, meaning all linked patients now show the new (incorrect) address. 
A backlog ticket exists to address the root cause, ensuring Titan always creates individual address records during patient registration. Interim Action  To prevent future instances and correct existing ones, an overnight job is now in place (currently for Pod 1 only) that: 
Detects shared address records linked to multiple patients.
Clones the address for each patient, creating a unique version.
This ensures that if one patient moves, their new address change does not affect others.
Monitoring is in place, and once confirmed stable, the job will be rolled out to other Pods. Support Guidance If a customer reports a patient with the wrong address, follow these steps: 
Confirm whether the address has recently been changed for another patient at the same location.
Advise that the overnight job should detect and correct this automatically if the site is in Pod 1.
If the incorrect address is still showing the next day, or the site are not on Pod 1, escalate to Engineering. 
Note: Until the overnight fix is live for all Pods, similar issues may occur elsewhere. Related Resources How to: Edit Patient Records

articles.title: Some Card Labels not Scanning all Items into Package
articles.content:
IssueWhen scanning card labels into a package, not all associated prescription items are always added.  Re-scanning the same card labels does not resolve the issue.
 
ImpactThis slows down the packaging process and increases manual intervention.
 
WorkaroundPrint a new set of card labels for the same prescription and scan those instead — this resolves the issue and allows all items to be scanned and added correctly.Alternatively, you could manually add the remaining items to the package.

articles.title: Some Welsh Prescriptions Do Not Populate After Scanning
articles.content:
IssueWhen scanning some Welsh prescriptions, the “Getting your prescription” message displays but no prescription details appear. Re-scanning the same barcode then shows a “Prescription already scanned” error, despite the prescription not being visible. Impact
Scanned prescriptions may appear missing
Re-scanning can cause confusion and delays in processing
 WorkaroundManually enter the prescription instead of scanning.

articles.title: Sometimes Preferred PIP Code Reverts to Generic & Incorrect PIP Displays in Stock Ordering
articles.content:
IssueWhen selecting some drugs in Titan, the preferred PIP code does not save and reverts back to the generic version.
Additionally, when selecting a PIP code in Stock Ordering, a different PIP code may display in the column.
Impact 

Branded selections may revert to the generic item.
Risk of incorrect product being added to the order pad if not manually checked.

WorkaroundManage the version added to the order pad by either:• At Clinical Check – Ensure the correct branded item is selected and confirm the correct PIP is added to the order pad. OR• Before sending the order – Review the item on the order pad and manually amend the PIP code if required.

articles.title: Supervised MDA Labels Do Not Display "Supervised" When Barcode Is Scanned
articles.content: IssueFor MDA prescriptions where Supervised is toggled ON for all dispense dates, scanning the item during labelling does not result in the label showing "Supervised". However, if the label is created manually, the "Supervised" indicator does appear as expected. ImpactPharmacy staff may unknowingly dispense supervised MDA medication without the correct supervision indicator on the label if relying solely on scanning. WorkaroundManually label all supervised MDA items until resolved to ensure the "Supervised" label prints correctly. FixThe fix for this issue is included in Titan v2.45.6.

articles.title: TITAN  AI Bursts Ending Prematurely
articles.content:
IssueWe are aware of an issue with TITAN AI bursts ending prematurely.
ImpactThe burst will stop and you will need to do any required QA checks before you can start a new burst again.
WorkaroundComplete the required QA checks as prompted, then restart the burst.

articles.title: TITAN AI 'Start Audit' Button Launches Version That Cannot be Saved
articles.content:
IssueWhen a TITAN AI burst has completed, selecting ‘Start Audit’ from the top-right prompt incorrectly opens a version of the audit that does not save, preventing users from progressing or restarting the burst. ImpactUsers are unable to complete or re-start a TITAN AI burst via the top-right audit prompt, causing confusion and delays in auditing and restarting the AI process. WorkaroundInstead of using the audit button in the top-right, users should:
Open the TITAN Audit Clinical Dashboard (change dashboard via the settings cog if needed).
Find the latest burst and complete the audit from there.
Once complete, the user can re-start the AI burst successfully.
 FixThe fix for this issue has been added to TITAN version 2.44.7.

articles.title: TITAN Mobile Displays Incorrect RTEC Exemption Status During Handout
articles.content: IssueTITAN Mobile incorrectly calculates the number of RTEC-exempt prescriptions in a package. Instead of recognising 3 RTEC-approved prescriptions, it appears to count by item and reports a partial exemption (e.g. "3 of 12 prescriptions exempt"). This leads to the TITAN Mobile prompting for charges, despite the entire prescription being exempt under RTEC. ImpactSites may incorrectly believe charges are required, slowing down handout and increasing the risk of incorrect charging or delays during handout on TITAN Mobile. WorkaroundSelect Skip on the TITAN Mobile handout screen, then re-run RTEC from the Claims screen on desktop to correctly confirm exemption status.

articles.title: Titan AI - Automation Inconsistencies on Level 3
articles.content:
Problem StatementWhen Titan AI is set to Level 3 (Full Automation), the following inconsistencies may occur: 
An item does not meet the criteria for full automation but is still processed as fully automated.
Items that do meet the full automation criteria are incorrectly held as partial automation.
 Impact 
Automation confidence is undermined, causing potential misprocessing or delays.
Support and pharmacy users face confusion over why items have behaved inconsistently.
Could lead to unsafe or inappropriate outcomes if unchecked.
 Status Resolved - After a period of monitoring in v205, we can confirm this issue is now resolved. Cause This problem is linked to application-level issues in Titan AI version 204 and earlier, specifically in how Level 3 automation logic is applied. Interim Action The problem has been confirmed resolved in Titan AI version 205, which includes the following fixes: 
Proper handling of automation criteria to prevent false positives or missed automations.
Improved processing logic for all items passing through Level 3 automation.
 Support Guidance 
Confirm the site is experiencing the problem (e.g. incorrect automation behaviour on Level 3).

Check the Titan AI version:

If version 204 or below and on Titan 2.44.3+ → Raise Galaxy ticket for v205.
If already on v205, raise a ticket to Engineering for investigation, as the fix should cover all known symptoms.

Reassure the site that version 205 addresses the known root cause.
 Related Resources
TITAN AI: Video
TITAN AI: What Do the Different Levels Mean?
TITAN AI: What is the Difference Between Full Automation and Assisted Mode?
TITAN X: Video

articles.title: Titan AI Burst Duration Not Updating Live on Same Device
articles.content: IssueWhen the burst duration is changed via Titan AI settings (e.g., from 1 hour to 4 hours) while the current burst is live, the timer does not update on the PC where the change is made. Instead, the countdown continues showing the original duration until Titan is restarted or another user signs in. ImpactUsers may be misled by the displayed burst time, believing they have more/less time than they actually do. The burst may appear to be running normally but is in fact over, resulting in prescriptions not being processed until a new burst is started. This can delay prescription downloads and disrupt pharmacy workflow. WorkaroundIdeally, do not change burst settings while the burst is live. However, if necessary, after changing the burst duration in Titan AI, restart Titan on the PC where the change was made to reflect the correct burst timer. Alternatively, sign in using another user account, which also refreshes the timer. FixThe fix for this issue will be included in Titan version 2.45.3.

articles.title: Titan AI Flyout Shows Incorrect User As Automation Starter
articles.content: IssueTitan AI flyout displays the incorrect user as having started the automation. ImpactCan cause confusion when multiple users share a workstation or use the same account, as the flyout incorrectly attributes who initiated the Titan AI Burst. WorkaroundSign out and back into Titan. This refreshes the user attribution and displays the correct name of the user who started the automation.

articles.title: Titan Crashes When Scanning Certain Barcodes During Prepack Creation
articles.content:
ISSUETitan may crash when scanning certain product barcodes while creating a prepack from the Assembled Pack screen.
This occurs after scanning the affected product barcode.IMPACT

Titan crashes during prepack creation.
Workflow disruption for assembled packs.
Prepack cannot be completed using barcode scanning for the affected item.

WORKAROUNDManually add the item as a prepack instead of scanning the product barcode.

articles.title: Titan Mobile Not Displaying All Items In “Being Processed” View
articles.content: IssueOn Titan Mobile (TM), the “Being Processed” section within Patient Information does not consistently display all prescription items that are present on the Titan desktop board. Some items appear correctly, while others are missing. ImpactThis can mislead users into thinking items are not on the prescription or have not been processed, potentially causing confusion or incorrect dispensing decisions when relying on Titan Mobile. WorkaroundUse Titan desktop to view the full prescription, as this accurately reflects all items on the board.

articles.title: Titan Mobile Prevents Adding Mobile/Email Contact Details
articles.content: IssueIn Titan Mobile version 2.0.1087, users are unable to add mobile phone numbers or email contact details.  Impact Sites using this version of Titan Mobile cannot update patient contact details directly within the app. This may lead to incomplete patient records if details are not updated through other means. WorkaroundUse the Titan desktop software to add or update mobile phone and email contact details until a fix is released. Fix The fix for this issue is included in Titan Mobile v2.0.1094.

articles.title: Titan Mobile – Connection Failure via Titan VPN on Android
articles.content:
IssueSome Android users using the Titan VPN to access Titan Mobile are currently experiencing connection issues. ImpactAffected users may be unable to connect to Titan Mobile while using the Titan VPN on Android devices. WorkaroundWe have identified the issue with the Android Titan VPN and have a workaround should you experience a loss of connectivity following successful connection to the VPN on an Android device: 
Open FortiClient.
Check that the IP address begins 100.67.40…
If it does, disconnect and reconnect until the “40” changes to any other number.
Once it changes, try to access Titan again. 
We are working with our firewall team to rectify this and will provide a further update shortly.If you need further assistance, please contact Titan Hardware Support:hardware@titanpmr.com0117 325 4755 (Option 2)We’ll share an update once more information is available regarding the cause of this issue. Fix Our firewall team have made a change which has fixed this issue.We can confirm this issue is resolved after a period of enhanced monitoring and thorough tests.

articles.title: Unable to Add Notes to SSP Item During Clinical Check
articles.content: IssueWhen attempting to add notes to an SSP (Serious Shortage Protocol) substitute item during the clinical check stage, the notes field appears, but pressing Enter does not save or display the note. ImpactNotes cannot be added to the SSP item during the clinical check stage, potentially resulting in a delay in adding the information needed. WorkaroundAdd any necessary notes before or after the clinical check stage. Notes added outside of this step do save and will carry forward as expected.

articles.title: Unpinning or Pinning Patient Notes Removes “Print on Package Label” Setting
articles.content:
IssueWhen a user pins or unpins a patient note in TITAN, the “Print on Package Label” setting is automatically deselected — even though it was previously applied.For example:
Adding and pinning a note with “Print on Package Label” ticked works as expected.
However, if the note is later unpinned, the package label option is no longer active.
Similarly, if an existing note with the package label ticked is then pinned, the setting is also removed. 
ImpactLeads to notes not being printed on package labels as intended, which could result in missed patient instructions or site-specific information not being communicated.  WorkaroundAvoid pinning or unpinning notes if you require the “Print on Package Label” setting to stay active. Leave comments unpinned to ensure the package label setting remains applied. FixThis issue is fixed in TITAN version 2.44.7.

articles.title: Wrong Drug Scanned Error – Sharpsguard Disposal Unit 5L Yellow
articles.content: IssueWhen scanning the correct barcode (5056067802885) for Sharpsguard Disposal Unit 5L Yellow during labelling, Titan triggers a “Wrong Drug Scanned” error.The item is recognised in Power Search (manufacturer: Daniels Healthcare Ltd), yet still fails validation during the labelling scan. ImpactSites are unable to label prescriptions containing Sharpsguard Disposal Unit 5L Yellow via barcode scanning.This increases manual input times, especially for high-volume dispensing environments. WorkaroundManually add the label in the labelling screen instead of scanning.

articles.title: Wrong User's Name Recorded Against an Action
articles.content:
Issue
We have identified an issue with the wrong user's name has been recorded against an action in Power Search>Item History.
The wrong user name seems to be a random one from across all TITAN users. As such, if this happens, it will be very likely that the user name displayed will be for a user that does not work in your pharmacy (in about 1 in 500 cases it could be a user in your pharmacy) and so it should be obvious to you that this data is incorrect. 

Impact
This will lead to inaccurate date being displayed in your audit.
 
Workaround
There is no know workaround to this.
Please report any instances to the Help Desk asap to help us to identify the cause.
This is a high priority issue and we hope to fix it promptly.

articles.title: £ and % Symbols in Welsh Prescriptions Cause Scan Failure and Scanner Crash
articles.content:
IssueScanning a Welsh prescription with a £ or % symbol in the dosage field causes the prescription to not be recognised by TITAN. When this happens, the scanner stops responding entirely.
 
Impact

The scanner becomes unresponsive and requires a restart.

The prescription cannot be processed via scanning, increasing the manual workload.

An error message will appear at the time of scanning, adding to the confusion for staff.

 
Workaround

Manually enter the prescription into TITAN instead of scanning.
Restart the PC to restore scanner functionality.

articles.title: ‘Release’ Button Missing in Power Search for Long Medication Names
articles.content: IssueIn the Active ERD Issue(s) section of Power Search, long medication names are not wrapping correctly. As a result, the Release and ERD status buttons are cut off and not visible to the user. ImpactUsers are unable to release ERD items from Power Search when this occurs, potentially delaying the prescription processing workflow. WorkaroundUse the ERD view instead to release affected prescriptions. The buttons display as expected in that view. FixThe issue will be fixed in TITAN version 2.44.7.

articles.title: ‘Show on Picking’ Not Working For Medication-Level Notes On First Entry
articles.content:
IssueWhen adding a medication-level note in Patient Therapy and selecting “Show on Picking”, the note does not display on the picking label if it is the first time a comment is added for a newly added therapy item. Impact
Notes intended for the picking label may not display if added on the first attempt.
Could cause missed instructions for dispensers and require users to repeat steps.
 Workaround
Re-enter the note a second time.
On the second attempt, the comment saves correctly and will display as expected on the picking label.

articles.title: ‘View on Board’ in PowerSearch Doesn’t Override Existing Board Filter
articles.content: IssueWhen using the "View on Board" option from PowerSearch, TITAN does not override any pre-existing filter already active on the prescription board. Instead, it simply loads the filtered view, meaning the patient you’ve selected may not appear. ImpactUsers may be confused when clicking "View on Board" but not seeing the expected patient or their prescription. This can lead to delays in processing, unnecessary troubleshooting, or assumptions that the prescriptions are missing. WorkaroundBefore clicking "View on Board" in PowerSearch, clear any filters currently active on the prescription board to ensure the selected patient's prescriptions load correctly. FixThis issue has been resolved in version 2.44.7.

articles.title: Dispensing Label Colour Meanings
articles.content:
Green: When the label was printed, none of the scenarios that trigger final checks as set in Settings>Clinical Settings>Final Checks were triggered.
 
 
Red: When the label was printed, a Final Check was triggered. The label could have been a split pack, printed without barcode verification, a high risk item, or it could have matched any other scenario as set in Settings>Clinical Settings>Final Checks.
 
 
Purple: The item was sent to Owing during labeling as there was no stock available.

 
Grey: The item was marked as Not Dispensed during labeling.

articles.title: Single Scan Mode. How to enable and what is it?
articles.content:
What is Single Scan Mode?
TITAN Single Scan Mode is primarily designed to assist with processing your 7-day MDS prescriptions. When the tag setting is enabled, you will only need to scan a product pack once during labelling. TITAN will automatically cycle through all identical items on screen and allocate the pack across as many prescriptions as the quantity allows. You’ll only need to scan a second pack if the number of tablets in the first box is insufficient to fulfil all the prescriptions.

articles.title: TITAN MAR Charts v1
articles.content:
Titan MAR charts
Introduction
Titan PMR produces Medication Administration Record Charts for the recording of administration of medication, booking in of quantities supplied and carrying forward any existing stock of medication.
The aim of the document is to explain the different sections of the MAR chart and to clarify the booking in process.
Sections relating to the MAR chart
The different sections of the MAR chart are designed to ensure that the person administering the medicines is able:

Identify the patient, their allergies, their Doctor and Surgery
Identify the week, date and day
The medication name, strength, formulation
Instructions for administration
BNF / Special warnings
Times of administration – Please note that only times of administration specified for the patient are printed, as opposed to all the times of administration for the care home. This is a safety feature to avoid confusion and may be different to other MAR charts provided by other pharmacy software systems.
Quantities to be administered at a specific time
Space for care home staff to initial and write quantity administered
If the medication is supplied in a tray / MDS
Usual prescribed quantity on a prescription – Please note that this may be different to other MAR charts supplied by other pharmacies where the quantity supplied is indicated and if there is no supply, Zero is indicated.
Space for care home to write down quantity received for booking in purposes
 Space for initials of care home staff who booked in the medication
 Space for care home to write down quantity of existing stock carried forward
 Space for care home to write down quantity of existing stock returned
 Space for initials of care home staff that carried forward / returned stock
 Codes to indicate reasons for non-administration

An example MAR chart is provided overleaf.
Process for booking in of Medication
The process of booking in of medication is the responsibility of the care home.
The recommendation is the following:

Care home staff to open every package supplied from the pharmacy and physically count the quantity in each medication box received.
To write down in the “Qty received” section the actual quantity counted.

If there has not been a supply for the medication with the MAR chart, the staff member is to write down Zero, initial and date.

In the space “By” , the person who carried out the count, to initial / sign and date.
If any existing stock is to be carried forward, in the section “C/F” to write down the quantity.
If any existing stock is to be returned, in the section “Qty Ret” to write down the quantity.
In the section “By”  the person who carried out the carry forward / return , to initial / sign.

Process for recording the administration of medicines
The recording and administration of medication is the responsibility of the care home.
The recommendation is the following:

Identify the resident / patient using the information on the Header of the MAR chart.
Identify the medication and the times of administration that is due to be administered.
Select the physical box of medication.
Check the label and instructions for use, the expiry
Pop out the medication required for that time into a pot/container
Repeat processes 2-5 of the above
Take a glass of water and the pot of medication to the resident / patient
Identify the patient / resident and give them the pot of medication followed by a glass of water
Once observed that the medication has been taken, initial the MAR chart
 If medication has not been taken, write the code in the appropriate box on the MAR chart and initial.
If you require to write notes, simply turn the MAR chart over where there is a blank space. Write the date and the medication that your notes relate to.

 
Process for making amendments on MAR charts
Although it is recommended to reduce the number of hand amended MAR chart entries, CQC allow hand amendments as long as they are accurate and checked by two people and witness signatures are recorded. The Titan MAR charts have spaces for new times of administration to be added.
 
 
 
Example MAR charts and sections
