articles.title: Full Walkthrough (Original Pack Dispensing)
articles.content:
New rules for Original Pack Dispensing, or OPD, are coming in from January 2025, allowing Pharmacies to supply up to 10% more or less than the prescribed quantity for EPS prescriptions, (in addition to the already permitted private prescriptions), as long as it's in the manufacturer’s original pack and meets other prescription requirements.
Using this flexibility depends on the pharmacist’s professional judgement. For example, it may not be appropriate to use for medicines like antibiotics or steroids if an exact dose is critical.
Not all products are eligible. OPD ±10% applies to Prescription Only Medicines, but not to controlled drugs in Schedules 1-4, special containers, or some appliances.
It’s also worth noting that OPD reimbursement will only apply to electronic prescriptions, not paper ones, and excludes certain protocols like SSPs and PGDs.
Specific OPD Dispensing Rules

General Rule

Up to ±10% of the prescribed quantity may be dispensed if it aligns with the nearest available original pack.

Example: A prescription for 28 tablets allows dispensing of 25–31 tablets (±3 tablets, rounded to the nearest whole number).

Special Considerations

Acute antibiotic prescriptions: OPD may not apply if the prescriber’s regimen would be disrupted. This is at the supervising pharmacist's discretion.
Special containers: If a prescribed quantity (e.g., 20g) requires a larger container (e.g., 30g), the existing special container rules supersede the ±10% rule.

Sodium Valproate-Specific Rules

OPD is not subject to the 10% restriction. Full packs must be dispensed unless a risk assessment determines alternative packaging is in the patient’s best interest.

This table will highlight what products can and can’t be used for OPD:
 

Product Type
Does OPD +/- 10% rules apply?

Yes
No

POMs
✔
__

Non-POMs including P, GSL and non-medicines (i.e. ACBS products, food supplements, cosmetics, toiletries etc)
✔
__

Schedule 5 Controlled Drugs
✔
__

Part IX Appliances
__
✔

Controlled Drugs in Schedules 1-4
__
✔

Special containers
__
✔

Unlicensed specials (Part VIIIB, Part VIIID and non-Tariff specials)
__
✔

Products supplied in accordance with SSPs
__
✔

Medicines supplied in accordance with PGDs
__
✔

 
New Features Planned from Jan 2025

Organisation Setting for OPD Activation

A new toggle under the Dispensing tab in the settings screen allows you to enable or disable OPD functionality.

Patient-Level OPD Exclusions

A new patient tag to exclude specific patients entirely from OPD rule processing.
A checkbox added to individual patient therapies allows the exclusion of specific medications from OPD processing.

Labelling and Quantity Adjustments

When labelling:

If the scanned (or manually entered) pack quantity is within ±10% of the total prescribed quantity, the label quantity automatically updates to the scanned quantity.

Example: If 28 tablets are prescribed and a pack of 30 is scanned, the quantity updates to 30 as it is within 10%.
This adjustment is badged or highlighted on the label (e.g., similar to “SC” for Special Container).

If the scanned quantity exceeds the ±10% range, the system proceeds with the split pack process.

Exclusion Categories

OPD applies to all POMs except:

Schedule 1–4 Controlled Drugs (CDs).
Sodium Valproate-containing medications (unless a risk assessment allows otherwise).
Unlicensed medications, special containers, products under Serious Shortage Protocol (SSP), PGDs, appliances, and sub-packs.

Implementation Details

Rounding Rules

The ±10% calculation does not adhere to normal rounding rules:

.5 and below rounds down.
Above .5 rounds up.

User Interface Changes

Addition of OPD toggle in the settings screen to activate/deactivate OPD.
New patient tags and checkboxes for therapy exclusions.
Label adjustments and badging for OPD-specific changes.

Operational Scope

OPD functionality is limited to EPS Prescriptions and Private Prescriptions  

OPD should not apply to MDS dispensing.

This update will introduce functionality to enable and manage OPD while maintaining regulatory compliance and supporting pharmacy workflows. The changes enhance flexibility in dispensing, ensure patient safety through exclusion options, and simplify processes with clear automation and labelling adjustments.

Important Note
Although regulations state that OPD should not be used for SSP items, TITAN will allow the dispensing of +/- 10% for SSPs. This will be patched in an upcoming release.

articles.title: Owings
articles.content:
Original Pack Dispensing also applies to the dispensing of Owed items.
Scenario: 
- You have a prescription for 56 x Cetirizine 10mg Tablets 
- Cetirizine 10mg Tablets come in boxes of 30 Tablets 
- You provide one box of 30, and set the remaining label as an Owing 
- You dispense the remaining 26 tablets
- You are permitted to dispense a pack 30 against the owed 26, despite this being more than a 10% difference between the amount owed and the amount you just dispensed
 
This is permitted because the total now dispensed is 60, which is within 10% of the prescribed quantity (56).

articles.title: Payment
articles.content:
The BSA will pay you for the pack size that has been dispensed as long as it is within 10% of the prescription quantity, is a qualifying product, and is in the original pack (e.g. an original pack of 30 tablets were dispensed against a prescription for 28) 
 
This is regardless of whether or not you have turned on OPD in settings, as it is set out in legislation. 
There are no endorsements required for OPD (neither automatically, or manually applied), as the BSA will simply look at the quantity prescribed and dispensed. 
 
The OPD setting in TITAN only controls if TITAN will do within the User Interface.

articles.title: Under-Allocation
articles.content:
There may be instances where you are required to provide less than the prescribed amount of medication to be able to provide the original pack to a patient under OPD rules. As it currently stands, the process for under-allocation of items that qualify for OPD is as follows: If the Original Pack quantity is less than that of the prescribed amount (e.g. the prescription states 30 Tablets, and the Original Pack is 28), as it falls within the +/- 10% scope of OPD Dispensing - You must mark the remaining label of 2 Tablets as 'Not Dispensed'. 
 
This is not an automatic process as under-allocation of medication requires the involvement of the pharmacist, and is ultimately at the said pharmacist's discretion.

articles.title: Video
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Hello everybody and welcome to another quick Titan video. This time, OPD— or original pack dispensing. OPD is coming in with all the new legislation on the 1st of January, 2025. It's gonna be available from version 2.4, 2.2, and above. It won't be activated until the first, so if you are running this version before then, don't worry—it's not gonna be active now. So I guess we should start with what OPD is. The key features really: Pharmacists must consider dispensing up to 10% more or less than the prescribed quantity if it enables them to dispense in the original manufacturer's pack. Professional judgment is required, so that means it may not be suitable in some circumstances. For example, if you have some antibiotics or steroids where there's a short course, it is probably gonna be appropriate to dispense the prescribed quantity, which is likely to equal the length of the course rather than the full box, which may encourage the patient to take more medication than necessary. The main purpose of OPD is about improving patient safety. If you dispense a medicine in the original pack, the patient has the information leaflet, they know the manufacturer, the expiry date, and the batch number. By not opening up the pack, you're reducing the chances of contamination or losing a tablet. So it can make things a little safer. Furthermore, it's gonna increase pharmacy efficiency by reducing the need for repackaging medicines, saving staff time. Eligibility: Prescription-only medicines and EPS England and Wales only. That means no P medicines or GSL, most appliances are not covered, and OPD cannot be used for: Schedule 1 to 4 controlled drugs Unlicensed specials, SSPs, or PGDs. Moving on to Titan itself— very straightforward on the first. If you go into your settings, you'll see under the miscellaneous section that the "Allow original pack dispensing" toggle will have been turned on automatically. For dispensing, just scan the pack as usual. If the product qualifies, a label will automatically be produced detailing the pack quantity instead of the prescription quantity. You'll see on-screen, on the little green or red square, an "OP" badge confirming it’s an OPD item. No clinical checks, no final checks required. No extra endorsements to worry about— Titan handles everything, so you're in safe hands. If you want to turn off OPD for a particular item, go into the patient's complete view, find the patient therapy tab, look for the item, edit it, and check "Exclude from OPD." To turn it off for an entire patient, this is done within patient tags. You could create a new tag called "Exclude from OPD" or use an existing one like "DOTS." Within the tag manager under the workflow section, toggle "Exclude from OPD" on, and any patient with that tag won't receive OPD dispensing. That's it—very straightforward. Any questions or comments, please get in touch. The help desk is available and happy to assist. Thanks very much. Bye-bye.

articles.title: Video
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
The Titan Owings module is designed to help you to manage your owings more effectively. It enables you to bulk dispense or nd any mix of your existing owings all in one go. To make the most out of this feature, it is important to make sure that all of your out-of-stock items are sent to owing during the labeling stage. If you are out of stock of a particular item when you're dispensing, even if you have already ordered the stock in, or if you are not expecting the patient for a few more days, it's best practice to send the items straight to owing. Just click the round menu button and hit the owing button. There's no need to keep the owing label in the basket for your reference. Now that you are sure that all items that were unavailable at the labeling stage have been sent to owing, we can now start to make use of the Owings view. The first thing to do, though, is to set up your print profiles. Just go to settings and click into print profiles. From there, set up your batch picking label to use the same profile as your dispensing label and the A4 batch picking list to use the same profile as your backing cards or MAR charts. Now we can start dispensing some owings. To begin, go to the view screen and open the Owings tab. From here, you can see a list of all the owings in your pharmacy. Although you are still able to dispense one at a time from the labeling screen as normal, you can now create a batch of owings from here. As most of our users now use batch flow, you will be familiar with this process, but you do need to understand that this is slightly different in that the owings batch will not remove the items from the current prescription location in the board. Owings batch is completely separate from the prescription board and does not change the item location. To begin, just filter the screen as needed. For example, you may have just got a delivery of an item that's been unavailable for some time, and so you want to dispense them all in one go. Once you've identified all the items that you want to add to the owings batch, tick them all one at a time or with the select all button and click Create Owings Batch. A screen will now open that allows you to choose a name for that batch. Then choose how you want to print the picking list. You can use A4, a label, or Eden. A picking label will be printed along with your basket labels. The new owing batch will be created and will show on the left-hand side. Just click it to see the content. Then start picking the required items into a basket or a tote. If you use Edo, scan the picking label into your patient screen to allow you to check the items off as you go. Layout and label one basket for each patient, and then either scan the picking label or click labeling to get started. Scan your first item, basket one, stick the label on the item, and then place it into the basket as per the audible prompt or the number printed on the dispensing label. Once you've labeled all the picked items, just package them up as normal. Back on the owing screen, we can now take a look at some of the other features. You can add notes to items in bulk. Just tick the required items and click add note. Write your note and then click OK. View the note at any time by clicking on the item to access the patient flyout. You are able to add and edit statuses from the status column to help you to keep track of things, and you can use these statuses to filter the board. You can also use the owing period filter to filter by prescription date. Another great feature is the ability to bulk mark owings as not dispensed. This will help you to make sure you can claim the dispensed items on any prescriptions that had owings before they expire. And that's it! We really hope you like this new feature.

articles.title: Do I Need to Keep My Smartcard in?
articles.content:
To initiate a Patient Insights Nomination Check, a Smart Card must be inserted and authenticated on any terminal within the pharmacy. It does not need to be the terminal you are directly using to trigger the check.
 
During a patient insights check, if a user removes their smart card after the request has been successfully sent (indicated by the appearance of the blue toast notification), the process will still continue without issue. At that stage, the necessary credentials have already been transmitted, and the service will proceed with processing based on the current or most recent authenticated session.
 
Therefore, it is safe to remove the smart card once the blue toast appears

articles.title: Is There a Way to Highlight Gained or Lost Patients?
articles.content:
Using Patient Insights reveals which of your patients who have sent you a prescription within the last six months are currently nominated to which pharmacies. If they are in the list, then you have received a prescription from them within the last six months and you haven’t removed them manually (as you should do if the patient has confirmed that they have intentionally moved to another pharmacy).
 
Try grouping by pharmacy name to see clearly which patients are at which pharmacies. Patients not registered to your pharmacy can be considered "lost" (they are patients that you have dispenses for before but are not currently nominated to you).
 
To see a list of gained patients, go to the Patient List report. This report logs patient registration dates. You would need to export to Excel to count everything from, say, last month.
 
View patients who have been lost to pharmacies

Follow the normal process for doing a Bulk Nomination Check as detailed here.

Review the information on the screen
Consider grouping by Pharmacy Name if you want to see a clear list of who is at what pharmacy

 
See a list of gained patients:

Go to Views

Download and open the report
Click the "Registered Date" column header
Sort descending (Z - A)

Io another video for you today. And this time it's about a fantastic feature called Patient Insights. Patient Insights is an incredibly useful tool for bulk checking patient nominations. With Patient Insights, you can easily see which patients are still nominated to your pharmacy and which ones have switched. With their permission, you can update the nomination right back to you. It's simple, it's powerful, and yes, it's great for your bottom line, so we think you're gonna love it. First things first, just download and install the Patient Insights app from the marketplace as normal. Once installed, you'll see the new Patient Insights tab in the manage patient screen. At the top, you'll see three useful panels. You'll see the last time your nominations were checked, any gains or losses based on patient nomination status before and after your check, and the top five pharmacies that your patients are switching to. The main table displays all active patients. That is any patient who's sent you a prescription within the last six months. A triangle icon will indicate that a patient is no longer nominated to your pharmacy, and you'll be able to see the pharmacy they're currently nominated to and the date of the last check. Want to focus on just tray patients or deliveries, or maybe you've got a tag of the most valuable patients that you want to check more regularly? You can draw down on whatever you need to right here. We've also added a dashboard tile to display a view of patients who were identified as no longer being nominated to your pharmacy during your last check. So let's have a look at how you actually run a check. Firstly, you go to Patient Insights, select all patients, and click bulk check nominations. Patient Insights will run in the background and you can continue to use Titan as normal. When it completes, you'll receive a notification if needed. You can click on any patient that's moved to a different pharmacy, tick their name, and click nominate. One important thing to know here is that the NHS does not allow bulk nominating. So any nomination changes that you want to make must be done individually and of course, with their permission. Also, you can only bulk check a patient once every few days. So plan ahead. What would you do if a patient is permanently lost? Well, you can just click the remove button to tidy up your list and prevent them from appearing here. Again, don't worry— if they do send in a new prescription later on, they'll automatically reappear on the screen. And just a final heads up: This tool runs manually, so you will need to trigger the checks yourself when you are ready. And that's it! Patient Insights helps you stay ahead, stay organized, and stay competitive. You're now ready to take control of your patient nominations smarter, faster, and more efficiently than ever before.

articles.title: What Do the Numbers Next to the Top 5 Pharmacies Represent?
articles.content: In Patient Insights, the numbers displayed next to the Top 5 Pharmacies represent the number of patients who had those specific pharmacies nominated as their preferred pharmacy at the time of the last Bulk Nomination Check. These figures indicate how many patients from your selected cohort are currently assigned to each of the listed pharmacies.

articles.title: What Do the Numbers in the Patient Section Mean?
articles.content:
After running a Bulk Nominations Check, you will see some statistics added to the Patient Card in the top centre of the screen.
The nomination check produces three key figures:

Checked refers to the total number of patients assessed during the last run (this could be less than the number you selected if some of those were checked within the last 24h, or if they are missing the minimum demographic data required to access their Spine record, such as the NHS number)

Lost counts how many of those patients were showing in Patient Insights as nominated to your pharmacy before the last Patient Insights check but are no longer showing as such after the last check.

Gained counts how many patients were showing as not nominated to your pharmacy before the last Patient Insights check and are now showing as nominated since your last check

IMPORTANT
When assessing whether patients have been lost or gained, Patient Insights simply compares the most recent Bulk Check with the previous one. It does not take into account any nominated prescriptions received, or any manual nomination checks that may have taken place in the interim period.
 
These numbers are always based solely on values help in Patient Insights before and after the most recent check, and the values must satisfy the formula:
Lost + Gained + No Change = Checked.

articles.title: What Does the Warning Triangle/Exclamation Mark Mean?
articles.content:
If you see a warning triangle/exclamation mark, this means that the patient was not nominated to your pharmacy at the time of the last Bulk Nomination Check.

They will either be:

Nominated to another pharmacy (see the Pharmacy Name column in the main table)or
They have no nomination at all

articles.title: Criteria for Duplicate Patients
articles.content:
The following data must be exactly the same on both patient records for a patient to be recorded as a duplicate:
TitleForenameSurnameDOBGender

Mobile App User Guide(Version 2.1)
Downloadable Link
Contents
3. Introduction & device compatibility4. Downloading & updating the PharmAppy app5. Registration7. Login8. Forgotten password9. Placing a request11. Tracking your order12. Adding a dependant14. Updating your medication15. Updating your information16. Contact

Introduction
The PharmAppy app (version 2.1) allows you to effortlessly order, track and manage medication for yourself and/or those you care for, and connect with your pharmacy.
 
Device Compatibility
This App requires an iOS device on iOS 13 or later, or Android device, both with a minimum of 120mb of memory and the iOS or Android operating systems. ONLY stock operating systems distributed by these manufacturers are permitted. For example, iOS devices that have been jailbroken or Android devices that have been rooted are NOT permitted to use this App or Service.
Downloading & updating the PharmAppy app
The PharmAppy app can be downloaded on both the App Store (iOS devices) and Google Play Store(Android devices). To find the app, simply search ‘pharmappy’ and download it for free.
The App will regularly be updated. When an update is available, you will be able to download the newversion through the App Store (iOS devices) or Google Play Store (Android devices).Keep your automatic updates turned on to ensure you’re always on the latest version and canexperience the most up-to-date features.
 
Registration (Part 1)
Once you’ve downloaded and opened the PharmAppy app, tap the ‘Continue to NHS login’ button andcreate or log in to your NHS account. Then, your pharmacy & medication will be pulled straight in.

Registration (Part 2)
Once you’ve confirmed the information pulled from your NHS medication record, you simply need toagree to our Ts & Cs and Privacy Policy before continuing through to your account.

Login
To log in to the PharmAppy app, simply tap ‘Continue to NHS login’, and enter the email and passwordyou use to access your NHS login account.

Forgotten password
To reset your password using NHS login, simply tap ‘Reset your password’. You’ll then be sent an emailwith a link to choose your new password. Once done, simply enter your new password to log in.

Placing a request (part 1)
To place a request for your medication, from the ‘Request’ tab, simply tap ‘Start Request’, select themedicines you’d like, tap ‘Request’ and then review the items you’ve selected are correct before continuing.

Placing a request (part 2)
Once you’ve confirmed the items you selected are correct and have placed your request with your GP,you’ll begin the tracking process, where you’ll be able to see the status of each of your items.

Tracking your order
When your items are approved by your GP, your order will arrive with your pharmacy. You’ll bekept up to date where each item is every step of the way with complete visibility throughout.

Adding a dependant (part 1)
To add someone you care for, from the ‘Request’ tab, simply tap the ‘+’ icon and enter their unique code and DOB. This would have been sent to them via SMS or email, but if they haven’t received this, you can request it from their pharmacy. Once entered, it will automatically pull in their pharmacy and medication.

Adding a dependant (part 2)
Once you’ve confirmed that your dependant’s information that’s been pulled in is correct, you’ll simplychoose their relation to you and finally review all their details are correct before adding them.

Updating your medication
Talk to your GP surgery to update your medication. As and when they update your record on theirsystem, pull down from the middle of the ‘Request’ tab and you’ll see your up-to-date medicines list.

Updating your information
To update the email and phone number linked to your account, from the ‘Account’ tab, tap on the pen toedit these details. You’ll then be redirected to NHS login to update your record which will update the app.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
If you have any questions about the features in the app, you canemail patientsupport@pharmappy.com.
Alternatively, if you’d like to provide feedback, you can do so herepatientfeedback@pharmappy.com.
Our team are always on hand to help, ensuring you receive the highest quality of service and consistently improving your experience using PharmAppy.

articles.title: Set Up & Use
articles.content:
Overview Power BI is an analytical software created by Microsoft. We utilise this software to bring you detailed pharmacy performance data.  Information about clinical checks, labelling and packaging, staff performance, near misses, breakdowns of prescriptions dispensed and much more is available.  The data shown in Power BI always reflects yesterday and earlier; today's data will not be visible until tomorrow. Each report gives valuable insights and can be filtered or drilled into for more detail.  Set Up / Activation 
Click in to Marketplace

Select Power BI App from list of available Apps
Select the price button
Accept the EULA

 After this, you will receive an email from TITAN containing: 
Your login details
A link to your Power BI report
A webinar recording that takes you through the key Power BI features and how to make the most of your data
 Available Reports  Below is a breakdown of each available report: Performance Reports Daily ScorecardA quick glance summary of key KPIs for your site compared to successful pharmacies. Highlights your performance vs the expected benchmark and helps you identify areas for improvement. These stats are from the day before today. For example, if you checked the Scorecard on 22/07, the data shown will be for 21/07. You cannot filter this data. If you wish to see similar data to this report for a particular day, please navigate to the Weekly Stats Report section of this help file.   Daily Report A breakdown of your site's stats for the previous day. Includes key metrics across different areas like dispensing, labelling, and clinical checks. These stats are from the day before today. For example, if you checked the Scorecard on 22/07, the data shown will be for 21/07. You cannot filter this data. If you wish to see similar data to this report for a particular day, please navigate to the Weekly Stats Report section of this help file.  No image shown as it is a scrolling report. Weekly Stats Report Summarises pharmacy performance across the previous week. Useful for spotting trends, issues, or improvements across the week. These stats are from the previous week. For example, if you check the report on Wednesday 23/07, the data shown is for the week commencing the Monday prior. That would be from 14/07 to 18/07. You can also use the filters on this screen to one a particular day, which is useful as you cannot filter the daily reports. This report is also interactive. For example, click on the items packaged on the Wednesday (under Items Package by Day). The report will auto-filter to only show you data for prescriptions that were packaged on the Wednesday. To get the report to revert back to normal, click on the Wednesday data again.  Month to Date Ongoing summary of all key metrics from the start of the current month up to yesterday. Helps monitor mid-month progress. The data in this report is based on Prescription arrival.  Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report.  This report is also interactive. For example, click on the items packaged on the 14th. The report will auto-filter to only show you data for prescriptions that were packaged on the 14th.  To get the report to revert to normal, click on the 14th again.  Month's Review with Filters Provides a full-month view of performance data, with filters to help drill into specific areas like date ranges, staff, tags, or task types. The data in this report is based on Prescription Arrival.  Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Arrival Time 
Label Packaged
Handed Out  
This report is also interactive. For example, click on the items packaged on the 14th. The report will auto-filter to only show you data for prescriptions that were packaged on the 14th.  To get the report to revert to normal, click on the 14th again.  General Reports GENERAL – Baseline Stats High-level data across the site. Good for identifying general performance levels and consistency. This data is based on prescription arrival.  Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Arrival Time
Patient Tags 
This report is also interactive. For example, click on the items received on Wednesday (Items by day section). The report will auto-filter to only show you data for prescriptions that were received on Wednesday.  To get the report to revert to normal, click on Wednesday data again.  GENERAL – Tag Analysis Analysis of patient tags used during the month (e.g., delivery, compliance, blister). Helps understand the volume and type of patients being supported. This data is based on prescription labelling.  Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Label Packaged Date
Scan Status 
Patient tags  
This report is also interactive. For example, click on the volume for a certain tag (under Rx Volume By Tag). The report will auto-filter to only show you data for prescriptions that were tagged with said tag.  To get the report to revert to normal, click on the tag again.  GENERAL – Dispensed Volume Analysis Tracks the number of items dispensed, giving insight into pharmacy workload and output volume. This data is based on prescription labelling.  Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Route of Administration
Month
Year
Label Printed Date
Written as  
This report is also interactive. For example, click on the Amlodipine 10mg tablets (in drug details), and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected drug. To get the report to revert to normal, click on Amlodipine 10mg tablets again.  Safety & Accuracy Reports SAFETY – Staff Barcode Performance Measures how well staff are scanning GTIN/FMD barcodes (on product labelling). Helps identify who may be missing scans or causing dispensing accuracy issues. The data is based on prescription labelling. Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Label Printed Date
Scan Status 
Patient Tags 
This report is also interactive. For example, click on a staff member's name (in Label Printed By), and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected staff member. To get the report to revert to normal, click on the staff member's name again.  SAFETY – Tag Barcode Performance Analyses GTIN/FMD barcode scanning at the tag level (i.e. across specific patients), helping identify gaps in scanning compliance. Data is based on prescription packaging in the last 3 months. Filters on the right hand side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Label Printed Date
Scan Status 
Patient Tags 
This report is also interactive. For example, click on a patient tag (in Patient Tags in the middle), and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected patient tag. To get the report to revert to normal, click on the patient tag again.  SAFETY – Drug Barcode Performance Tracks how often the correct drug barcode (GTIN/FMD) is scanned during dispensing. Helps identify accuracy issues, ensures the right product is selected, and supports audit and safety compliance. Data is based on prescription labelling in the last 3 months. Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Label Printed Date
D Label Week Number
Scan Status 
Patient Tags 
This report is also interactive. For example, click on a drug name (under Witten As), and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected drug. To get the report to revert back to normal, click on the drug again.   SAFETY – Needs Check Item Overview Looks at how items marked as “Needs Check” are being handled. Useful for reviewing accuracy and clinical safety processes. Data is based on prescription packaging in the last 3 months. Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Label Printed Date
Week 
This report is also interactive. For example, click on a drug name (under Witten As), and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected drug. To get the report to revert back to normal, click on the drug again.  SAFETY – Batch Overview Breakdown of batch numbers scanned during the dispensing process. Useful for tracing product batches for recalls or audits. Data is based on prescription packaging in the last 3 months. Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report.  This report is also interactive. For example, click on week 27 (under Checks by package week), and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected week. To get the report to revert to normal, click on the week again.  SAFETY – Invalid Item Scan Overview Shows how often products are scanned that don’t match expected GTIN/FMD codes. Helps catch scanning or stock issues. Data is based on prescription packaging in the last 3 months. Filters on the right side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the Event Time Stamp filter on the right. This report is also interactive. For example, click on a barcode, and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected barcode. To get the report to revert to normal, click on the barcode again.  Process Reviews Clinical Check Review Tracks completed and missed clinical checks on scripts, giving insight into pharmacist workflow and clinical safety adherence. This report excludes bot checks. Filters on the right-hand side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Clinically Checked Date
Check Week Number  
This report is also interactive. For example, click on a staff member (under Count of Items by Checker), and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected staff member. To get the report to revert to normal, click on the staff member again.  Labelling Review Overview of labelling activity. Helps assess volume, timing, and potential bottlenecks in label generation. Filters on the right side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Label Printed Date 
Label Week Number 
Batch Type  
This report is also interactive. For example, click on a staff member (under Count of Packs by Dispenser and Batch type), and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected staff member. To get the report to revert to normal, click on the staff member again. Packaging Review Tracks packaging completion rates and errors. Useful for understanding fulfilment speed and packaging accuracy. Filters on the right side can be used to narrow down the report. You can also use the following built-in filters: 
Label Packaged Date 
Package Week Number 
Batch Type  
This report is also interactive. For example, click on a staff member (under Count of Packs by Packaged by and Batch type), and the report will auto-filter to show only data specific to the selected staff member. To get the report to revert to normal, click on the staff member again.  Tips 
You can filter all reports by team member, date, tag, and more. Click on a graph or figure to drill down into specifics. Great for investigating issues or recognising top performers.
You can also export these reports to save them to your PC or share them with others.

articles.title: Overview
articles.content:
PRIMO Overview The PRIMO process uses an Epson scanner connected to a PC running the PRIMO application to scan prescriptions and send them directly to the Titan prescription inbox for processing. See the video below for a quick overview of the physical setup and workflow.  The scanning process creates an image of the prescriptions, and they are then printed with a unique identification code or letter to distinguish them. Once a good scan is achieved, a green shadow will appear around the prescription. To send these prescriptions to Titan, tap the 'Send to TITAN' button within the app. PRIMO Model  Name & Model: Epson TM-S2000MJ (M274A)Required ink: SJIC18(K) Ink Cartridge Manual: 📄 Download the TM-S2000MJ User's Manual (PDF) Install Guide: How To: Install Primo Frequent Primo Issues Error communicating with Primo Cloud 
Check that the VPN is connected and working.
Also, it could also be that the configuration file is corrupt.
Reapply their current config file again, saved here (C:\TitanReleases\Primo) and see if it fixes the issue. If not, get a new config file from TC and deploy.
It's also common to receive this error if their IP address has changed, this will require whitelisting in our database and permission granted.
 Stuck Prescriptions in the Scanner This can be a result of paper jam or obstruction between the spaces. Therefore, it is suggested to clean and clear the path and reduce the number of scans. Red Prescription Scans 
This can happen because the printed barcode cannot be read either due to smuggled text, text overlap, a fold on the paper, or just unreadable.
The script that causes a red scan should be removed from the pile and inspected. Then, re-scan those scripts until you get a green scan.
 Any Other Issues To troubleshoot any other hardware issues such as error lights, ink errors, power issues; refer to the Epson manual TM-S2000MJ (pages 9-14 and 17-18).

articles.title: Fee Calculation
articles.content:
Click the Settings cog
Click the System Settings tab
Enter the Dispensing Fee. This is the standard fee that is added to all items. 
Enter the Markup Percentage. This is multiplier used on the Drug Tariff price in the pricing equation.
Enter the Minimum Fee. This fee will be used if the result of the pricing equation is lower than this number.

The recommended private prescription fee is calculated as follows: Drug Tariff price per unit multiplied by quantity multiplied by Markup Percentage plus Dispensing fee.
Examples
Dispensing Fee: £2
Markup percentage: 50%
Minimum fee: £9
10p DT price x 30 tablets = £3
£3 x 50% markup = £4.50
£4.50 is less than £9 minimum fee so final price = £9.00

 Tips: 

The pricing calculation is only ever advisory and can be overwritten at the Clinical Checks stage.
This pricing calculation does not affect your reimbursement, which is calculated by the NHSBSA using a different formula. 
The drug tariff price may be looked up by searching for the product in Power Search (F9), or by going to the following NHS website: https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/pharmacies-gp-practices-and-appliance-contractors/drug-tariff/drug-tariff-part-viii

articles.title: Prescription Status Definitions
articles.content: Overview This reference explains the various Prescription Statuses displayed in Titan.Statuses indicate where a prescription is in the workflow - from preparation to handout - and can be used for filtering and tracking progress across the dispensing process. Ready To Check (NotSpecified = 0) Prescription is ready to be clinically checked before moving to the next stage. Ready To Pick (ReadyToPick = 1) Prescription has been approved and is ready for dispensing staff to pick items from the shelf. Ready To Label (ReadyToLabel = 2 / Pending = 3) Prescription items are ready to be labelled.Note: “Pending” may also appear under this display name in some views. Label Printed (LabelPrinted = 4) Labels have been successfully printed and are ready for application. Label Print Failed (LabelPrintFailed = 5) An issue occurred during label printing, the label did not print successfully. This should be retried or checked for printer errors. Owing (Owing = 6) Indicates that part of the prescription is owed to the patient. The remaining quantity will be dispensed once stock is available. Central (SentToCentral = 7) Prescription has been sent to the Central dispensing workflow. Batch (SentToBatch = 8) Prescription has been sent to the Batch dispensing process for bulk handling. Deleted (Deleted = 9) Prescription has been deleted and is no longer active in the workflow. Ready To Package (ReadyToPackage = 10) All items have been picked and labelled; prescription is ready for packaging. Packaged (Packaged = 11) Prescription has been packaged and is ready for final handling. Ready To Hand Out (ReadyToHandOut = 12) Prescription is packaged and ready for collection or delivery. Handed Out (HandedOut = 13) Prescription has been given to the patient or delivery driver. Not Dispensed (NotDispensed = 14) Prescription was not dispensed. Usually used for prescriptions that were cancelled or no longer required. Cancelled (Cancelled = 15) Prescription has been cancelled and removed from active processing. Emergency Supply Reconciliation (EmergencySupplyReconciliation = 16) Used for emergency supply scripts that require reconciliation once a valid prescription is received. Not Started (NotStarted = 17) Used in Methadone workflows to indicate that the prescription has been created but dispensing has not yet begun.

articles.title: Best Practice - Titan PMR Repeat Flow Webinar
Full Video
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Titan are excited to release our latest new feature repeat flow. Repeat flow is designed to help you manage the entire prescription ordering process from start to finish. Ordering through repeat flow will mean that Titan is able to automatically match the prescriptions as they are received with your order. If the items are not received within enough time to be able to dispense the product for your patient, you'll be alerted to this and you'll be able to take the required actions. Repeat flow uses a highly advanced process to calculate exactly when the next repeatable order needs to be placed. The following information is taken into account when doing this, the surgery, opening days and their cutoff times, your pharmacy leads time and your opening days. Patient tag settings via the repeat flow extra turnaround setting, and also whether or not it's a weekend or a bank holiday. There are two types of orders that can be made to repeat flow, ad hoc and repeatable. Ad hoc orders are one off orders and repeatable orders are ones which will automatically be placed at a frequency as set in the patient profile. Let's start by taking a look at the setup process. To begin, you'll need to install the app from the marketplace as normal. Then we just need to configure a few settings. Choose whether or not you block unreconciled prescriptions. If you turn this on, this will mean that prescriptions will only show on the prescription board when all the items have been reconciled in repeat flow. Then we need to choose who we send order reminders to. By default, choose not to send them at all to send 'em to the surgery to send them to the patient or to both. This setting can be overridden. When placing an order, you can then choose how your next due date for future repeatable orders will be calculated. Choose from either the previous order date or the handout date. These last two settings may be overridden on an order by order basis from the repeat flow screen. Lastly, you need to configure the SMS text that will be sent to your patients that order their own items to tell them that it's time to place their order. Now you can configure your main pharmacy settings. Let's start by setting up your pharmacy opening days. Just go into the main setting screen and toggle on your normal opening days. Then we're going to go into clinical settings and from here we can set tight into automatically archive certain items if they've not been dispensed for a specific period of time. You can configure a different time period for chronic items, acute items, and for antibiotics and antivirals. Next, we need to set up our surgeries. We can search for any surgery in the system from power search and hit the edit pencil to set it up, but we've also added a handy surgeries view that allows you to see all the surgeries linked to your patients. From here, you can see if a surgery has been fully set up or not from looking at the checkbox To set up a surgery, just click on the surgery's name. From here, there are some key fields that we need to configure. If you want to be able to request orders and send chasers by email, be sure to add an email address as the contact. Next, you'll need to specify how you want to send the orders. You can print a repeat letter or send it by email, or you can print off tokens for ticking side B and sending to the surgery. If the surgery does not accept orders from your pharmacy, set this to patient only. The next important field to set up is days to prepare. Configuring. This will ensure the orders are sent in time for them to process. Finally, set the opening days and order cutoff times. Again, this will be used to calculate when the order needs to be sent to the surgery. When you're done, just hit save and you'll see that the setup completes checkbox has now been ticked automatically. The source of the list of surgeries is the patient's record. Depending on your settings, Titan will automatically add surgery information to your patient when prescriptions are downloaded or scanned in. However, if a surgery is missing from this list, you can either add it from the patient's complete view or from the power search menu. Some surgery settings can be overridden at an item level, so for example, you could set a surgery order method to be NHS email, but then set one item in patient therapy to be managed by the patient. And that's it. The setup is now complete. Let's start by taking a look at the repeat flow screen. The repeat flow board is designed to look a lot like the prescription board, so you should find it very easy to use. Just like the prescription board, the screen is made up of different cards in different columns. There are specific cards for each batch of orders. Normally, there'll be one card for each patient, although some patients may have multiple cards if they have items that have been set up with different order intervals. For example, a patient may have three items that are ordered every 28 days and also one item that's ordered every week. These would show on two separate cards. Ad hoc orders are also shown on separate cards. On the left hand side, we have the future orders column. This column list all the repeatable orders that have been scheduled. Just click on one of the orders to edit it. The actions column details any orders that are due to be placed, but there are some outstanding actions that need to be taken before this can be done. The specific actions will be highlighted in red and can be filtered out and processed in bulk. The most common actions that you're likely to see will be for things like where the surgery has not been set up for a patient, where the surgery's email is missing, where you need to print the token B side in your pharmacy, or if the order form has been set to be printed locally. A full list of actions is available in the help center and are shown on screen. Now. Just pause the video if you want to take a moment to read them. Moving on, the requested column lists all orders that have been successfully placed. Orders will remain in this column until the pharmacy due date. That's the date that you need to have the prescription in your pharmacy by to be able to dispense in time for the patient's due date. Next is the chasing admin column. Orders in this column will show if either the items ordered have not been received by the pharmacy due date or if prescriptions for new items have been received that have been partially matched to the order items rather than being a full match. Items in this column will have one of three statuses. The arrived status refers to items that are an exact match with the ordered items. The new status refers to items that are partially matched with the ordered items. And the waiting status refers to items that have been ordered but not yet received at all. For an item to qualify as a new partially matched item, they must be in either the same VMP category, the same VTM category, or the same BNF category. It's worth recognizing at this point that order matching can only happen if the prescription has been fully matched to the patient. Therefore, if the prescription is not fully matched to the patient's record at download, you will need to complete the patient matching during your clinical check before the order matching can take place. Finally, the completed column will show all orders that have been fully accounted for. Each item in the orders in this column has been fully matched to received prescriptions or has been canceled. Orders are removed from this column after seven days. Let's take a look at how we set up a repeatable order. To begin, search for the patient and navigate to the patient therapy screen as normal. Choose one of the items that you want to be able to order in the future and click the edit pencil. From here, you'll just need to configure a few fields. Click into the cycle days box. Then you'll need to select the order frequency that the patient requires. Let's set this item to have an automatic order every twenty-eight days. Next, we need to choose who will manage or place the order. If this is left as unassigned, then you will not be able to order this item. Then you need to record if the item is acute or chronic. We've also added the ability to add a note that will show on the order letter or the repeat letter at this point. Finally, if your patient has an item infrequently but long-term, you could choose to exclude the item from auto archive in your main setting screen. The last thing to do is to make sure that your patients are kept up to date as new items are added to the therapy. To do this, you need to make sure that the patient has a serviced patient tag. This will ensure that if new items are added to the patient therapy from a new prescription or if there's been a dose change on that prescription, a clinical check will prompt the pharmacist to ensure that the order preferences are updated. There's also a new tag setting which allows you to add extra days into the processing lead time for any patients with that tag. Now let's look at creating the repeatable order from the repeat flow screen. Start by clicking the create request button in the top right corner, or you can hit F1 from any screen. Search for the patient as normal. Then set the order type to repeatable. And then choose the cycle length which you are creating the order for. For example, selecting twenty-eight will show you all of the items that you've set to a twenty-eight day cycle in patient therapy. Then you need to set the initial due date that the patient would like to receive the items by. Next, we need to choose which items we actually want to order. If the item you want to order isn't on the list, this is because the item either has a different repeat order interval to what you've selected or because it's a new item that isn't yet in the patient therapy. If this is the case, just click the plus button to add it to the patient therapy. We now have the opportunity to override the pharmacy settings for this particular order if we want to. I'm going to decide to only send reminders to the surgery and to calculate the next due date based on the handout date. Finally, we're going to add a comment to repeat order to request that the patient is prescribed tablets instead of capsules. Then just click add request, and the order has been successfully set up. The order will now show on the repeat flow screen. On the morning of the scheduled order date, depending on the item settings, the order will appear in actions to allow you to manually print the token or the repeat letter. Alternatively, if the order is due to be placed by email or SMS, it'll automatically be sent. After the actions are completed or the order has been sent, it will then progress to the requested column. Once all items are received, matched or canceled, the card will move to the completed column. If, on the other hand, some of the items were not received by the pharmacy due date or if similar but different items were received, the order will automatically move to the chasing admin column where you will need to manually match the items received to the ordered items. Send a reminder to the surgery or patient. Or cancel the outstanding items. Repeat orders can be edited by clicking on the card in the first column. From here, you can edit the reminder and next order date preferences. And add new comments. You can also add them to the order letter and emails. Now let's have a look at ad hoc orders. If a patient requests a one-off order, you can place an ad hoc order from the ad requests. Flyout access the flyout from the patient's power search window. By clicking the ad requests button in the repeat flow screen or by clicking F1. From here, all you need to do is select the items that you wish to order. You can edit the anticipated date if the item order is not needed until later. And you can choose if you want to override the surgery's order preferences. Once you've entered all the information, just hit add request. The order will then progress through the columns in exactly the same way as it. Would with a repeatable order. Finally, We need to take a look at how we can send reminders if the prescription is not received in time. If ordered items have not been received by the date that the patient needs it minus the pharmacy turnaround time, then reminders may automatically be sent. The default reminder settings are set in the marketplace but can be overridden when placing the order. In the reminders field, reminders may be sent to both parties if different items are managed by both the surgery and the patient from within the same order. Further to this, It is also possible to send a reminder manually from the order flyout. Just click on the order in either the requested or chasing admin column and hit send reminder. Depending on the settings, The reminder will be sent to either the surgery or the patient or both. You may also decide to manually chase orders, for example, By phoning the surgery. If you do this, Just click the manually chased button on the flyout to record your actions. Doing so will mark the order as manually chased and will move the card to the chased swim lane, and that's repeat flow.

articles.title: Gmail Set Up (Wales ONLY)
articles.content:
Due to Welsh sites unable to use NHSMail, and Outlook for Repeat Flow emails, we have introduced Gmail. Gmail should only be used by Welsh sites; English sites must use an NHSMail application/SMTP enabled account, the guide to set this up can be found here NHS Email SMTP & Application Account Process – Titan PMR
 
In order to set up Gmail for Repeat Flow, please follow the steps below
1. Set up Two Factor Authentication on your account 
Turn on 2-Step Verification - Computer - Google Account Help
 
2. Create an 'App Password' that you will need to use on Titan in System Settings
Sign in with app passwords - Google Account Help
 
3. Log into Titan, and click the settings cog

4. Click 'System Settings'
5. Enter Gmail email address and the App Password that you created in step 2 and output method is set to email

6. Click 'Save Changes'
Your Gmail account to use for Repeat Flow is now ready to be used.

articles.title: How the Order Date is Calculated and How to Change the Settings
articles.content:
The following things are taken into account when calculating when an order needs to be placed to get the required items to your patient in time.

Surgery opening days and ordering cut off times
Pharmacy lead time and opening days
Patient Tag settings via the "RF Extra Turnaround" setting
Weekends and Bank holidays

Surgery opening days and ordering cut off times

Access the edit surgery screen by searching for it in Power Search of clicking on in in Views>Surgeries.
Enter the Days to Prepare. This is how long the surgery needs to issue the prescription.
Toggle on or off the surgery opening days as required.
Enter the Surgery Cut Off times (the time that you need to order by for the prescription to be issued).

Pharmacy lead time and opening days

Go into your main settings.
Toggle on or off your normal opening times.
Toggle on or off if you are open bank holidays (if you open some bank holidays but not others, it's best to leave this off as this will ensure you always order in time).

 
Patient Tag settings via the RF Extra Turnaround setting

Create a new tag.
Turn on RF Extra Turnaround.
Set to the number of days extra that you want to have to process the prescriptions for anyone with this tag.
Assign the tag to the required patients.

articles.title: How to Turn off Reminders
articles.content:
For Active Orders
The only way to stop reminders going out for active orders is to either archive the order or to remove the surgeries email address / patient's number.  
 
For Future Orders:
Delete the order and set it up again with the required settings

Click on the order in the Future Orders column 
Click Archive Order

Create a new order
Set the Reminder Preference as required.

To change your default reminder status for new orders:

Go to the Market Place.

Find the Repeat Flow app under Installed Apps and hit the cog.
Set the Send Reminders as required.

articles.title: Initial Set Up
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

 
NB: If you want to be able to email your surgery's prescription requests from an NHS email account, you will first set up an Application Account. Click here for more info. Install the Repeat Flow app from the Market Place and configure the app settings.

Choose whether or not you block unreconciled prescriptions.

On: Prescriptions will only show on the Prescription Board when all ordered items have been reconciled in Repeat Flow. Until this point, they will be hidden.

Off: Prescriptions will show on the board as soon as they are downloaded.

Choose who Order Reminders default to when placing new orders (this can be overridden when placing the order).

You can then choose how your next due date for your repeatable orders will be calculated. Choose from either the previous order date plus the order frequency or the handout date plus the frequency (this can also be overridden when placing the order).

Set up the SMS message that will be sent to the patient to prompt them to order their meds, if they do the ordering. You can use the following macros within the message to input custom information if you want:

{PatientName} - Shows the patients name 
{MedicationName} - Lists all chronic items separated by commas"Hi, {PatientName}. It is time to order the following items: {MedicationName}, thanks, Peel Green Pharmacy."

Setup your outgoing email address.. Enter your username and password into Settings>System Settings>NHS Email Settings. Ensure you have setup an Application Account and that it has been SMTP enabled.

Pharmacy Settings

Setup your opening times

Settings
Toggle on the normal days that you trade

Setup your Pharmacy Turnaround days. This is how many days you want to have to process the prescription before the patient collects.

Settings
Dispensing settings
Under Dispensing, configure the "Pharmacy turnaround time (in days)" field

Setup auto archiving (this will remove items from active orders).

Settings
Clinical Settings
Under Patient Therapy, set the required values for chronic items, acute items and for antibiotics/antivirals.

Surgery Settings

Search for the surgery by name in PowerSearch and click the edit pencil, or go to Views>Surgeries, find the surgery and click it.
Add the surgeries email address in the Contact Information section if the surgery accepts emails.
Specify how the surgery likes to receive orders. 

NHS Email - TITAN will auto send the order on the required date.
Token Print - TITAN will prompt you to print the token on the required date.
Repeat Letter Print - TITAN will prompt you to print the letter on the required date.
Patient Only - TITAN will send an SMS to the patient prompting them to order their medication on the required date.

Set how long the surgery need to prepare the prescription by entering a value in the "Days to Prepare" field.
Set the surgery opening days. Toggle on or off the days the surgery is open, and then enter the cut off times. If an order is placed after cut-off, this day will not count towards the time required to get the prescription.
The surgery will now be marked as "Complete" in Views>Surgeries.

articles.title: Q and As
articles.content:
When does Chasing Admin send? Orders in the Chasing Admin column resend the order email daily at 10am until a prescription is received or the order is moved out of this status. How often do reminders send? Reminders are sent once per day at 10am while the order remains in the Chasing Admin column. Does the ERD release buffer affect this? No, the ERD release buffer does not affect the Repeat Flow process. How does the Block Prescriptions feature work? If an order contains multiple items and a prescription is received for only one of them: 
The received prescription will be hidden from the Prescription Board.
It will only become visible again once all items on the order are received (or the remaining items are cancelled).
 This prevents partial fulfilment and ensures all items are processed together. What triggers an order to move into Chasing Admin? An order moves into Chasing Admin when it reaches the last day of the surgery turnaround period. This is calculated as: Date patient required medication − Pharmacy turnaround time When should orders show in the Completed Column? For scripts completed AND where the (anticipated) DUE DATE was within the last seven days.  Jan 20th at 12:03 PMRF calculates the last dispensed date based on when an item is physically handed out and does not take into account the ND status of an item, meaning ND does not trigger an update to the last dispensed date.Jan 20th at 11:47 AMThe next order date calculation is item-based. If an active script exists on the prescription board but does not include an item from the future order, the next order date will still be calculated. The system checks when an item in the future order is handed out, and once that occurs, it calculates the new date.Jan 20th at 9:27 AMThe next order date for a future order updates when the first item from the order is dispensed. If a prescription includes only one of the items from the future order (e.g. paracetamol), the next order date is adjusted based on that item's updated dispensing date, regardless of when the remaining items are prescribed.Dec 2nd, 2024 at 4:39 PMFor Repeat Flow to order prescriptions on a 28-day cycle, patient therapies must be set to 28 days. It is not possible to maintain a 7-day cycle in patient therapy while using a 28-day ordering cycle in Repeat Flow.10:44 AMThe Repeat Flow board should provide the option to bulk print B Side Tokens, and it is not limited to Surgery Letters only.Sep 10th, 2024 at 2:02 PMBulk setup of Repeat Flow profiles cannot be done on the back end. The user needs to handle the setup themselves rather than sending a list to TITAN support/developers for processing.10:31 AMThere is currently no option to bring discrepancies to the top of the chased column or filter by discrepancies in Repeat Flow. However, there is a filter available for surgeries.9:41 AMThe "Bulk Print Repeat Documents" function in Repeat Flow prints Surgery Letters and tokens, depending on the order settings.9:46 AMBulk printing in Repeat Flow is only possible if the order was initially created with a print method. The order output cannot be changed once the order is in progress.Aug 13th, 2024 at 10:42 AMRepeat Flow (RF) primarily works with EPS prescriptions and does not automatically match Primo scripts, as they are manual and lack a download link. However, some Primo scripts triggered an arrival message on an RF order, likely because scanning them initiated a download from the spine.12:12 PMAn RF template can be set up on TITAN Mobile (EDO).July 17th, 2024If the turnaround time for repeat flow (RF) orders is changed, only awaiting orders will update automatically. Active orders that have already moved past the "Future Orders" column (such as those in Action, Requested, or Chasing Admin status) will retain the original anticipated date based on the previous turnaround time. However, the reminder message timing will adjust accordingly—if the turnaround time is reduced, reminders will be sent closer to the anticipated date (e.g., from 4 days before to 2 days before at 10am). The audit can be checked to confirm if reminders are resending.July 5th, 2024If a patient’s preferred contact is not set, notifications may not work correctly. The system requires a mobile number, as landlines are not supported. The preferred contact must also have "Allow Notifications" enabled.10:04 AMWhen repeat flow is set to send reminders to both the patient and the surgery, the system does not notify the patient when an order has been placed. Instead, it only sends a reminder if the pharmacy has not received the items back. If the pharmacy does not receive the items, the patient is reminded to place the order themselves. The audit log can be checked to review the reminder message content.June 18th, 2024If a surgery does not accept emails, repeat flow (RF) can still be used by selecting an alternative order method in the surgery settings. If "Token Print" is chosen, RF will prompt the user to print the slip, which can then be given to the surgery manually.May 2nd, 2024If a surgery setup displays incorrectly and is causing order delays, it may be due to duplicated surgery opening times. This issue requires resolution via a third-line support ticket to remove the duplicate entries.April 30th, 2024On the repeat flow board, the "Future Orders" and "Completed Orders" columns are collapsed by default, while all other columns remain open. There is currently no option to modify this behaviour.April 25th, 2024To set the order preference in Repeat Flow, it should be configured within the surgery details. If the correct settings appear in place but the preference still shows as "unknown," possible causes include a duplicate surgery entry that is not properly set up. If no duplicates are found, removing and re-adding the surgery to the patient record may help. If the issue persists, a support ticket should be created for further investigation.April 18th, 2024Ad-hoc orders cannot be placed if there is already an existing order that has moved past the "Future Orders" column, regardless of whether it was created as a repeatable or ad-hoc order. If an order is already in the "Requested" column, the system will prevent an additional ad-hoc order from being added.April 11th, 2024Orders set to print move to the "Action" column at different times depending on their type. Ad-hoc orders move immediately, while future orders transition at 10am on the day they are due. This timing is standard across all pharmacies and cannot be changed for individual sites. If an order appears in the audit as moved at 10:03am but does not display until later in the afternoon, this is unexpected behaviour and should be investigated further. A support ticket should be raised if the issue persists.April 10th, 2024If the next order date is blank while the order date is visible on the card, it may be due to the order being set to base its next date on handout. In this case, the next order date will not populate until the order is handed out. For first-time Repeat Flow (RF) users, the date should typically be based on the initially set order date unless changed during setup.If the repeatable order is set for today, a card may appear in both the "Future Orders" and "Actions/Requested" columns, depending on the selected order method.March 6th, 2024Repeat Flow (RF) orders continue to be processed regardless of a patient's deceased status. The system does not automatically prevent orders from being requested for deceased patients. Manual intervention may be required to stop orders from being generated.February 16th, 2024Auto-chase in Repeat Flow (RF) can be turned off by setting reminders to "No Reminders." This option is available in Marketplace settings and can also be selected when placing an individual order. The Marketplace setting only affects the default value when creating new orders; the chosen setting at the time of order creation will apply to that specific order on a per-order basis.January 3rd, 2024If an archived order still appears in the "Future Orders" column, it is because future orders are considered separate entities from the archived order. Archiving an order does not automatically remove its corresponding future orders, which will continue to appear unless they are manually addressed.January 3rd, 2024In Repeat Flow (RF), the bin icon removes a specific item from the current order, meaning the order will no longer wait for that item. The cancel button cancels all waiting items in the order, preventing any further reminders. However, actions performed in the "Order Flyout" do not affect future orders. To remove future orders, the bin button must be used within the "Future Order" flyout. The bin icon in the bottom-left corner archives the entire order.January 3rd, 2024If dates are missing from some future orders, it is likely because the order is set to "Calculate next order date on item handout." In this case, the date will only be populated once the previous item has been handed out. 12 DecemberIn Repeat Flow (RF), only items managed by the pharmacy should be emailed to the surgery. If patients marked as "Managed by Patient" in patient therapy, are having their reminders emailed to the surgery despite the order being set for patient reminders only, this is not expected behaviour. It is likely that the orders were created before the items were correctly marked as "Managed by Patient." Ensuring the correct settings are applied before order creation should prevent this issue.27th NovemberIf a site has Repeat Flow (RF) installed, they must use RF to send repeat orders, as the previous functionality is no longer available. However, if RF is not installed, the old repeat ordering functionality should still be accessible. 27th NovemberThere is no prompt when processing prescriptions from the Prescription Board to indicate that items are still awaiting reconciliation. Pharmacies can either enable the 'Block Prescriptions' setting to prevent partially reconciled orders from showing on the board, or continue dispensing freely without restrictions.Oct 24Clicking "Send to Patient" on a Repeat Flow (RF) comment sends the message to the patient instantly. 12/02/2025 11:09 AMRepeat Flow does not detect discrepancies in prescription quantities. If an order is placed for a specific quantity of an item, but the prescription issued is for a different amount, the system will still consider it a match and move the order to completed. The quantity is ignored, and the item will not remain in chasing administration.

articles.title: Safety Features
articles.content:
Repeat Flow Safety Features
Repeat Flow is designed to automate repeat prescription ordering while ensuring safety and preventing over-ordering or duplicate orders. Below are the key safety features built into Repeat Flow:
1. Future Order Already Exists Warning

Repeat Flow prevents duplicate orders by checking if an active future order exists for a patient before allowing a new order.

2. Order Matching and Reconciliation

When a prescription arrives, Repeat Flow automatically matches it to an existing order based on the prescribed medication.
If a prescription does not fully match an order, it moves to the Chasing Admin column for review.

3. Block Unreconciled Prescriptions

Pharmacies can choose to block prescriptions from appearing on the prescription board until they are reconciled with an order.
This ensures that prescriptions are only processed when they have been correctly matched and that all items are dispensed together.

4. Reminders and Alerts

Automated alerts notify users if a prescription is due but has not been received, allowing timely action without duplicate requests.
If an order has been placed but not received by the pharmacy due date, it moves to the Chasing Admin column for follow-up.

5. Patient and Surgery Communication

Repeat Flow can send automated reminders to surgeries and patients, reducing missed orders while preventing unnecessary reorders.
This in turn, massively reduces the likelihood of a patient running out of important medication.
If a prescription is delayed, pharmacies receive notifications to prevent over-ordering.

6. Audit Trail and Tracking

Each prescription request, order placement, and reconciliation is logged in the system, providing a full audit trail for pharmacy staff.
This ensures accountability and allows tracking of any discrepancies.

7. Flexible Ordering Settings

Pharmacies can configure whether the next order is based on the previous order date or the last handout date, ensuring that prescriptions are not ordered too early.
Customisable settings allow orders to be patient-managed or pharmacy-managed, reducing unnecessary orders.

These safeguards ensure that Repeat Flow maintains safe and efficient prescription management, preventing over-ordering and duplicate prescriptions while keeping pharmacies in control of their workflows.

articles.title: Overview
articles.content:
Do you have a robot at your site?
 
Are you thinking about purchasing a robot and wish to see how your TITAN environment would work alongside it?
 
Our robot guide below covers all robot integrations including:

BD Rowa (Vmax, Smart, EasyLoad)

SynMed (XD, ULTRA, Assist)

Avonnex (SINTESI)

Coming Soon:

Omnicell (Medimat)

Willach (Pouch & Picking)

 
The below is a guide to your new TITAN robot screens. 
 
Stock Management Screens:
 
Assembled Packs This is where you can see all of your pre-pack batches, add and edit them, and scan the pre-packs into the system. 
 
There are 7 columns, which shows all essential data (Batch number, Expiry etc).
 
You can use the search functionality on the left hand side to locate the pre-pack you are looking for.
 
You can also filter the individual columns using the filter icons highlighted in blue at the top of the log.
 

 
To find out more about how to use this please follow this link and watch the video. 
 
Robot Stock
 
This screen gives you a live view of every item inside of your robot. 
 
You can 'Sync stock with robot' anytime in this screen, using the blue button at the bottom of the page.
 
Like the screen above, you can use the search functionality on the left hand side to locate the pre-pack you are looking for.
 
You can also filter the individual columns using the filter icons highlighted in blue at the top of the log.
 

 
Robot Flyout (F2)
 
This screen allows you to manually pick the stock you require.
 
Just search for the drug, add the quantity, and hit enter. This will add said drug at said quantity to the list.
You can edit this list using the tick boxes and the grey bin icon.
When you have completed your list, hit the blue 'Pick Items' button at the bottom of the flyout.
 
You can also 'Sync Robot Stock' from this page, using the grey button at the bottom of the flyout. 
 

 
The following screens only apply to:
 

BD Rowa 
Avonnex

 
Main Titan Settings 
 
In the main TITAN settings, under 'Dispensing Settings' there are some Robot Settings.
 
This controls the pick prioity for this particular PC. There is Low, Medium and High.
 
Also controlled here is the chute number drugs arrive to when requested from this PC. 
 
Ensure this is set up on each PC as this is a PC level setting. 

 
Labelling Screen 
 
The labelling screen has lots of robot functionality and indicators. 1. You can see in real time what items have been picked and which haven't using the 'Not Picked'/'Picked' indicators on the right of the drug waiting to be labelled.
These indicators are also next to the compact drug view on the left hand side of the screen. 
 
2. On the left hand side is where you can see if the robot has the drug in stock or not.
Using the example below, you can see the robot was unable to locate any stock for paracetamol, but there are tick boxes next to the other 2 drugs. 
The tick boxes mean that the robot has the stock for that drug. 
 
3. In order to request stock when labelling, tick the boxes on the left hand side of the drugs required, and hit the 'Request stock' blue button at the bottom of the screen. 
 
The stock requested will drop into the shoot selected in your TITAN settings (as per above).
 

 
The following screens only apply to:
 

SynMed 

 
Order Pads
 
The patients that show in your SynMed order pad will have the corresponding SynMed tag, and live prescription(s) on the board to fulfill. 
 
In order for these scripts to be completed by your SynMed robot, ensure all patient therapy is set up correctly. i.e tray/regular
 
Please also ensure all scripts are in parked. 
 
Then when you're ready, hit the blue 'Place order' button. 
 

 
The other page on the order pad is the 'Responses' section.  
 
These are the latest responses for previous orders placed. You can see when orders are 'In progress' or 'Complete'.
 
Once you have a successful 'Complete' message, you are ready to finish off the prescription(s).
 

 

 Tips: 
A step-by-step guide on how to restart your robot can be found through this link. We also have a robot video (specific to BD Rowa) that you may find useful. You can access that by clicking here.
