articles.title: Character Limit and Billing Information
articles.content:
Cost
SMS messages are charged at a fixed rate per 160 characters. You can check your latest invoice for the current charge.
 
SMS length limitations
Campaigns are limited to 320 characters, with a maximum of 2 SMS charges.
There is no limit for other SMSs, such as those sent on assign to shelf or patient order reminders
 
How we calculate the length of your message
A messages length is determined by the total number of characters as displayed on the phone of the person who receives the message.
This includes output of the special syntax. For example, using {collectioncodeurl} in your message will take up 22 characters, rather than the expected 19 due to the length of the URL. Similarly, {collectioncode} will take up 6 characters and {patientinitials} just 2.
  You could incur high charges if you have a particularly long handout message 
To make things easier, we have provided you with a handy character count calculator that will take all this into account.
Click here to have a go

articles.title: Allocating to a Shelf
articles.content:
Introduction
Once the package is finished from the dispensary, the next stage is to put it into a suitable location ready for collection or delivery, or handed out directly to the patient. Titan uses the TITAN Mobile device for helping navigate these steps.
This SOP explains the process of allocating the package to a suitable location.
Scope
Scanning onto shelf, sending text messages, directing the package for delivery or handout
Key Steps

Take the completed package from the dispensary area
Log onto the Titan TITAN Mobile device
Scan the Package barcode
A message will display to tell you what to do with this package

Customer Handout

If the Handout message appears, you will need to proceed to handing it out to the patient - go to SOP 8 - Handout

Delivery Allocation

If the Delivery message appears, you will need to take this to the Delivery area of the pharmacy and put it onto one of the Delivery locations

Fridge/ CD Allocation

If the Fridge or CD message appears, you will need to take this to the Fridge or CD cupboard and put it onto the correct location

Allocating to Shelf

Scan the shelf location you wish to allocate this package to
Repeat from Step 3 for all packages in the dispensary

Tips and Advice

If the patient has registered for Text Message services, a message will be sent to the patient at the point of scanning onto the shelf

The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here: 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1E7nyyJ_RibLiUuJ1U1L_hk2LXxGXs_jhbOn2Ufxbtdo/edit

articles.title: Batch Flow
articles.content:
Process Name
Batch Flow

Purpose

Once the prescription has been clinically checked, the process moves on to Picking. There is a Titan workflow option that allows you to print the stock needed for multiple patients in “Bulk” and to label the medicines for multiple patients thereafter. This option is called “Batch Flow”.
 
The picking list displays the stock that you need for all the prescriptions that you have selected. This list can be printed on an A4 sheet or sent to the Titan Mobile device. You use the picking ist to get the stock that you need for those prescriptions.
 
At labelling stage, the instruction labels are produced per item (rather than per patient) and you are guided to place the labelled items into each appropriate patient basket.At all times Titan displays the percentage complete each patient basket is and if there is an item in the basket that needs an additional accuracy check.
 
This SOP explains the process that needs to be followed for Batch Flow.

Scope
Using Batch Flow for picking and labelling

Responsibility
Pharmacy Staff

Key Steps

Creating a Batch

Go to the prescriptions board.
Click the Bulk toggle at the top of the picking list.
Tick the prescriptions that you want to add to the batch.
Select “Create Batch Flow”.
Enter a name for your batch (this will appear on the Prescription Board card and the picking list).
Choose how you want to print/display the Picking List.
Click Confirm
Your tray labels will now be printed, together with your picking lists or Titan Mobile label

 
Label the baskets

On your bench, set up one basket for each patient.
Label each basket with the labels that have been printed

Pick the stock in bulk
 
Picking list on Titan Mobile
Login to Titan Mobile and scan the Batch Flow Picking Label from the patients screen (you can also scan the normal picking label or sheet)
Start picking each item from the displayed list into a large container such as a delivery tote. Optionally, you can also barcode verify the product at this point using the auto scan feature to ensure that you have selected the correct item.
 
Picking List on labels or A4
Pick each item from the printed list into a large container such as a delivery tote.
Start labelling and distribute into the correct baskets
Pick any item at random from the tote and scan it. A dispensing label will be printed if you have scanned the right item as normal for you to stick onto the box.  Check on screen or on the dispensing label to see which basket to put the packet into. Put the packet into the corresponding basket. Repeat this process until you have labelled all picked items. Once you have labelled all items, click Batch Owing to send any remaining items for the batch to Owing.
 
Accuracy Checking and Packaging
All items must be scanned into the bag from the packaging screen. As normal, dispensers without the “Can package needs check items” permission on their role will not have access to the packaging screen if there is a check due.
If you prefer to have the checks done on TITAN, just put the basket to one side as normal. The ACT/Pharmacist will then be able to scan the basket label to access the labelling screen where they can either Quick Check the items and give them back to the dispenser to package, or they can scan each item into the package, checking as they go.
 
Alternatively accuracy checks can be done on Titan Mobile Quick Check. Checking a batch flow item on Titan Mobile will automatically change the status from Needs Check (red) to Clean (green) without you having to refresh the labelling page. (Titan Mobile menu>Quick Check>scan the picking label>Accept Checks).

Tips/ Advice

Please ensure that your PC has a sound card
You can purchase stackable containers with open access at the front for batch flow.

Related SOPs
See also

Label Stock

 
 

 
 

Office Use Only
 Titan 1.0 

 
Titan steps are shown in blue

articles.title: Clinical Checking of Prescriptions
articles.content:
Introduction
Once all the data entry has been completed, prescriptions must be checked by a pharmacist for clinical safety. Although clinical checks are understood by pharmacists, it is important to understand how Titan works. Essentially, the Clinical Check is a sign off of the prescription to say it is safe to supply. In other words, once the pharmacist confirms they are satisfied with the contents, the only job that follows is to ensure the right drug is supplied to the right patient at the right time. 
As Titan’s workflow allows other members of staff to carry out these jobs effectively, the clinical check may be the last time the pharmacist views this prescription. Therefore the clinical check is very important to get right.
As Titan’s workflow allows other members of staff to carry out these jobs effectively, the clinical check may be the last time the pharmacist views this prescription. Therefore the clinical check is very important to get right.
The clinical check process to be carried out by the pharmacist

To ensure that the prescription is safe to supply to the patient   

To ensure that the prescription is clinically appropriate 
To ensure that the prescription is legally valid 
To ensure that all items prescribed are reimbursable 
To ensure patient concordance and appropriate use of medicines 
To minimise medication errors

Scope
All Prescriptions
Key Steps
Conducting the Assessment

From Titan Prescription Board, select a prescription card to check
Check the validity of the prescription, eg signed, dated, prescription in date. Controlled drug prescriptions must comply with CD requirements (See SOP CD Legalities).

For each prescription image, you will be presented with a list of items. Each item will have a set of clinical checks for review by the pharmacist including the following: 

Interactions and warnings
If the dosage is within prescribed range
If there are any medical conditions to consider
Possible side effects and risks of adverse reactions
Over ordering of medicines
A high-risk medicine eg Methotrexate, see below
If the patient has a similar drug that can be classed as therapeutic duplication
If prescription date has expired
If the prescription was dispensed in the last 7 days
If the patient has an allergy
If the drug is susceptible to data entry error
NHS black listed item
Drugs requiring “SLS” endorsements
If the manufacturer cannot supply the item
Extra endorsing

Pharmacist has the ability to leave notes against the prescription for future reference or to display on TITAN Mobile 
Pharmacist to confirm that they have clinically checked the prescription by pressing Save
You can now move to next prescription check by pressing “Save and Next” or press “Save and Exit” to go back to the Prescription board
Prescription will now have moved to the next stage of Picking Stock

Tips and Advice

Always work in priority order when selecting cards
If you choose not to dispense a prescription you can press ND

The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here: 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/17TKfD8HAD1jNLo2Jw2P5OsmYlS8J6iWYuQGvxpvKglo/edit

articles.title: Data Entry
articles.content:
Introduction
Data entry is the process whereby the information written on a prescription is transferred into Titan. The process varies depending on how the prescription has arrived so far. This SOP explains the various ways in which prescriptions can be entered ready for the clinical check.
Titan allows data entry to be separated from the Clinical Check stage. This means that junior staff can enter the details in readiness for a pharmacist to reduce pharmacist time and involvement. However, if a pharmacist enters the details then they can conduct the clinical check simultaneously.
Scope
Ensuring the details of all prescriptions are entered and completed ready for clinical checking. Includes; Primo Rx, Power Mail, manually entered Rx, Welsh 2D Rx, EPS Rx
Key Steps
Manual Entry - no image in TITAN

Take Prescription from basket
On Titan Prescription Board, select New Rx
Select Type of Rx (e.g. private, FP10, Dentist etc)
Enter all details of Rx

Power Mail / Primo Scanned Prescriptions

Primo and allocated Power Mail prescriptions will appear as a card in the Inbox on the Prescription Board
Select the Rx Card you wish to process
Using the image on screen input the details as for manual prescriptions - step 3 -4

2D Rx Prescriptions

Primo Rx will appear as a card in the Inbox on the Prescription Board
Details from the Welsh barcode will be read into Titan in which case you can follow the process for EPS - step 12-15
If the 2D barcode is not recognised, you will need to follow the process for manual entry - step 3 -4

EPS Prescriptions

For EPS prescriptions, pay attention to the dosage text
ensure all the fields are complete
pay particular attention to the name, address and date of birth of patient to ensure that it is matched correctly
If there are any amendments / corrections needed, double click on the field to input the correct details
Confirm any corrections made

Confirm

Do a final review of the details of the prescriptions and those inputted and press complete to move the prescription on to the clinical checking process.

Tips and Advice

For manual prescriptions speed up data entry by selecting from history
You can quickly repeat the previous dose from history if you prefer the previous over the new one on the prescription

https://vimeo.com/373154004/6031ae0c89

articles.title: Dispensing Owings
articles.content:
Introduction
Owings are created during the dispensing process when stock is unavailable. For further information about creating the owing itself, you should refer to the Labelling process. This document explains the process for dispensing owings that have been created.
Scope
Receiving stock for owings, getting owings ready for collections
Key Steps
VIEWING YOUR OWINGS

You should keep an eye on your owings log on a regular basis. 
You can view all your owings either on Titan by going to the Views section, or on TITAN Mobile by going to the Settings section.
You can also use KAN ban board and filter the items on Owing

PLACING ORDERS

Orders for Owing stock should be placed as soon as possible during the dispensing process

WHEN STOCK ARRIVES

When your delivery arrives, take the TITAN Mobile device and go to the Owings list.

Check if any of the items in the delivery contain owing stock.
Put this stock to one side for dispensing as soon as possible.

DISPENSING OWINGS

Go to Titan Owing List in the View section
Find the Owing Item you wish to dispense and click on the transaction
From the Labelling screen, scan the manufacturer barcode
Attach the label to the pack, package the item and put on the shelf in the usual way.
Repeat this process for all owings
If owings still remain on the list, make sure that stock has been ordered

Tips and Advice

If you have text messages switch on, the patient will receive a message to say their Owing is ready at the point on assigning it on the shelf using TITAN Mobile 

The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here:
 https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dpYJCXUbjWbVRHJr8dQPRYL_gCLi7QIINOD30jAd9bQ/edit

articles.title: Endorsing and Claiming
articles.content:
Introduction
When the prescription has been dispensed and supplied to the patient, the claim needs to be made to the NHS in a timely and efficient manner. EPS and paper prescriptions clearly follow a different pathway and involve doing different things.
This SOP explains how to manage the endorsing and claims for both NHS paper and EPS prescriptions
Scope

NHS Prescriptions only
For EPS Rx - Submitting EPS claims following Dispense notifications
For paper Rx - endorsing Rx and getting it ready for submission

Key Steps
For EPS Prescriptions

Open the Endorsing screen screen
This will show the Rx which are ready for claim
Any Rx which require further endorsing information, you will need to enter and complete
Click on the items you wish to claim and press send
This will allocate the prescription to this months submission

For Paper Rx/ Welsh 2D Rx (with Primo barcode)

Go to filed prescriptions what were put through Primo
Open the Endorsing screen screen
Scan the Primo barcode
Titan will confirm if the prescription has been handed out and is ready for endorsing
The image will display along with any endorsing details which need to be written onto the prescription
Press complete - this will allocate the prescription to this months submission
File the prescription in this months box

Tips and Advice

Always try to enter any missing endorsing information at the time of labelling to help speed up the endorsing and claim process

The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here: 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XlcyECm5F29pru3DnJr3eZxbnpr4Cb5WOaqx-MBfqiA/

articles.title: Final Checks and Packaging
articles.content:
Introduction
When all items have been labelled, they are now ready for a final check and packaging. Titan dramatically reduces the need for final checks that a pharmacist needs to carry out but there will be times such checks are necessary. Titan also ensures that every labelled item is accounted for as part of the packaging process so nothing gets left behind.
This SOP explains the process for final checks and packaging. It's scope will be checking split items, accuracy checks, accounting for all items before packaging. Covers all prescriptions.
Key Steps

Take a basket with a picking label for each patient
Go to the Titan Kanban screen
Scan the picking label barcode to get to the Packaging screen
Take the first item and scan the dispensing label barcode
Titan will warn you if there are items belonging to the patient that have not been package

Autocheck items

If the dispensing label was produced by scanning the manufacturer’s barcode and the dispense quantity was a full pack, this item will not need a final check

Items Needing further check

If the quantity is not a full manufacturer’s pack or the dispensing label was produced without scanning the manufacturer’s barcode, this item will need a final check by an ACT or pharmacist
At the end of the process the basket will need to go to the checking station.
Repeat step 4 for each item belonging to the patient.

Pharmacist/ ACT Checks

Take the basket where items need a final check
Scan the picking label barcode to recall the transaction
You will be presented with the item(s) that need a final check
Check the item physically for accuracy
When complete Save and Close, or complete the package as shown below

Completing Package

Once all the items have been checked for the patient, select package to obtain a package label.
EPS - If the patient is non-age exempt, a message will appear asking if you wish to print the dispensing token
Repeats - If the patient manages their own repeat ordering, a message will appear if you wish to print the repeat slip
If you require more than one package to accommodate the patient’s items, at any stage select package to produce a package label. You can then scan items into another bag and produce another package label.
Put the package label on the bag
Once all the items have been packaged or accounted for, “press complete”.
Package is now ready to put on shelf or handout

Tips and Advice

Titan will warn you if you have “fridge items” so that you can package these separately in to another bag and an extra “Fridge item” for identification on the bag will be printed.
Titan will warn you if you have “CD items” so that you can package these separately in to another bag and an extra “CD item” for identification on the bag will be printed.

The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1D-JKfh9Fz9U50JdNKDWXhbHNQbzfWGsrD7xnqrT3-5k/edit

articles.title: Handing Out
articles.content:
Introduction
The last part of the prescription journey is to handout the package. Customers could have been waiting at the pharmacy or they could come in to collect their items. At the time of handing medicines over, there are many checks that need to be done and there may be messages that need to be passed over. Titan TITAN Mobile device manages the handout process.
This SOP explains the process for taking the completed package from the dispensary or shelf and transfer to the patient or their representative.
Scope
Patient Handout, managing messages, exemption checking for all prescriptions
Key Steps

If you have taken a scanned a package on TITAN Mobile and the message has told you to hand it out, go to From Package below
If the patient has presented and asked for their package, then go to From Patient below

Identify From Package

After scanning the package the screen will show the details of the patent
Call the patient and confirm their details, or scan their barcode
Go to Handout Process

Search by Patient/ Code

If the patient asks if there is a package to collect, click on Search and enter their details. If they have a text message, enter the number on the text message to identify the patient
The package location will show
Get all the packages from the locations and scan each package
Go to Handout Process

Handout Process

Check if there are any Owings. If there is an owing take the barcode on the screen and scan onto a Titan Station to produce an owing label
Check exemption status. If the patient pays, collect the correct money otherwise select the exemption reason
Check any messages. If there is a message give this information and confirm you have done so
If the signature screen appears, you will need to ask the patient to sign the box on TITAN Mobile 
When all tasks have been actioned the handout will be complete

Tips and Advice

If the patient wants to see what items were on the prescription, you can view an image of the prescription

Upon completion of handout, the EPS Dispense Notification will be sent automatically where applicable

There is a companion video for this article which you can view here:
https://vimeo.com/373158234/10104a48c5
The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/15ztPlIoeHsdfDaN-a6uh8MmxCgV24v-dR2Oqqg83sV0/edit

articles.title: Labelling Stock
articles.content:
Introduction
After all the stock has been picked for a patient’s batch using the Picking Label, the items now ready to be labelled. 
Titan’s preferred method of labelling uses barcodes to ensure the right label is issued for the right pack. Titan also incorporates FMD verification when barcoding is used. However, there are times when it is not possible to use barcodes and you will need to manually split labels and check. 
This SOP explains Titan’s process for labelling.
Scope
Labelling, barcode scanning, FMD verification, split packs. All prescriptions
Key Steps

Take a basket with a picking label for each patient
Go to the Titan Kanban screen
Scan the picking label barcode to get to the labelling screen

Barcode Process

Take the first packet and scan the manufacturer’s barcode, to receive the dispensing label.
If you have the 2D manufacturers barcode scan that instead to perform the FMD verification
If the correct item’s barcode has been scanned a label for the correct quantity will be issued
Put the dispensing label immediately on the manufacturer’s pack you scanned
Repeat steps 3-4 for all items in the basket that need a dispensing label
Press complete when all items have been labelled

Wrong Barcode scanned

If the wrong manufacture pack is scanned, a warning will appear
A record of a near miss will be captured along with staff details

Barcode not found/ unavailable

If the manufacturer’s barcode will not scan or there is no barcode available, you can press the label tile
Select the correct manufacturer from the list of products and this will print a label manually

Splitting the label

If you want to manually print labels and split the label first, click on the action circle and select split. Enter the quantities to split by and the label cards will be split accordingly.

No Stock Available

If you do not have the stock, you will need to account for this. 
Go to the Action Circle and select “Owing”
The balance quantity that has not been labelled will be sent to Owing

Completion

When all the prescription items have been account for either by producing labels or marking them as owings, you can press Save to exit
Place the basket with the labelled items in the area ready to be packaged and checked
Or you can click Package Now to proceed to package these item

There is a companion video for this article which you can view here:
https://vimeo.com/373155829/f816b4dc5c
The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here: 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Cz-dQcn0Cnsnl6t_TTdMCnb6a90JepvQzKpU1T8ma2I/edit

articles.title: Picking Stock
articles.content:
Introduction
Once the prescription has been clinically checked, the process moves on to Picking. Titan workflow requires that you get the stock first before labelling can commence. Therefore you use the Picking Label to get the stock that you need for that prescription. Titan Picking Label batches prescriptions for the same patient together so get all the stock you need to fulfil all the items for a patient in one go.
This SOP explains the process that needs to be followed to get the Picking Label.
Scope
Printing picking labels individually for a prescription or as a bulk action
Key Steps
For Individual Picking Labels

Go to Titan Prescription Board
Click on the prescription you wish to pick stock for
On the Prescription Fly Out, press Picking Label
A Picking Label will be produced and the Rx Card will move to the Labelling Stage on the Prescription Board

For Bulk Labels and Picking Sheet

Go to Titan Prescription Board
If you want to print Bulk Picking Labels for many items in one go, on the Prescription Board select Bulk Actions
Selecting the Rx cards you wish to process and press OK

Collecting Stock

Put the picking label for each patient in a separate basket and use to pick the stock
Take a basket with a picking label for each patient
Pick the items required from the dispensary shelf and put in to the basket
Place the basket with the stock for each patient in the area where it is ready to label
GO TO Scan and Label SOP

Tips and Advice

If there are multiple prescriptions for a single patient, the Picking Label will create a single batch for all items on those prescriptions
Attach the Picking Labels to the side of the basket for easy identification
If you want to automatically print picking labels after clinical check, you can have this setting switched on

The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here: 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B-QT5-AxJ2lXgmE7oSioKhceL6MUhOkIM5Z77HawOTQ/edit

articles.title: Prepack of Products
articles.content:
Process Name
Prepack of Products

Purpose

The purpose of this SOP is to ensure there is an accurate and accountable process and documentation for the production of pre-packs in the pharmacy.
 
This SOP explains the process for the preparation of pre-packs

Scope
Preparation of documentation, Picking of Stock, Preparation of pre-pack labels, preparation of the batch and checking of the batch.

Responsibility
Pharmacy Staff

Key Steps

Preparation of Pre-pack documentation

Print off a Pre-pack preparation sheet
Write down the name, strength and formulation of the medicines to be prepared.
Write down the quantity of pre-packs to be prepared – Always add an extra pack as this will help in the checking process
Sign and date the document
Put the document into a plastic sleeve folder

 

Picking of Stock

Take the Pre-pack preparation sheet
Pick the required number of the manufacturer’s pack that have the same Batch Number and Expiry Dates

If you do not have the correct quantity pick the quantity that is available

Place the stock into a tote
On the pre-pack preparation sheet write down the quantity of stock that you have picked
Write down the batch number and expiry of the stock picked.
Sign and date the sheet
Put the pre-pack sheet into the plastic folder and place in the tote

 

Preparation of pre-pack labels

Log on to Titan and Go to the Stock Management menu

Click on the “Add Prepack” button on the bottom left of the screen

Scan the 2D barcode on one of the packs that has been picked to populate the name of the drug, the batch number and expiry.

If barcode is not available you can search for the drug, and input the batch number and expiry

Input the quantity that will be contained in each pre-pack “pack size to produce”

Input the number of labels to produce. Always add an extra label as this will help in the checking process

Put the labels and the pre-pack preparation sheet into the plastic folder ready for the physical preparation of pre-packs

 

Physical preparation of pre-packs

Take the tote and the plastic folder containing the pre-pack
Take out the labels and the preparation sheet.
Take one pack of the stock picked
Check the name, strength, quantity and batch number
Prepare the tray equipment ready to be filled.
Pop out the tablets into each compartment.
Ensure that all the compartments are filled.
Close and seal the tray
Take one of the pre-pack labels and stick on to the front of the tray.
Place the completed tray into the tote
Repeat until the required quantity of trays are completed.
Sign and date the prepack preparation sheet

 

Checking of the pre-pack batch

Take the prepack preparation sheet
Physically check a sample of the trays, pay attention to the name, strength and formulation and quantities.
Ensure that the tray compartments are full.
Check the batch number and expiry dates
Sign and date the prepack preparation sheet.
Store the sheets appropriately.
Give the stock to be put on the shelves for storage.

 

Tips/ Advice

Ensure that you pick stock with the same Batch Number and Expiry

 
 

 
 

Office Use Only
 Titan 1.0 

 
Titan steps are shown in red

articles.title: Product Adding - Internal Use
articles.content:
Process Name
Product Adding - Last reviewed: 08/04/25

 
 
Purpose

The purpose of this SOP is to ensure there is an accurate and accountable process and documentation for adding products into a sites database.
 
This SOP explains the process for adding products. This procedure applies to all non dm+d items that are requested to be added to the sites database.
 

 
Scope

This procedure applies to all items that are requested to be added to the sites database.

Responsibility
Integrations team.

Key Steps

Once the product adding spreadsheet/macro is received from a site follow the steps below: 

Ensure ALL required fields are completed for the product
Confirm that the site are 100% sure that the items are worded exactly how they would like the item to be displayed on their dispensing labels as we cannot make amendments once the item has been added. Please make the site aware of this.
Check the item on dm+d register to see whether these items exist. If they do abort this process.
Open TC and select ‘Product Adding’ from the main menu.

Fill out the 6 sections based on the product information provided to you by the site. 
a. Always tick the warning addition box when uploading a product.
b. Double check you have written out the product details correctly and have not made any errors/typos. 

Click ‘Add’ this will immediately upload the data to the site’s environment.

Tips/Advice

Regardless of how many/which warning labels the site has requested for the product, ticking advisory warning machinery will add all applicable warnings. 

ALWAYS double check the fields to ensure no errors are made. 

Items are added per site, e.g. if an item is added to FLF77 it will NOT exist on FN849. 

Endorsing - The items being added onto a sites database do not exist on the dm+d therefore these items will be prescribed on a manual/Private prescription, these will never be on a NHS EPS prescriptions. https://cpe.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/PSNC-Briefing-052.15-NHS-medicines-database-dmd-2020.pdfDue to the prescription being a manual sites will need to manually endorse the item on the prescription that they will then send off for submission. Sites will not need to add an endorsement on Titan, these will ALWAYS need to be done manually.

Date written
06/11/2024

articles.title: Receive Prescriptions
articles.content:
Introduction
Prescriptions can be received into a pharmacy in a variety of ways. Paper prescriptions are still common although EPS is the dominant method in England.
Titan enforces a structured method of managing paper prescriptions in both England and Wales. The preferred method is using the Titan Power Mail app, which converts the prescription into the image. This means that physical paper prescriptions does not need to follow the dispensing process as the image is used instead.
This SOP explains how to manage the various ways in which prescriptions arrive.
Scope
This procedure applies to all paper prescriptions received in the pharmacy, including Paper FP10, Paper Private Rx, Welsh 2D Rx, EPS Rx
Key Steps
RECEIVING THE PRESCRIPTION
Patient arrives with paper Rx

Tear off repeat slips and hand back to patient
Check name and address of patient and clarify any incorrect or incomplete details
If the patient is exempt, ensure the reverse side of the prescription is completed appropriately and if evidence has been provided previously and seen. Take payment as appropriate.
Put prescription into basket ready for data entry

Rx arriving with driver or post

Check name and address of patient and clarify any incorrect or incomplete details
Put prescription into basket ready for data entry

GETTING RX INTO SYSTEM
Manual Process

Where Primo or Power Mail is not available go directly to Data Entry

Scanning Paper Rx into PowerMail

Email a scanned copy or photo of the prescription to your PowerMail email address using a secure email system.
Open the PowerMail app and click on the email.
Select the image thumb nail and click the button to indicate that the image is a prescription.
The prescription image will appear in the Prescription Board for data entry. See Data Entry SOP.

Scanning Paper Rx into Primo

Log in to Primo using your PIN
Separate the repeat slip from the prescription
Put the prescription in Primo
Allocate Rx to Waiting or Calling back as required
Press the Scan Button on Primo & Scan Rx and Send to Titan
File the paper prescriptions in the “ready to be endorsed” file under the appropriate day of scanning. File the repeat slips in the “repeat slip” file ready to be scanned.
The scanned paper prescriptions will now appear on the Data Entry card of Titan

EPS downloaded Rx

Titan will automatically download any EPS prescriptions who have the pharmacy nominated.
You can also download the EPS Rx by scanning the EPS R2 barcode
The EPS prescriptions ready for processing will be on the Data Entry card of Titan.

Tips and Advice

The default of the Allocation will be “Unallocated”. If you wish to change this, you can manually change this to “Waiting” if required. 

There is a companion video for this article which you can view here:
https://vimeo.com/372975853/129c745d45
The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here: 
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uWpphx0DzEoNUrzwUmCwYphymKzGZ_ipS8ecukVI6mc/edit

articles.title: Stock Ordering
articles.content:
Introduction
To manage the process of ordering stock and replenishment. This includes placing orders with suppliers using a range of cascading systems.
Scope
Placing orders, stock replenishment. Please note, this is not a full stock control system.
Key Steps
BEFORE YOU START

Make sure the pharmacy has the right suppliers set up and the correct settings for each. 
To view or update the settings, use the Supplier Management section within the Stock Management screen
You will need to decide if you wish to manage your ordering process through auto-ordering. You can choose from the following; 

 
Auto-Order at Clinical Check - this will add the item to the ordering pad at the clinical check stage
 
USING AUTO ORDER

If you have one of the Auto-Order settings on, then the system will manage the day to day ordering at the point of Clinical Checks
At the point of Clinical Check, you will be informed about the order to be placed, the pack size and the supplier. if you wish to cancel that particular order, you can do so at this point.

MANUAL ORDERS

At any point, if you wish to add an item to the Order Pad, you can do so in one of two ways;

At Clinical Check stage - Click on the shopping bag against the item during clinical checks

At Labelling Stage - click on the dispensing wheel to add the item to the order

At Any time - you can press F6 and either enter the product you wish to order or scan the product barcode if available

Via TITAN Mobile - Go to Stock Management in Settings and either enter the product you wish to order or scan the product barcode if available

REVIEWING ORDERS

You can view your current order by clicking on F6 and going into the Order Pad.
You can change quantities and add or delete items as required

TRANSMITTING

At the preferred designated time, you can transmit your order the supplier. 
Go to the Order Pad (F6) select ALL items OR filter by supplier you wish to order with, OR use TITAN Mobile to go to Stock Management Screen

Click Place Order and the order will be sent via that suppliers preferred method.Once transmitted, you can view Historical Orders

Tips and Advice

Whether you choose an Auto-Order method or not, you are always able to order manually at various points when required
The Stock Management section shows a Product List and the default suppliers for each item. The system will learn and populate your preferred items as you dispense prescriptions, but you can you view the status of each item. More information on Product Management is available elsewhere.

You may find this video helpful as a companion to this SOP article:
https://vimeo.com/user87918304/review/385355708/3776abda4e
The formatted SOP document, should you need it for your records can be found here:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/11IMaIbrMBhqwOvkG8tBm0ghhf1zv1j_j-elEG4xSn_g/edit

articles.title: Batch Lock Bypass
articles.content: What is Batch Lock Bypass?Batch Lock Bypass is a safety feature that prevents two users from accessing and working on the same prescription simultaneously from different PCs. This helps to avoid duplicate label printing, conflicting updates, missed changes, and other errors that could compromise accuracy and workflow.  How do I disable it?The setting can be adjusted via Settings → Dispensing Settings → Miscellaneous → Prevent Batch Lock Bypass, but altering it may affect prescription integrity and safety across the system.  Should I disable it?Probably not!Instead of disabling the feature, it is recommended to use it as a staff training opportunity, reinforcing the importance of fully exiting a prescription once processing is complete.

articles.title: Patient's Name Doesn't Fit on Label
articles.content:
Please navigate to Settings ➝ Dispensing settings ➝ Dispensing
First, Toggle on "Shorten long patient name on picking/dispensing/owing label"
If this doesn't work, change Dispensing label type from "Large Barcode" to "Default"

The patient's name should now appear without error.

articles.title: Trigger DN When Closing Package
articles.content:
The default setting for sending a Dispense Notification (DN) in Titan is when the prescription is collected.
This feature allows you to configure TITAN to send a DN when the medication is dispensed and the package is closed.
It does not affect the claim or payment, it just allows you to choose the timing of the DN.

Click the item

articles.title: How to Perform a Stock Take/Stock Audit in Titan Mobile
articles.content:
Overview This guide explains how to complete your first stock take in Titan Mobile. The stock take process ensures your recorded stock levels match the physical items on your shelves. By scanning each shelf and product, Titan Mobile automatically identifies whether an item is already assigned to that shelf, needs relocating, or is being added for the first time. Once all quantities are entered, completing the stock take updates your system records and ensures accurate stock control moving forward. Steps To carry out your first stock take: 
Open the Stock Audit screen in Titan Mobile
Start by scanning one of your shelves

Then scan a product from that shelf 

If the belongs on a different shelf, you will be asked if you want to relocate all stock to this shelf
If the product is not on any shelf, it will be added with a quantity of zero

articles.title: Introduction to Split Pack Management
articles.content:

You can add this stock to a shelf and monitor the stock holding in the normal way You can also make these up ahead of time from the Assembled packs screen. PrePack labels will need to have an accuracy check after labelling, unless you do this ahead of time from the Assembled Packs screen.If you are using a dispensing robot, labelled packs can then be fed back into the robot. Set UpYou just need to set up your print profile: 
Settings 
Print Profiles
Set your PrePack Label report to the same Profile that your Dispensing Label is using
Click Save Changes
  Making a Pre-packFrom the Assembled Pack screen, you can break down large packs into smaller pre-packs.For example, scan a large box of 1,000 tablets and create 31 packs of 32 tablets.Each pre-pack created this way will appear with the status “Require Checking.” Steps:   1.  Go to Stock Management   2. Click on the Assembled Packs screen   3.  Click Add Pre-pack   4a. Scan in the product you will make the prepack from         or   4b. Click I don't have a barcode and then manually select the product   5. Enter the pack size you want to produce, together with the batch number and expiry date   6. Enter how many labels you wish to produce   7. Click Create  Get The Pack Approved to Avoid an Accuracy Check After DispensingAfter creating your Pre-pack, you can do the approval from the Assembled packs screen. articles.content:
Overview Titan Stock Control includes a paperless stock picking feature designed to make picking faster, simpler, and more accurate.Instead of printing and using physical picking labels, the process is handled completely within Titan Mobile, allowing you to label and manage your baskets digitally. You will be alerted during picking if you select the wrong product, and will no longer need to keep printing picking labels. Step 1: Creating and Labelling Basket Totes Before you begin picking, you’ll need to set up your baskets for digital tracking:

 Click Add New Tote

Select the patient from the list
Scan the basket you want to pick into
Scan the products (or swipe left if you can't scan)
Tap Complete Batch

Enough packs will then be automatically added to your Order Pad to bring you back up to your maximum holding. From Stock Ordering, open the Stock Control tab for an item
Enter your minimum and maximum required stock holding (in packs)
Click Save

Click Save again
 
 

Do a Stock Take This is to ensure the stock is correct.  Do this as soon as you do the above to prevent orders from being sent at the wrong time or for the wrong amount.  See the article "How to Perform a Stock Take in Titan Mobile".

Stock is subtracted from the total when you label an item and added back when you book it in. If you delete a label, the Stock will be added back on.  You can also manually amend the stock holing in the Stock Control tab, by clicking "Add Stock Movement":

Transcript (AI Generated):In this video, we are going to look at how to use the latest feature from Titan BMR, stock Control. As usual, let's begin by installing stock control from the marketplace. Once installed, the new option called stock management will appear in your Titan menu. All stock will be set to zero, but stock movements will now be monitored. Stock is subtracted from the total when you label an item and added back on when you book it in. Let's start by setting up our bin locations. This is the name given to your stock shelves that can be labelled within Titan. You can actually order the items on your picking list by bin location, which will help you to pick in the most efficient way possible. So I'd recommend you turn this on. Next, go to the stock item shelf management screen and click on the stock item shelf management tab. Just hit add New shelf and give it a name, and then hit submit. Once you've finished making up all your shelves, you just need to print out the shelf labels and stick them on. It is now time to do your first stock take entitled Mobile. Go to the stock audit screen and start by scanning one of the shelves. Then Scan a product from the shelf. The products will be added to the shelf and will show at the top of the screen with a quantity of zero. Then just enter the correct number of full packs that you have in stock. Repeat for all items on your shelves, and then click complete stock order. Once you've completed your stock order, you'll be able to see exactly what's on each shelf in the Stock Item Shelf management screen. Once your stock take is complete, you'll want to set up your stock ordering rules. Go to the stock ordering screen and order by average use. Then you can start setting up your order thresholds in that order. Take threshold ordering and then go to the stock control tab and enter your maximum and minimum required stock holding impacts and click save. What this will mean is that the items will no longer be ordered until you get to below your minimum holding. Now, which time an order will be placed sufficient to get you back up to your maximum holding. The next part of the setup process is to set up your order pads. Just edit the pads that you want to use or create new ones and tick track on Titan Mobile booking. This will make sure that any orders placed on this pad will be sent to Titan Mobile for booking in when the stock arrives. If you want to try just setting up stock control with a few items to begin with, you could consider just turning on tracking for one order pad like your fast movers or even a brand new pad. Then just make sure that all the items you want to track are set to that pad and have threshold ordering turned on. So let's place an order as normal to start the process. The next step is to book in the stock. It's very important that you do this before you take any items out of the delivery totes. If you don't, your stock levels will be incorrect and your threshold ordering will not work properly. Over on type mobile, you'll see that the order has appeared on the book Booking stock screen. Each product you ordered will be listed along with what shelf the stock is kept on, how many packs were ordered and still need to be booked in. How many of the given items are on owing and which order pad the order actually came from. Just scan any item from your delivery tote to book it in. The number outstanding will be reduced accordingly until you've scanned all of the expected stock. At this point, the product will be removed from the expected stock screen altogether and will appear on the booked in screen. If you're unable to scan a particular product, check how many packs are expected, count how many you have, and then click book. In clicking. This will book in all remaining stock of that product in one go. If the quantity you had delivered differs from the expected quantity, just go over to the booked in screen to amend it. Similarly, if you want to book in the whole order in one go without scanning or accounting for each individual pack, you can just check select all items, and then hit book in. Select it. This is obviously the fastest way to book in all your stock, but be careful because booking in this way will mean that you will not notice if your delivery was missing certain items, and if that's the case, your stop levels will be wrong. Once you've booked everything in, anything remaining on the screen should be considered missing. Check these against your invoice and see if you are charged. If not, you can safely delete the items with the dustbin icon. Once you've finished click Complete Booking, you can also hit complete booking at any point during the booking in process, your progress will be saved and you can come back to finish the booking in later. Let's go back to Titan and have a further look at some of the other important screens back in the stock management screen. Clicking on an item and then into stock control, you'll see a full ledger of all stock movements for that item. You can see when an item was booked in dispensed and where stock was manually adjusted and by whom. We can also manually adjust the stock from here using the add stock movement button. Choose from stock take to update the current stock value book in to add new stock or remove to subtract a quantity from the stock balance, great for if you need to book in stock that wasn't ordered through Titan. Also, with stock control comes full split pack management. This will be turned on automatically when you install the app, allowing you to label your split packs with the correct quantity. The label will include a QR code that can be used at dispensing to validate the transaction. Before we start, just make sure you set up your pre-pack label to use your normal label print profile. Now, that's done. Let's see what happens when you dispense a split pack. I'm going to dispense 28 tablets from a box of a hundred. We see that as well as the normal dispensing label. Titan Stock Control has produced a pre-pack label for 72 tablets. Just stick this on the pack to use. Next time. There's an optional step of monitoring your stock holding for your split packs. If you want to do this, just scan them onto the shelf in Titan Mobile. Using stock order, the stock will then be added to your shelf and the new entry will be created on stock ordering for you to monitor that stock holding. You can also manually create pre-pack cables for your existing split packs. To get this stock recorded from the assembled pack screen, click pre-pack and scan the barcode. Then enter the number of units, the batch and the expiry date and click create. The label can now be stuck onto the box and added to the shelf like before. You can also use this screen to break down large packs of tablets into smaller pre-packs ahead of time. For example, you could scan a large box of a thousand co-codamol and make 31 smaller packs of 32 tablets. When creating pre-packs, you will see that they're created with the status require checking. This means that after they are dispensed, an accuracy check will be required. However, if you wish, you can do this ahead of time from this screen. Just scan the pack into the same screen, count the tablets, and click approve. Finally, we've included a bonus stock picking feature for you here. So instead of using the picking labels, stock control comes with a fully paperless approach to begin and label all your baskets so that pick stock can be assigned to them. Go to the basket totes and create your basket labels. These labels can now be stuck onto your baskets permanently. Now let's pick some stock. Instead of printing a picking label, just go to the pick stock screen in Titan Mobile. From here, you'll see your whole picking column. As per the prescription board, select the batch you want to pick, scan the basket that you want to pick it into. Then just start scanning your stock as you pick it in. If the barcode won't scan, just swipe left. If you scan the wrong product, you'll be alerted preventing a potential dispensing error later on down the line. Once you've picked everything, just hit complete batch. The card will then progress to the next column in Titan, ready for labelling, and that's it. That's stock control. Enjoy. Yeah.

articles.title: Basket Colour Definitions
articles.content:
- No packs have been ordered (they may have gone to remainders or the item may not be available from the selected supplier)
 - 1 pack has been added to the order pad
- 1 pack has been ordered
 - There are multiple flavours available. Items have not yet been added. Hover the icon to make a decision.
 
 
Tips: Reasons for an item not being auto-ordered include the following:

The item is a special.
The item is not listed with the supplier that it has been set to.
The quantity prescribed does not equal at least 70% of the pack size available (read about remainders for more information).

articles.title: How does TITAN decide What Pack Size to Order?
articles.content:
The following logic is used by TITAN to identify what pack sizes should be ordered:
Retrieve all active pack sizes from our database for the prescribed item.

Exclude pack sizes that the selected supplier does not provide.

Order the preferred pack size if available.

If the preferred size is not available, order the pack size that matches the prescribed quantity.

If not available, fulfil the quantity by ordering multiples of smaller pack sizes if needed (e.g. if the prescribed quantity is 112, order 4 packs of 28, rather than one box of 100).

Order pack sizes closes to the prescribed quantity as possible (e.g. of the prescription is for 112 and the item is available in 28 and 56, order 2x 56).

If it is not possible to order the exact quantity prescribed, add the remaining quantity to the  Remainders tab.

articles.title: Remainders
articles.content:
Remainders
Depending on your settings, TITAN will add items to your order pad when a prescription is downloaded or when the clinical check is done. A prescription needs to be for at least 70% of a pack size for it to get added to the pad.
If a prescription is received for less than 70% of the pack size, the full quantity will be added to the Remainders tab to be ordered later.
Similarly, if the quantity on the prescription is different to the pack size, any left over quantity will be added to the Remainders tab.
The next time a prescription is received for this item, the quantity on the remainders tab will be added to that of the prescription to calculate the amount of packs needed.
Example 1

A prescription is received for 14 Warfarin 2mg tablets. The pack size is 28.
As the quantity is less than 70% of the pack size, the item is not ordered but put onto the Remainders tab.
The next week, a second identical prescription is received. The 14 on the prescription are added to the 14 on the remainders tab to equal 28 tablets. One pack is now added to the order pad and there are no longer any remainders left.

 
Example 2

A prescription is received for 30 Sertraline 50mg tablets. The pack size is 28. 
1 pack of 28 is added to the order pad, and 2 tablets are added to the Remainders. 
The same thing happens later that day, pushing the remainders up to 4.
After the tenth prescription is received, 20 remainders have been added to the order pad. A pack of 28 tablets is ordered because of the prescription, but because the Remainders are now at more than 70% of the pack size, a second pack of 28 is also ordered.

articles.title: How Many QA Checks Will I Need to Do After My Burst Finishes?
articles.content:
Titan AI uses three levels of inspection to determine how many prescriptions need to be checked during an audit. The system adjusts the level based on how well automation is performing.

Reduced Inspection Level (Fewer Checks) – If multiple audits show no issues, the system lowers the number of required checks to improve efficiency.

Normal Inspection Level (Standard Checks) – This is the starting point. A standard number of prescriptions are checked per batch.

Tightened Inspection Level (Stricter Checks) – If errors (major or too many minor ones) are found, the system increases the number of prescriptions that need to be checked.

Indicative Sample Sizes

 
How It Works

If no issues are found, the system gradually reduces inspection levels to speed up the process.
If errors exceed the allowed limit, the system tightens inspection to catch more mistakes.
If too many problems occur at the tightened level, automation may be paused until the issue is resolved.

This method ensures a balance between efficiency and safety, keeping automation running smoothly while maintaining high standards.

articles.title: How to Do a QA Check
articles.content:
Once you finish your burst, you will need to complete all your QA checks before you can start a new burst. This is to make sure you are in control of the actions taken by TITAN AI and are able to report any issues to us for us to rectify.

Open the Prescription Feed.
Select any prescription you want to audit (we recommend prioritising the "New Dosage" ones).
Review the prescription image and any dose changes that were made. 
Click either Approve, Major Issue or Minor Issue as appropriate.
Continue until you have done all of the required checks.

Tips:

Once you have done all your checks, and not before, you will be able to start a new Burst.

Click here to learn more about how to identify an issue as Major or Minor.

articles.title: Major and Minor Issues
articles.content:
Titan AI uses the AQL international standard to ensure accuracy and safety in its automation process. At the end of each burst, a pharmacist checks a sample of them and can choose to log an issue:
Major Issue
A significant error that could impact patient safety.Once submitted, they require a final check, a report is sent to the TITAN Clinical Safety Group, audit requirements in future bursts will increase, and any associated learning will be removed.Classify as Major if the Titan AI instructions changed any of the following in a clinically significant way:

Quantity instructed to be taken
Frequency of taking the medication
The timing of when the medication is to be taken

Minor Issue 
A small, non-clinical error (e.g. formatting or minor text changes).
You accept the actions taken by TITAN AI. Your report will be sent to the TITAN Clinical Safety Group for review.

articles.title: Video
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Hello everyone, and here's another quick video about an amazing new feature, Titan ai. Titan AI is changing the way that our pharmacists work. It's the first AI powered clinical tool for pharmacies. It automatically reviews and optimizes prescriptions for safety and accuracy, significantly reducing workload. With its advanced AI and machine learning, it handles most clinical checks on its own saving pharmacists time and effort. So how does Titan AI actually learn? Well, Titan AI gets smarter over time with four different training levels, and you get to decide which one you use at level one, it only makes changes automatically after you've manually adjusted the same thing at least five times for the same patient. Level two expands the learning to including all patients in your pharmacy, needing 20 changes across 20 different patients before it kicks in. Level three goes even further. Pulling in learning from all Titan AI pharmacies with 20 pharmacists needing to have made the same change in 20 different pharmacies. Or if you prefer, you can skip straight to global only, which uses the biggest data set for maximum accuracy. The most advanced option, though, is level four full Titan ai. Combining our AI language model with big data to be able to automate about 90% of your clinical checks, it cleans up and formats, doses, handles drug interactions and duplicate prescriptions, and even makes clinical recommendations when needed. There are two different ways to run Titan ai. You can choose either assisted mode or full automation in assisted mode, Titan AI processes prescriptions, but you still get the final say on everything. It automatically checks for interactions, duplicate drugs and allergies, and even automated dose changes. But you will always have the last word before anything moves forward, and you'll always have sight of each prescription. Full automation mode runs and bursts of one to four hours, after which you will review a sample of prescriptions before starting the next round. The live prescription feed keeps everything visible so you always know what's going on. If it comes across a new dose that it hasn't seen before, it flags it to the live prescription feed. For easy review, need to exclude certain patients or prescriptions. No problem at all. Just tag them and Titan AI will always leave them alone. Sometimes Titan AI won't fully automate a prescription because there's just not enough learning or data, or there's a clinical concern When this happens. A banner at the top of the check screen will explain why dose changes can still be automated under partial automation, and you can review them by hovering over the blue dot Titan. AI follows the international A QL standard to ensure accuracy and safety after each first. A pharmacist checks the sample of prescriptions and rates them as either no issue, meaning everything is correct, minor issue, so maybe there's a small formatting or text adjustment that they'd like, or a major issue where there could be some issue there could potentially affect patient safety. If no major issue is found, Titan AI keeps running as usual, but if problems are identified, then flagged items will require a final check before they can be dispensed. Any flagged issues get reported to the Titan Clinical Group, which will increase the number of future audits needed. Learning for flagged items is also removed to prevent mistakes from happening again and newly encountered doses get prioritized. For the review, Titan AI adjusts how many prescriptions get checked based on past audit results. It starts with the normal inspection level where a standard number of prescriptions are reviewed. If errors are found, it moves to a tightened inspection level where more prescriptions are checked. If everything looks good over multiple audits, it drops to a reduced inspection level, meaning that fewer prescriptions are needed for reviewing. Speeding up the process. Getting set up on Titan AI is quick and easy. Install the app as usual, then tweak the settings to fit your needs. Set your preferred burst length, which is how long Titan AI will run for. Before you need to do your checks, decide if new patients and new therapies should go through automation and select your AI training level. Once you're ready, just hit the play button and choose between assisted mode or full automation. Then sit back and let tighten AI do all the heavy lifting. Once a burst is finished, it's time for quality assurance. Open the live prescription feed and check the process prescriptions. If everything looks good, take a proof. If you spot an issue, select minor or major issue and comment, then record it. Titan AI is always learning and improving, making it even more accurate than manual checks. It saves pharmacists a huge amount of time while ensuring high safety standards. With Titan ai, you can spend your time focusing on what really matters, caring for your patients and growing your business. Yeah.

articles.title: What Checks Are Excluded From Full Automation?
articles.content:
There are a number of checks that TITAN AI will not be able to fully automate and will always require a pharmacist's input as a partial check
 
A full list of these are as follows:

Notes marked as "Show at clinical check"
High risk drug warnings
Unit Of Measure code not found
Partial patient matches
Expired Rx
Prescription Type is retired
Drug Availability messages
Presence of additional dosage information
Presence of additional patient information
Patient is under 12 years old
Special container pack size checks (eg Ventolin Inhaler where quantity is 28)
Future dated prescriptions (Wales)
1st issues of all ERDs (as of version 2.28.10)
Any prescription for patients with a tag that has the "Exclude from TITAN AI" setting turned on.

articles.title: What Do the Different Levels Mean?
articles.content:
Level 1 – Patient Learning Only: TITAN AI requires at least five manual changes for the same patient and item before is can apply the same change automatically.

Level 2 – Pharmacy Learning: Expands training data to include all patients across the pharmacy, with a threshold of 20 changes for 20 separate patients.

Level 3 – Global 1.0: Sources learning from all TITAN AI pharmacies across the TITAN PMR customer base, requiring 20 changes from 20 separate pharmacists in 20 different pharmacies.

Level 3 – Global 1.0 Only: Skips Levels 1 and 2, meaning that it will always leverage the largest data source for maximum accuracy.Level 4 – All 2.0 Only*: The most advanced model, utilising a sophisticated AI language model combined with big data and detailed training to fully automate approximately 90% of clinical checks, dramatically saving pharmacists' time.

Cleans all doses, removing irrelevant information while fixing capitalisation and formatting issues to ensure best practices.
Clinical checks such as interactions and drug doubling are managed automatically.
Makes clinical suggestions in cases like Excessive Quantity or Incorrect Route of Administration.*Level 4 is available in Partial Mode only while TITAN AI is in beta.

articles.title: What Does the Percentage Represent?
articles.content: The percentage as displayed in the Live Prescription Feed is the percentage of items that have gone through full automation. You will need to click the refresh button to see the up-to-date figures.

articles.title: What is the Difference Between Full Automation and Assisted Mode?
articles.content:
In Assisted Mode, TITAN AI supports prescription processing by handling interactions, allergy checks, drug duplications, and proposing dose adjustments. However, all prescriptions still require a pharmacist’s final approval before progressing to the dispensary.

In Full Automation Mode, the system processes prescriptions autonomously in bursts lasting 1 to 4 hours. After each burst, a designated number of prescriptions are audited by a pharmacist to ensure quality control before initiating the next burst. A Live Prescription Feed is available for real-time visibility into prescriptions that have been processed.

articles.title: Known Issues
articles.content:
Known Issues Tab Guide  Firstly open up the main menu, type in the ODS code and press enter.Tip: This main menu will also always show you the pod of whichever ODS code you are searching  This will then open up the screen shown below, from here click on known issues: Backing Card Failing to Print:  Double click on this and TC will either come up with a pop up to let you know that this has been successful, or tell you 'no issue detected'. Click on on either message and the fix is complete.   Bulk SMS Alerts: Double click on this and TC will ask you to press yes or no, if you the site have confirmed this is what they would like then press yes. TIP: This will not work for email alerts.  Card Disappeared: Double click on this and TC will ask you to click yes or no, this will fix any EPS prescriptions with a null batch ID (TKI-001) the symptoms of this is that theprescription will “disappear” from the board after clinical check. If the fix has been successful the script/scripts will the appear back on the board after a refresh. TIP: This fix does not work for manual prescriptions.  Chem Code Updates: https://bso.hscni.net/directorates/operations/family-practitioner-services/pharmacy/contractor-information/drug-tariff-and-related-materials/code-book-and-amendments-2/There is an Excel spreadsheet in that link above, use this to get the latest file, choose the tab in the spreadsheet which says "full codebook"And CTRL+F to search for the product and find the right oneTIP: There is a new codebook released every month. And this is only for NI sites.Double click this, find the product within the full codebook, add this into the search drug bar and press enter, copy the correct chem code from the spreadsheet, paste into the chem code bar at the bottom and hit save. It will apply to all products within your search list and take effect immediately.  Claim Stuck: Double click on 'Claim stuck'. This screen will populate:   Tick 'Auto Fix Mode' and hit 'Claim Fixer', this should auto-fix all of the failed claims.   Claim Status: Status 7: ClaimedStatus 3: FailedStatus 0: QueuedStatus 1: SubmittedStatus 15: Archived Failed claims should populate under 'Barcode' on the right hand side of the screen. Click on one of the barcodes to populate the claim status and begin the fixes. When you double click on the claim in the left hand side of the screen, it should populate the problem and solution. Clicking 'Fix it!' should resolve the issue with that claim in particular. Repeat this process on every failed prescription. You can also enter the prescription barcode in the search bar if you cannot see the specified claim you are looking for in the right hand side. You can use the 'Load Tracker' button to populate the spine status so you can monitor when the claim has been successful on the spine.  ERD No Patient: Double click on this and click run fix. This error is TKI-M085 and happens quite rarely when a site try to bulk release several issues of an eRD.TIP: You do not need to enter the prescription barcode, clicking run fix will run this in bulk and fix any eRDs affected.  Invalid Signature: Double click on this, enter the prescription barcode in the search bar and hit fix invalid signature  Merge Patient: Double click on this and it will open up the merge tab.TIP: This tab was created for Pilltime, they now have the ability to complete these merges within their Titan environment and this tab is no longer used.  Missing Stock Records: Double click on this and it will open up a search tab to search for drugs.  Type the first 4 letters of the drug to search for a drug record. To search for Amlodipine 20mg tablets, search like this: Amlo%20. Click search.  The missing drugs will show under drug, and you can also see the pack size. To add the item to the site's environment, click 'Add All'.   TKI-015:Simply double click the TKI-015 option, and it will run that for any items affected for the whole pharmacy. TIP: If the issue remains after doing this, it's not a TKI-015 and needs to be escalated.  Pill Time Orders in Robot:  Double click on this to see all orders currently in the robot. Pill Time will send you the times that they sent these orders to the robot, so use the 'Sent to Robot' column to select the orders that you need. Once you have selected the orders affected, click 'Set to Failed Production'. TIP: You can also use ToteId search to find the affected order.   Pill Time Unable to Process Order: Double click on this, copy and paste the long guid into the search bar, click fix. This will tell you at which stage the script is at (returned, already released and ready to be dispensed, already handed out, successfully released etc…)TIP: Collect the long guid from the payload sent to you by Pilltime, often payloads will include multiple prescriptionids so ensure you have checked them all.  Shelf Clean Up: Double click on this and hit yes. This fix is used when sites have handed out packages still showing on their shelves after a self audit, this fix will run in bulk.  SMS Diagnostics:  Double click on this to open the SMS Analysis screen. Enter the patient name or NHS number in the search bar and click search. Select the patient you want from the list, then you will see the mobile number show in the box below. You can copy and paste this phone number to continue your analysis. TIP: 
All of the most recent text messages sent will show in the bottom box.

Use this helpfile to fully diagnose an SMS issue.
  Split Large Batch: Double click on this, enter the patients NHS number in the search bar at the top, hit search, select the prescriptions you would like to split into a new batch on the right hand side and then hit create split batch.  Titan Mobile User Cannot Login: Double click this. A message will pop up on your screen: 'Please view the Users list and check for users with the same username. Edit one to something different and this will fix this issue.' When you click 'ok', it will take you to the Users view to complete this.  Titan X Inbox: Double click on this, click yes, after this ask the site to restart Titan X and the stuck prescriptions should then begin to pass through.  App Removal Requests: Double click on uninstall marketplace app, this will open up the Apps tab, click on the app the site have requested to have removed, click remove app, click yes. This will then show in the marketplace sales channel and Raff will then add an emoji once salesforce has been done too.TIP: It is highly important to always have confirmation that the owner wants this app removed and that the ODS code has been confirmed. Also remember to check the slack channel too, to ensure salesforce has been done.  View Tracker/ Rx Card Stuck:This can be used for multiple issues/scenarios. Removing a Duplicate Card: Double click on view tracker/rx card stuck, enter the prescription barcode or the incoming ID (select the correct option) and then hit refresh. Symptoms of a duplicate card:
Same prescription barcode, same prescription date, same issue number.
The duplicate will always have an arrival time after the original.
 Example:
Original arrival time 12:02:34
Duplicate arrival time: 12:03:34
 Once the duplicate has been found, click on this and hit set selected to returned. TIP: If the prescription incoming ID is the same for both the original and the duplicate this will need to fixed by the developers as removing this via TC would also remove the original.  Removing a Returned Card: Enter the prescription barcode in the search bar (or incoming id) select prescription barcode, hit refresh, hit search tracker, if the script is successfully returned to the spine however still appearing within Titan, hit set selected to returned. Withdrawn Prescriptions: Sometimes sites will contact us to say they are having difficulty bringing a withdrawn prescription back onto the board. In this instance enter the prescription barcode in the search bar, hit refresh, select the withdrawn script and hit set selected to inbox.TIP: Do not use set selected to inbox for any eRDs or acutes that have any status other than withdrawn. It will put the script in the inbox but the site will get red toast and it will not work, only use for withdrawn. Tracker FAQs: When can I set a prescription to 'complete'? When the prescription is claimed on the spine by the site, but is still showing on the board. When can I set a prescription to 'returned'? When the prescription is 'to be dispensed' on the spine, but is still showing on the board. When can I set a prescription to inbox? When the prescription does not have a 'dispensed' or 'claimed' status on the spine, and is not showing on the board.  Footnote: 
The tracker will only affect scripts on the board and patient history.
Any changes made in tracker will not change the ERD flyout statuses.
If the prescription is in the inbox, you will not be able to see the prescription in this tracker.

articles.title: NHS Mail Logs
articles.content:
NHS Mail Logs Guide The NHS Mail Logs section in Titan Console allows you to view and search daily email logs sent from our mail server. This helps identify whether messages were successfully delivered or if errors occurred. How to Access NHS Mail Logs 
From the Titan Console main menu, double-click NHS Mail Logs.
In the Date field, select the day you want to review.
(Optional) Enter part of an email address to refine your search.
Click Search.
  Notes on Performance 
If you do not enter part of an email address, the system will load all records for the selected day. This may take a few seconds, as there are typically around 3,000 records daily.
If you select today’s date, the search will take longer (around 30 seconds) as the system retrieves data from the live service rather than the faster overnight log storage.
 Reviewing Results 
Once loaded, you’ll see all logs sent from our mail server for the selected day.
Results will display each site and the status of their messages (success/error).
Click on any column header to sort and filter results, making it easier to locate specific records.
If there was an error with an email, it will be clearly shown in the log.

articles.title: Device Replacement
articles.content:
Last reviewed 09/04/25
 
If a customer replaces their TITAN Mobile device, they are allowed to transfer the licence at no extra cost, as long as they:

Ideally still have the original licence
Have uninstalled TITAN Mobile from their old device

As we are unable to check if a licence has been used on another device like we do with TITAN (please do not tell customers this) it is important the the original license is used for the device as this will cause issues if the wrong license is used.
 
If the pharmacy have lost their original licence:
Old licences will either be saved in Clickup (Implementation team will be able to retrieve this for you) or we can block the original license and issue a new license, if they have access to the device they will need to provide the device ID from the Titan Mobile app. Once they have provided you with this you can block the license the same way you block a PC license from TC
If they no longer have access to the device, you can find out when the last time the device was used on TC by double clicking on a serial number and asking the site to confirm if the date/time is correct and proceed to block the license as normal
 
If they have lost their original VPN credentials:
You can request new VPN credentials/issue new ones from TC

articles.title: Install
articles.content:
Last reviewed: 22/05/25
Log in to the Play Store (you may need to make an account)
Search for TITAN Mobile and install it (do not open)
Back arrow
Choose from Native or FortiClient. FortiClient is normally the best option, but you can use Native if you are having issues with FortiClient. 
FortiClient VPN:Preparation:Ensure you have your TITAN Mobile username and password ready. If you don't have this information, contact the Support Desk for assistance.Make sure there are no other VPN clients installed on your device, such as FortiClient VPN or OpenVPN. Installation:Open the Play Store and log in or create an account if needed.Search for the "FortClient VPN" app and click "Install." Do not install the app just called "FortiClient".Once installed, open the app and confirm all security prompts. Configuration:You will be taken to a login page.1. Click New VPN.2. For the VPN Name, enter "TITAN."3. Choose "SSL VPN" and hit "Create."4. Click on "Servers" and enter the following URL: https://vpn2020-8e.titan-5a.net:443 and click "OK."5. Click on "Username" and enter your unique username that was emailed to you, then click "OK."Do not use a username already in use, as this will prevent the device from connecting at the same time as the other device using this account.6. Click "Back" and then "Connect."7. Enter your password and hit "Login."8. Confirm the security prompt.9. Once connected, click "Disconnect." 10. Re-enter the password, however this time, you will need to tick the "Save Password" checkbox that would have appeared.11. Click "Connect" again. Native:1. In Android, go to Settings> Connections>More connection settings> VPN > click "…" icon in the top right corner.Input the following details: Name:                              TITAN MobileType:                                IPSec Xauth PSKServer address:                vpn-ike.titan-5a.netIPsec identifier:                edoIPSec preshared key:      mknjbhvgr4e3w2q1Username:                         You will be emailed this. Case sensitivePassword:                          You will be emailed this. Case sensitive 2. Click save3. Click the VPN that you just set up4. Click Connect TITAN Mobile Setup1. Open the TITAN Mobile app ensuring that the VPN is connected2. Click 'Allow' to the prompts that appear on the screen2. Scan the license barcode from the email In order to use the TITAN Mobile app you must ensure your VPN is connected at all times.ConnectWiseAlthough this is not a requirement, we recommend installing the ConnectWise app. This will make it much quicker for out Help Desk to remote access your device should you need a hand with anything.1. Open the Play Store2. Download and Install ConnectWise Control app (Red and white icon)3. Type in URL titanpmr.screenconnect.com
