articles.title: Video
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):Using the Titan system, we've been able to ensure that the items that have been dispensed are exactly the items that are required. We've been able to ensure that the dispensing labels have definitely gone onto the right boxes and to ensure that the correct boxes are in this bag, and of course, that the correct bag label is now on the bag as well. So we now have a very, very, uh, secure packet. We know exactly what is inside here. The next place where a lot of issues can happen in a pharmacy, um, is when it comes to, uh, handout and to, and to shelving the bag ready for the patient to come in. We can have issues where, for example, a patient would come in, uh, they'd give their name over, you'd go to the shelf, you would grab their meds, but you'd forget the other package that's in the fridge or in the CD cabinet. The way that we can get around those issues, uh, with Titan is using what we call Edo. So this tablet here is now going to enable us to correctly and safely stow away this package ready for when the patient comes in. And when the patient comes in, it will enable us to quickly find it as well as dealing with some of the other important steps that have to happen for the pharmacy here. So once we've bagged this item, the next thing we need to do is to put it onto the shelf. And this is a very quick and easy process. So we take you and we click on the button down here that says Assign to Shelf. It's now gonna ask me to scan the item that I want to take on the shelf. So I'll take my package and I'll scan the bag label, scan the shelf label, and pop the item onto that shelf. We now know where this bag is— that's going to update Titan. So on the prescription board there, we can now see it's on shelf and I can also see here what shelf it's on. That's the package—now safely stowed away. Should I have had another package with the CD, I would put it into the CD cabinet or into the fridge. If I had multiple packets for the patient, I can put them on the shelf. Alternatively, if this shelf was full, I could put one on that shelf, one on another shelf. It doesn't matter because we can remember exactly where the items have been put. Now, once the last package has been put onto the shelf, at that point, we will then trigger an SMS message to go out to the patient telling them to come in and get their meds. Next thing that happens—the patient walks in and says, um, that they'd like to collect their medicines. So we grab a Edo device again and we can now ask the patient for their name or their date of birth and they can enter that into Edo. So if I just type in FEL for Felix, searching as I type, it's now found one patient. So I can click on that, and on this screen now I can firstly start by asking the normal data protection questions. So I can say, Mr. Leon Felix, I've got his date of birth and his full address. At that point, it's now going to tell me exactly what's going on for this patient. So I can see I've got one package on the shelf. I've also got another couple of items that are still on the system waiting to be dispensed. So I could ask the patient to sit down and wait for five minutes. Um, or alternatively, I could just do the handout right now. So now I just go to the shelf, grab my package and click Handout and scan the barcode. Okay. And I can now see that it's gone blue to say that I've scanned the right item. At that point, had I picked up a package for the wrong patient, it would be able to tell me, again, that I've picked up the wrong item, stopping me from giving the wrong bag to a patient. Okay. Um, also now that this has gone blue, we can see, that there's only one package. In this case, had there been more, they would be listed down here one at a time. And I wouldn't be able to proceed until I've accounted for every package. So the patient is now standing in front of me and he may ask me, for example, has this package got my codeine in, for example? So, uh, in a normal system, what you'd have to do at this point is rip open the bag, make a bit of a mess, have a look, and then after I've got the answer to the patient, I now have to go back into the dispensary, rebag the item, print another bag label. It's a lot of fuss—it's not necessary. So with this system, all we do is we can click on See Contents and I can see exactly what's inside the bag.At this point, the patient may say, well, the GP did say that they're going to prescribe me my codeine. Why haven't you got it? Uh, so now I can even click on view prescription and I can show an image of the prescription to the patient right there and then without having to refer back to my PC. Okay, so I'll go back, go back. Next thing I need to do is just click on the next button and now it's gonna start to ask me about my exemptions. So in this case, I can say, uh, yes, the patient is exempt. I'll then now need to just select one of the normal reasons as to why they might be exempt. It's gonna ask me if I've seen evidence, I can say yes or no. If I say yes, I can now enter the expiry date. If I wanted to click confirm, then I can now ask the patient to sign for the item. So if in a week's time the patient does come in and say, uh, did you give me my tramadol? And you say, yes, the patient says, no, you've got a bit of a problem. Now with Edo, all I need to do is get 'em to sign for this item. And then if there's a dispute a little bit later as to what I've given to the patient, I can actually say, yes, I did give you this item and here's your signature. Okay, so now all I need to do is click on the next button. Um, now next thing it's gonna do is show me some notes. So if there was a note from the GP on the second page of the prescription, it's gonna show on here. Um, if the pharmacist decided to put a note on during the, uh, clinical checks, uh, it will show on here so we can ensure there's a good communication between the GP, the pharmacist, any of the pharmacy staff, and the patient themselves. So I'll confirm that. And now all I need to do is click complete handout and that's it, that's now been handed out. It's done the dispense notification to the spine. It's sent the claim notification, and it's also done the FMD decommissioning. All I do now is hit close and that's the process complete.

articles.title: What Can I Do?
articles.content:
TITAN Mobile (formerly EDO) offers several features, including:

Assign to shelf: Scan your packages onto your shelf/fridge/CD cabinet, etc

Handout: See what shelf your patient's packages are on and scan them to ensure you have all of them for the right patient (more info).

Shelf Audit: Audit all shelves to ensure packages are all stored correctly and to enable bulk handout of discrepancies from TITAN

Quick Check: Users can quickly check picking labels and accept selected accuracy checks​.

Stock Ordering: Add to the order pad via scan or search. Remove from the pad, change the quantity, and submit the order.

Barcode Registration: Allows users to scan and register new product barcodes with photos​.

NMS: Prompt for NMS and handout (and fill out engagement for TITANVERSE customers)

SMS: Send patients SMS/emails when assigning package to shelf.

Collection Barcode Scanning: Allows patients to scan a barcode from their phone for collection​.

Batch Flow Integration: Supports batch picking list printing and integration with TITAN Mobile​.

articles.title: What is the "Waiting Shelf"?
articles.content:
The Waiting Shelf is a 'system' shelf that's used in conjunction with TITAN Mobile.
Packages are automatically assigned to it when a user begins a handout transaction on TITAN Mobile for a package that is NOT on a shelf.
 
If you see a package on the Waiting Shelf, this is because a handout for a package not on the shelf was started but not completed.

articles.title: Video
articles.content:
Can't access the video?Launch the Help Centre via the  button or Click here instead

Transcript (AI Generated):
Titan notes are a great way of transcribing key bits of information throughout the prescription journey. Titan offers many ways of grading the story notes, and I'm going to show you how. You'll notice this icon throughout the app. This indicates that you can add a note to this section. All note sections have a box at the bottom where you can simply type in your note and press enter. Hitting the bubble will expand or collapse the notes. Once you've added your note, you'll see three dots. Press this for more options. These options will change depending on the type of note and the screen that you're entering the note. If you want to edit the note again, hit the three dots, click on edit, and change the note accordingly, and then press the tick. You can add a note to the patient by simply going into the patient detail screen, clicking onto the notes, and simply adding your note in the box below. Now, when the note is being added, you can click on the three dots to present a few options here on how this note could be presented later on down the line. For instance, this note may be critical enough that you would like to inform the pharmacist the next time a prescription arrives. In this case, you can just hit "Show on Prescription and RX Checks," and the note will now appear next time a prescription arrives for this patient. For patients that are on repeat medications, you may want to ensure the note is always displayed when this particular drug is dispensed. An example is with particular flavors or brands for a particular drug. Go to the patient therapy tab, find the drug in question, click on the bubble, and enter your note. This note will now appear every time this patient has a prescription for this item. There are drugs that you may wish to convey a message for whenever a prescription arrives. Search for the drug in the global search. Click on the comments, enter your note. This note will now appear the next time this item is prescribed. Now, when you receive a digital prescription or enter a manual prescription, you'll see these bubbles appear in all of the sections. These bubbles indicate that you can add a note to this particular section. Now, notice that some of these bubbles already have a number in them and are also in blue. This indicates that this particular patient has a note that was marked as "Show on the Prescription Entry." So if we go ahead and click the bubble, you can now see the note that was put into the patient's profile a little bit earlier on. Now, similar to the patient-level note, you'll also notice there is a number inside of the item level. I'll go ahead and click it. These two notes indicate notes that have come from the drug level—where a note was added to the drug—but also where this particular note was added to the patient's repeat medication. Now we can go ahead and add a new note by typing the note down here in the select text box. However, if we click the three dots again, we get a whole load of new options for this particular note. For instance, the "Show on Handout" option will show this note on EDO when you hand out the medication. "Show on Labeling and Packaging" will push this note to the labeling screen and the packaging screen. "Show on Picking" will print this particular note on the picking report. If you have chosen the "Show on Picking" option, this note will appear on the picking label. This is a great way to ensure the right medications are picked—for instance, a specific flavor for that patient. If you have chosen the "Show on Labeling and Packaging" option, this note will appear in both the labeling and the packaging screens. You'll see the bubble on the left panels in the labeling and packaging screen. You can also add new notes from here as well. This is a really good way to ensure the pharmacist is able to convey important information to the dispensing team. If you have chosen the "Show on Handout" option, the note will appear when you hit the handout button. Now, one of the most powerful features is the ability to mark a note as a query. For instance, there may be times where you need to call the GP to clarify something on the prescription. You could do this really easily by marking the notes as a "Waiting Query." Now, in some instances, you may not want to progress the prescription to picking and labeling as you are waiting on the GP to get back to you. In this case, you'll notice a new message when you go to complete the prescription, asking if you wish to keep the prescription at the current stage. These queried prescriptions are presented slightly differently on the prescription board, making it really easy to understand which prescriptions are being held up because of a query. You can also add prescription notes directly from the board and also mark them with a query.

articles.title: Role Permissions
articles.content:
Please see the below table for a short description of what each role permission does in TITAN.
 

Permission
What it does

Edit branch details
Controls whether or not the Branch Details tab in settings is editable.

View system audits
Not Used

Clinically check
Controls whether or not individual clinical checks can be actioned (accept, do not dispense, ignore etc). Also disables/enables the save button on the clinical check screen.

Package
Controls access to the Packaging screen and access to the Quick Package button on labelling.

Package controlled drugs
Controls whether or not a user can package/quick package controlled drugs.

Manage users
Disables/enables the People and Roles tabs in Profile. Also, it controls if a user can change their own role or link/unlink their own Smart Card.

Process prescriptions
Not Used

Can use TITAN Mobile
Controls whether or not a user shows on the TITAN Mobile login screen.

Can claim and endorse
Controls whether or not a user can access the Claims screen (users can still submit a claim from Power Search)

Can label
Disables/enables access to the labelling screen (users may still relabel by clicking "Change label" from the package screen)

Can view patients
Not Used

Can edit patients
Controls access to the patient's Complete View and PDS Sync.

Can package 'Needs Check' items
Controls if a user can add items to a Package that requires a check. Includes Quick Check.

Can change dispensing and clinical settings
Changes whether or not the Dispensing Settings and Clinical Settings tabs are displayed in Settings.

Can place orders on order pad
Controls whether or not the Place Order button can be clicked in the Order Pad

Can export views to CSV
Disables/enables the Export button on all Views/Managed Patients tabs

View SCR 1-Click audit
Changes whether or not the SCR 1-Click and NCRS audits show in Settings>Audits

Can check in as responsible pharmacist
Disables/enables the TITAN X "Play" button, as used to start a new Burst

Include AI learning
Not used

Can manage Marketplace apps
Controls whether or not a user may install apps or configure settings in the MarketPlace>Installed Apps list.

Can use robot storage
Not used

Can manually reconcile items
Controls if the "Mark as manually reconciled" button may be used in Views>Private Prescriptions to mark an outstanding emergency New Supply as reconciled.

Can use SSP
Prevents users clicking the SSP button when doing a Clinical Check to create an SSP alternative supply.

Can view pharmacist performance
Controls access to the Active Pharmacists panel on the Clinical Dashboard

Can approve prepacks
Determines whether or not new pre-packs can be approved for robot users.

Can clear/unclear claim records
Controls whether or not users can use the Clear button on the Claims screen, as well as the Unclear button on the Claimed tab.

Can perform quick package batch flow
Disables/enables the Quick Packaging button for Batch Flow batches.

Can package 'Needs Check' items labelled by same user
Controls whether or not a user can do Final Checks for items that they themselves have labelled.

Require barcode validation on packaging
If on, TITAN will display a popup when scanning a dispensing label into a package allowing you to do a secondary check by scanning the manufacturer's barcode to confirm that the label was put on the correct product.

View NCRS audit
Not used.

Can use 'package all' function
Controls whether or not the Package All button shows at packaging to allow users to add all of a given drink or dressing to a package with one click.

Can perform NMS consultation
Affects whether or not TITAN displays the consultation fields when handing out for TITANVERSE users. Fields include Drug Name, Dose, Decline Item, Contact Number, Ethnicity, Healthy Living Advice, Intervention Type and Intervention Date. Also controls the same thing on TITAN Mobile.

articles.title: Troubleshooting Guide
articles.content:
What to check in Windows 
Go to search and type in 'Printers'

Go to Printers and Scanners
Ensure the printer is added on the list and is not in an 'Error State'

If the printer does not show, ask the user to unplug the USB cable and plug it back in
If the printer still does not show, ensure the Printer is properly connected and click the 'Add Printer' button and follow the onscreen prompts. Most USB printers are plug and play so treat this like a normal install wizard and follow the on screen prompts to install the printer.
 If printer shows in an error state, check the following: 
Select the printer and select 'Open Print Queue'

Check if there are any jobs in the print queue 
Clear any 'stuck' jobs by right clicking and selecting 'Clear/Delete' and select 'Yes' on the dialogue box 
Then login to Titan and run the 'Reinstall Desktop Services' fix detailed later in the article under 'What to check in Titan'

 If this does not resolve, the printer spooler may be causing the issue: 
Go back to the Printers and Scanners list
Scroll down and make sure 'Let Windows manage my default printer' is ticked
If it isn't, it is possible the Zebra printer has been made the default printer, ticking this box will ensure that the incorrect printer is no longer default and the printer should no longer appear in an error state
  Checking Ports and Drivers 
From the Printer list in 'Printers and Scanners'

Click on the Zebra printer and select 'Manage'

Next select 'Printer Properties'

You should see the pictured window popup
Next select the 'Advanced' tab and ensure the correct driver is installed:
  You can ask Windows to scan for new/up to date drivers by clicking 'New Driver' button (The correct driver should already be installed after the printer is setup during implementation so it is unlikely you will need to do this) Next we need to check if the printer is assigned to the correct Port: 
Click the 'Ports' tab and you should see the image below
Make sure the port assigned to the printer is set to 'USB001 or 002'

If it is set to 'LPT1' - this is an older 'serial' type connection and should not be in use as Zebra are USB printers
Once the port is selected, click 'Apply' and then 'OK'
  
Finally, you want to ensure that print jobs are now being sent to the printer
Open the print queue window and make it sure it does not overlap with the Printer settings window:
  Then from the print management screen select 'Print test page' - a print job should appear briefly then disappear and a label will print. This will confirm that the print job was sent successfully. What to check in Titan 
Log into Titan and click the Powersearch bar or press F9
Check to make sure the 'System Status' lights are all Green:
  
If the Printer light is Red, then the print issue is being caused by Titan not communicating with Windows (If the test label print from earlier was successful)
To fix this go to 'Settings'

Select 'System Info'

Click on the blue button that says 'Reinstall desktop services'

You will see a number of CMD/DOS windows open running script
Do nothing until you are left with 2 windows that both have 'Close console to exit' as the final line command
Close both windows, logout of Titan, CLOSE Titan completely, then load Titan again and sign in
At this point all the services lights should be Green and you should be able to print.
 Other things to check: Ensure that all the print profiles have the correct printer assigned to them, make sure no A4 profile has the label printer assigned to it and vice versa.Ensure that the physical printer is aligned. There are small arms on the front of the printer. Ensure these are centred and aligned.  Crystal Reports Dependency:
If the labeller still does not talk to Titan or you get a red toast saying 'failed to print', check whether Crystal Reports is installed.
Disable Smart App Control (Win > search Smart App Control > select Off > agree to all prompts).
Install Crystal Reports by running CRRuntime_32bit_13_0_21.msi from: C:\Program Files (x86)\TITAN PMR.
Restart the PC.
Re-test the labeller connection. 
Useful Resources: https://titanhelp.zendesk.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360018197320-Label-printer-settings-and-marginshttps://titanhelp.zendesk.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360010666599-How-To-Setup-one-printer-for-2-programs-that-have-different-settings- https://titanhelp.zendesk.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4403680605458-Delete-Titan-Peripheral-Service-Fix

articles.title: Flashing Lights Issue
articles.content:
What is the issue?Zebra experienced a manufacturing issue between 4th March and 28th July 2024 affecting the primary sensor in the Printed Circuit Board (PCB).This issue has impacted approximately 5% of printers produced during this period.The problem typically presents as all or most of the lights on the display flashing, and the printer will be unable to print.Although temporary fixes like a factory reset may sometimes appear to work, the Zebra Help Desk states that the issue will "definitely return within a few weeks".The only resolution is to replace the PCB or the sensor. This must be carried out by Zebra.Please review this Official Statement from Zebra Engineering confirming this. Is my printer affected?Your printer is affected if the lights are flashing as shown in the GIFs below and if the week of manufacture, as indicated in the serial number, is between weeks 10 and 30 (inclusive). Light patterns:                     The lights are not always synchronous, as they flash independently.What is crucial is that:
The Status light flashes red,
The Pause light flashes red, orange, or green, and
The Data light flashes green.
 Serial Location (sticker on the bottom): How to decipher the serial number:Characters 4 and 5 indicate the year of manufacture.Characters 6 and 7 indicate the week of manufacture. What to do:If your printer's lights are flashing as shown above, and if it was manufactured between weeks 10 and 30 (inclusive), you will need to return the printer to Zebra.This is a free-of-charge service while under warranty (warranty is normally two years, so all affected printers will be covered until at least 4th March 2026.It is also worth noting that newly purchased printers are unlikely to be affected, as the manufacturing issue was resolved in early August 2024. How to contact ZebraPhone number: 0800 328 24 24Before you call: Have the printer’s serial number ready.Explain that you are unable to print anything, even a test page.Mention that:
The Status light is flashing red
The Pause light is flashing red/orange/green
The Data light is flashing green
Ask to return the printer under warranty.The Zebra agent should then arrange for the printer to be collected, repaired, and returned to you under warranty, or they may ask you to log into their website to book the repair.Example call script"Hi, I'm calling about a printer issue. I have the serial number ready—would you like that first?(Provide the serial number.)I'm unable to print anything—not even a test page. I've tried troubleshooting, including updating the drivers and resetting the printer, but it's still unresponsive.The printer’s status light is flashing red, the pause light is flashing red/orange/green, and the data light is flashing green.The device is still under warranty, and as it’s not functioning, I’d like to return it for a warranty repair or replacement. Could you assist me with this process?"

articles.title: Troubleshooting
articles.content:
Follow this diagnostic guide when troubleshooting scanners
 
This article is specific to the Zebra hand held scanner which is the most commonly used scanner for TITAN customers.
 
Basic Diagnostics:

Unplug the scanner and try a different USB port
Open Task Manager and select 'Services' - Check if Titan peripheral service (TPS) is running
Login to TITAN and press F9 and check the status lights - ensure the 'Printing' one is Green

 

 

If it is Red, please follow: https://titanhelp.zendesk.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4405981570706-Reinstall-Desktop-Services
Open up a notepad and scan a label/token - no characters should appear in the notepad

 
If the above does not resolve the issue, please do the following:

Type services in Windows search bar or Click the start button in the bottom left corner and then open up the “Control Panel”
From the Control Panel click on “Administrative Tools”, and then double click on “Services”

NOTE: You can just search for 'Administrative Tools' select it and then double click on 'Services' 
Find the “Human Interface Device Access” service and then restart it, if the service is not running, start the service. Close the services window.

 
Following the above steps will resolve most if not all scanner issues. If the above is unsuccessful, you can do further diagnostics listed below.
 
Further Diagnostics:
ID Automation and Zebra SDK Installation:

Go the the C directory on the PC
You will see a folder named TITAN
Open this folder and double click on the Zebra SDK file
It will ask if you want to Repair, Modify or Uninstall
Select uninstall and uninstall the SDK completely
Restart the PC
Go back to the same folder and now install the SDK 
Ensure you are selecting OPOS only when installing
When the install has finished - restart the PC again
Ensure you scan the config barcodes after reinstalling the SDK - these are also in the TITAN folder
Follow the same process for the ID Automation file

If none of the above has resolved the issue, raise in support_internal or titan_support_desk in Slack and we will look into this further.
